title: Design & Implementation of Smart Traffic Light Controller
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Computing and Intelligent Technologies (ICoECIT)
abstract: Overcrowding of urban sites visitors is an increasing menace in contemporary towns that follow through with increased delays, consumption of fuel and environmental pollution. The traditional visitors signaling structures operate on a fixed time scale, which is currently failing to adjust to actual-time site visitor variations, leading to an inefficient management of site visitors. This project is about the design and development of a Smart Traffic Light Controller the application of car density analysis within a python-based SUMO simulator environment. Each direction is initially given a predetermined inexperienced period of 10 seconds at an intersection. The generation always monitors vehicle queues, and when the lane is facing a high traffic, the inexperienced signal period is mechanically extended to 15 seconds. On the other hand, the period changes to the default setting when the visitors are reduced. The simulation shows real-time version, which improves the allocation of signals and reduces unnecessary delays on unused lanes. Compared to hardware or IoT-based solutions, this software program-based solution provides a framework that is available and scalable to educational and research programs. Findings indicate that there has been a large enhancement in visitors wafts to sites, reduction in mean waits, and better intersection throughput in comparison with conventional constant-time law. Such an overview highlights the potential of intelligent, information-based traffic management systems to enhance urban mobility and provides a basis on the future intelligent transportation solutions.

title: Design & implementation of stock-aware shelves using pervasive computing
venue: 2017 International Conference on Energy, Communication, Data Analytics and Soft Computing (ICECDS)
abstract: Pervasive computing also called ubiquitous computing is nothing but embedding microprocessors in everyday objects so they can communicate information. With the advancements in Internet technologies, a new trend in the era of ubiquity is being realized. Today, whenever we go out to buy grocery we may forget to buy any particular, which may cause inconvenience. This problem can be solved by using Pervasive Computing principles. Smart phones and wearable devices are being used to make the world around us reachable, inter-actable and to keep us updated. Utilizing sensor and smartphone technology we target to embed a mind in kitchen which interacts with user and automatically generates To-buy list and alerts depending upon the need of a particular item. Towards such a perspective, there is the need to continuously collect, elaborate, and present data, possibly deriving from smart objects. This can be achieved by the use of Sensor Networks, consisting of raspberry pi 3 development board along with HX711 load sensor interface to sense the weight of particular quantity and send it witlessly over the network. This raspberry pi 3 can be programmed in Python to serve our purpose

title: Design a Landmark Facial-Based Drowsiness Detection Using Dlib And Opencv For Four-Wheeled Vehicle Drivers
venue: 2021 15th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Drowsiness harms motorists because it can cause microsleep. A landmark facial-based drowsiness detection application is required for monitoring motorists while driving. Drowsiness detection applications are designed based on face recognition methods that have an advantage in face detection. Several facial detection methods such as computer vision, dlib face detector, dlib facial landmark, and eye aspect ratio (EAR) are combined to design drowsiness detection applications. Application Design uses python 3.6.8, which has a supporting library in designing applications. The library used in designing the drowsiness detection application is openCV to process images and videos in real-time, Dlib for face detectors, Tkinter to build GUI applications. Input drowsiness detection application in the form of real-time video taken through a webcam. The app will activate alarm sounds and warning posts when a person is detected as drowsiness. Drowsy detection application testing is done using machine learning, confusion matrix, real-time testing, and evaluation of consumption of resources such as power, memory, and CPU. The accuracy value of testing using machine learning and confusion matrix is 97%, and Real-time testing accuracy is 96%. When used, the CPU usage percentage of drowsiness detection applications is 30.8%, memory usage is about 130.4 MB, and power consumption measured using Open Hardware Monitor is 5.09 W when the application is working.

title: Design an RF Up-Down Convertor Using Software Defined Radio and GNU Radio
venue: Journal of Mobile Multimedia
abstract: There is a need to design of RF Up/Down- converter for (from C/Ku to/from L band) signals required for several applications. The proposed work presents a design of an RF Up/Down Converter that makes use of GNU Radio and Software-Defined Radios (SDRs). The converter helps in frequency translation between the C/Ku and L bands, leading to a cost-effective and versatile solution for RF signal processing. By using open-source GNU Radio software, the proposed system enhances accessibility, enabling its deployment in diverse applications, from satellite communication to radar systems. The converter's unique features include real-time processing capabilities, customization through an intuitive graphical interface, and Python scripting. This idea presents the design considerations, signal processing techniques, and performance evaluation of the RF Up/Down Converter. The advantages of an open-source solution over other available alternatives are in terms of cost, flexibility, and rapid prototyping. Simulation and hardware results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed work.

title: Design and Analysis of Heart Attack Prediction System Using ML
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Communication Systems (ICICACS)
abstract: Any diseases that is kept untreated for a long period of time directly impacts the human health and effect all the major organs of the body. Treating the chronic diseases in timely basis is highly recommended to avoid major medical problems coming over the way. On implementing Chronic Heart Attack prediction system using Hybrid SMLT (Split Multi Link trunking) technique is presented here. The proposed system considers machine learning algorithm in which Logistic regression (LR), multi-level perceptron (MLP) based on neural network, CatBoost regression (CB) algorithm and Random Forest regression algorithm (RF) is comparatively tested. Considering the data set provided, the presented approach is implemented using Python IDE and simulated in IoT (Internet of things) screen of Google Collab. A comparative analysis of various Machine learning algorithm is helpful to make the accurate processing with the help of robust method in short span of time. Further different machine learning techniques, with multiple features are considered as scope of implementation. The proposed approach is creating a machine learning model that can predict whether or not a person will experience a heart attack. The best model is used to forecast the result after many techniques have been compared.

title: Design and Application of Interactive Video Programming Educational Games for Cultivating Computational Thinking
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Computer Science and Technologies in Education (CSTE)
abstract: This study addresses the issues of low student interest and participation in junior high school Python programming instruction. By combining the concept of gamified learning with interactive video technology, we designed and developed a Python programming educational game for junior high school students titled “The Programming Challenge for Supermarket Staff.” The game uses a supermarket career experience as the narrative background and integrates Python programming knowledge into job scenarios through interactive mechanisms such as role-playing, branching plots, and instant feedback. Based on the interactive video technology of the Bilibili platform, it supports learners in autonomously choosing learning paths and receiving real-time feedback. Practical applications indicate that this game can effectively enhance students' learning motivation, engagement, and computational thinking skills. This study provides a feasible path for the design and development of programming educational games and offers practical references for the application of interactive video in educational games.

title: Design and application of parallel intelligent control system for denitration system in coal-fired power plant
venue: 2022 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Digital Twins and Parallel Intelligence (DTPI)
abstract: Based on the parallel control theory, a denitration parallel intelligent automation system is designed in this paper. It is composed of hardware system and software system. The hardware system has modules such as power supply, industrial controller and host, and real-time communication is realized between the control modules. The software system is based on the parallel control theory. Firstly, the pseudo-random sequence module, period data acquisition module, identification module, predictive control module and other modules are realized, and the specific basic functions are given;Secondly, the relevant modules and logic systems corresponding to manual system, calculation experiment and parallel execution are designed, the specific structure of denitration parallel control system is given, and the structure of parallel process controller is analyzed in detail;In this paper, it is proposed that the program-controlled signal flow is the key to realize the intelligent operation of parallel control, and the specific design method is given. At the same time, the virtual machine simulation operation in the hardware system is also an important part of parallel intelligent control, and the specific signal communication mode is given. Finally, an engineering application example of denitration parallel intelligent automation system is given, and the effectiveness of the system is verified by experiments, The design method proposed in this paper has strong practical significance for the application of parallel intelligent automation system.

title: Design and Construction of a UAV VTOL in Ducted-Fan and Tilt-Rotor Configuration
venue: 2019 16th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an hybrid Unmanned Aerial Vehicle that combines the capabilities of Vertical Takeoff and Landing (VTOL) as well as the hover flight of an helicopter, with the autonomy, load capacity and speed offered by an airplane. We start from an aircraft concept that uses the Tilt-Rotor configuration to perform the transition phase from one flight mode to another and simultaneously we used Ducted-Fans for increasing the flight performance during the vertical flight phase. The aerodynamic design is developed using computational tools, such as XFLR5 for preliminary design and ANSYS FLuent® for the verification of the preliminary fixed wing design. While for the vertical flight, experimental tests were conducted in order to determine the lift system requirements by using Ducted-Fans. Afterwards, the manufacturing process derived from the aerodynamic design is presented. The avionics developed is described for handling the control surfaces during the airplane mode and the main lift system during the vertical flight as well as the integration of mechanism and sensors used. Finally, the obtained results from the conducted vertical flight tests at outdoors environments are presented in order to show the effectiveness of the aircraft concept.

title: Design and Construction of Low Cost High-Performance Transducer Signal Processing and Data Acquisition System
venue: 2020 4th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)(48184)
abstract: In this paper, high performance transducer signal processing and 8 single ended channel Data Acquisition System (DAS) is proposed. Goal of designing system is to provide low cost, light weight, compact, high resolution and low noise interference data acquisition system (DAS). This system is designed using Open-source micro-controller ARM Cortex-M4 series processor TEENSY 3.6 board. Designed system acquires data more accurately with the resolution of 16-bits, real time data acquisition rate up-to 20KHz with user friendly Graphical User Interface (GUI). DAS has capacity of up-to 8 single ended channel input with user selectable channel sequence function.

title: Design and Development of a Portable Electrical Impedance Tomography System with Wideband Excitation
venue: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Multi-Conference on Systems, Signals & Devices (SSD)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an embedded electrical impedance tomography (EIT) system that performs wideband excitation and real-time imaging using a compact platform. The system integrates a Raspberry Pi 4 controller with a Digilent Analog Discovery 2 (AD2) module and an 8-electrode interface driven by analog multiplexers. A multisine voltage excitation covering $1 \text{Hz}-1 \text{kHz}$ is generated by the AD2 and applied directly to the electrodes, while response voltages are synchronously acquired for impedance estimation. The entire measurement, spectral analysis, and tomographic reconstruction are implemented in Python on the embedded Raspberry Pi 4 controller.

title: Design and Development of Capacitive Type Quasi-digital Sensor and Instrument to In-situ monitoring of the viscosity of Lubricant Oil
venue: 2022 2nd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Lubricant oil is used as protective layer between the metallic surfaces of gears and bearing of large rotating machinery for smooth operation of power plants and other heavy industries. Viscosity of lube oil plays an important role in reducing friction between rotating parts. Over the period of time, due to oil aging, its viscosity decreases along with deterioration in its various physical and chemical properties. Timely replacing of lube oil at critical viscosity level set by industry standards with fresh one can avoid the potential damage to the rotating machinery and unplanned shutdowns. This article presents development of a capacitive type quasi-digital sensor for real time measurement of lubricant oil viscosity. In addition to sensor an instrument is also developed to read the output from the sensors, to communicate the data to computer, and display on LCD. An experiment is conducted to check the capability of the sensor and instrument for measurement of lubricant oil viscosity. The sensitivity of the sensor is 232Hz/m. Pa.s, and the accuracy is ±10 m.Pa.s. A python based Graphical User Interface (GUI) is also developed to plot real time viscosity and temperature graphs by collecting the sensor data from COM port of the PC.

title: Design and Development of Digital Stethoscope
venue: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research explores the fusion of cardiac auscultation and phonocardiography (PCG) to enhance cardiac acoustic analysis. Traditional stethoscopes face limitations, including the need for expertise to discern abnormalities based solely on auditory information and the challenge of isolating heart sounds from background noise. We introduce a robust hardware and software framework for signal acquisition and processing, effectively reducing noise and enabling signal playback. The hardware incorporates an omnidirectional Electret Condenser Microphone, signal conditioning with AD620 and IC741, and a second-order bandpass filter for noise reduction. The Python-based software enables real-time signal recording, playback, and parameter computation. The heart sounds were acquired for 10 subjects using the fabricated chest piece. The recordings spanned a duration of one minute, and subsequently, sounds were played back, displaying both the waveform and the heart rate of the measured signal on the application screen, allowing for visual analysis. The heart rate obtained from our measurements was validated by cross-referencing it with the heart rate data derived from a patient monitoring system. Validation demonstrates accuracy comparable to clinical monitoring systems with a minimal acceptable variation. This standalone device holds great potential for healthcare, improving cardiac diagnostics' precision. Future work aims to integrate wireless capabilities, ensuring data security and ethical compliance.

title: Design and Development of Graphical User Interfaces for Detection of Forest Fires at early stages using Open-Source Technologies
venue: 2021 6th International Conference on Signal Processing, Computing and Control (ISPCC)
abstract: In this paper, a Graphical User Interface (GUI) is designed and developed using Python programming language for detection of forest fires at early stages, which is efficient, cost-effective, flexible, secure and uses open-source technologies. The user-friendly Graphical User Interface is interfaced directly with the computer port to fetch the data with the help of Python modules, performs an analysis on the data and predict whether there is a situation of fire or not and displays the status on the Graphical User Interface. Data is also stored in an Excel file for further analysis. The possibility to detect forest fire situation at its early stages makes this GUI a valuable software in environmental disasters and research applications. Numerical results along with future work have been discussed in this paper.

title: Design and Development of Low-Complex Methodology for sEMG-Based Hand Activity Identification and Actuation of Soft Robots for Rehabilitating and Amputated Patients
venue: 2024 31st IEEE International Conference on Electronics, Circuits and Systems (ICECS)
abstract: Advancements in automated rehabilitation and pow-ered prosthetics necessitate a holistic approach involving wearable sensor-driven activity identification followed by generation of appropriate control signals to drive user-specific assistive tools. Here, we demonstrate an end-to-end system facilitating low-complex energy-efficient surfaceElectroMyography (sEMG)-driven human hand activity classification using simple and accurate k-means clustering and subsequent control of in-house fabricated soft robotic actuator for rehabilitative and prosthetic assistance. A Delsys Trigno EMG device was used to capture EMG data from the left flexor carpi radialis muscle of 20 healthy individuals corresponding to seven different hand activities. Thereafter, a COordinate Rotation DIgital Computer (CORDIC) based k-means algorithm was implemented to classify the hand activities after the execution of CORDIC-based Ensemble Em-pirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and Fast Independent Component Analysis (FICA) on the acquired data, followed by, necessary segmentation and feature extraction. Simultaneously, a lightweight pneumatically actuated soft finger system fabricated out of silicone was developed with the aim of emulating the classified hand activities. The novelty of this soft actuator lies in its strategic design that enables large bending, even at pressure as low as 160 kPa yet restricts the movement in one plane with almost no bulging added with improved force exertion during contact. Accurate control signals representing each of the classified activities were realized on a Raspberry Pi 4 board with python environment. For a thorough analysis, the classification accuracy linked with the proposed algorithm was evaluated for different feature sets and an accuracy as high as 96% was obtained. Thus, an end-to-end system was established for real-time control of the soft actuator with a latency of 3 seconds, making it suitable for rehabilitation and prosthetic control applications where

title: Design and Development of Machine Vision-Driven Robotics System for Safe and Efficient Inner Pipe Inspection.
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Applications (MPSec ICETA)
abstract: This study focuses on developing an inspection robot, integrated with machine vision technology to identify and detect abnormalities on the inner surface of industrial pipelines. This robot can overcome the limitations faced by traditional methods. This robot is powered by Direct current motors on each wheel. To equip the robot with image capturing and object detection capabilities, it was integrated with a machine learning model trained in a Tensor-Flow environment using Python programming. Traditional methods required human presence on site with the implementation of this technology, humans can remotely control the robots functioning via a Bluetooth module and the captured data is displayed on a real-time data monitoring system. With capabilities such as autonomous navigation and advanced image processing techniques, this research aims to develop a robot to enhance safety, efficiency, reduced labor cost, and accessibility of pipe inspection robots for industrial applications. A prototype was developed to demonstrate the stated benefits and tests were performed in a practical environment to ensure robustness and reliability of the system for numerous industrial environments.

title: Design and Development of Temperature Controlled Intelligent Portable Reefer Container for Delivery Optimisation in Logistics and Supply Chain Management
venue: 2022 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
abstract: The statistics reflect the fact that a considerable quantity of perishable goods is wasted due to poorly designed supply chain management systems. This throws up the challenge in improvising or innovating a novel modus operandi in every stage of supply chain management. This article discusses a novel way of providing micro-management of goods by designing an intelligent temperature-controlled portable reefer container which can be transported effortlessly. The reefer container consists of a Peltier plate arrangement integrated with an automatic temperature control system (ATC) used to regulate the temperature precisely inside the container. The Global Positioning System (GPS) fitted on the container delivers precise location coordinates to the stakeholders in real-time. The multipurpose reefer container holds the feature of a seamless remote temperature setpoint change based on the type of perishable items loaded into the container. The supply chain management manager can remotely adjust the settings using Over The Air updates (OTA). The reefer container is equipped with an access control system to offer accurate delivery of products to the customer with the help of a quick response system with a credible user interface.

title: Design and Flight Test Validation of a UAS Lateral-directional Model Predictive Controller
venue: 2021 International Conference on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (ICUAS)
abstract: Recent advances in computer technologies have increased the processing power on-board unmanned aerial aircraft. Computationally potent avionic systems have provided new opportunities to implement more adaptive and capable flight controllers. Model predictive control is emerging as a method for controlling unmanned aircraft, satisfying state and control constraints, and improving aircraft performance in the presence of external disturbances and nonlinear and unsteady aerodynamics. Although model predictive controllers provide many advantages over classical or modern control methods (such as PID or LQR), their practical applications have been limited to high-level path plannings, guidance logic, and control of slow robots with less complex dynamics. This work presents the development of an inner-loop model predictive control flight controller and successful validation and verification of its performance in actual flight tests. The work also investigates the impact of number of horizon points on the performance of the model predictive controller in the presence of wind and other external disturbances.

title: Design and Implementation of a 256-Point FFT Hardware for Power Spectral Density Computation in EEG-Based Mental Stress Recognition
venue: 2026 National Conference on Communications (NCC)
abstract: This paper presents a high-throughput, low-latency 256-point Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) architecture employing two radix-16 butterfly ($\text{BS}_{16}$) units with a conflict-free dataflow structure and an integrated multiplierless power-accumulation (pAD) module for area-efficient power spectral density (PSD) computation. The design is synthesized using Synopsys Design Compiler in UMC 40-nm CMOS technology, achieving an area of $0.429 \text{mm}^{2}$ for the standalone FFT and $0.477 \text{mm}^{2}$ when combined with the pAD unit. The architecture delivers a latency of 62 clock cycles and a throughput of $3.2 \text{GS} / \mathrm{s}$, with a measured power consumption of 30.96 mW. The proposed design provides accurate PSD estimation, further validated through downstream electroencephalography (EEG) based, machine-learning-driven mental stress recognition. The 256-point FFT block achieves a mean Peak Signal-to-Noise-Ratio (PSNR) of 47.42 dB and a mean correlation coefficient of 0.998, while the hardwaresynthesized PSD achieves a mean Spectral Distortion Measure (SDM) of $56.98 \text{dB}^{2}$ and Spectral SNR (SSNR) of 48.72 dB. Subsequently, several discriminative features are extracted from the estimated PSD and are used to train benchmark machine learning classifiers implemented in Python. Among them, XGBoost attains the best overall performance with an accuracy of 89.01%, alongside strong precision $(88.21 \%)$, recall $(88.76 \%)$, and F1 Score $(88.48 \%)$, confirming its suitability for portable, real-time EEG-based stress recognition applications.

title: Design and Implementation of a Diagnostic Framework for Battery Monitoring in Electric Two-Wheelers
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents a Diagnostic and Fault management Unified Diagnostic Services (ASDFM-UDS) based Adaptive Severity-driven Diagnostic and Fault management model of battery monitoring in an electric two-wheeler via virtual ECU. The implementation of standard UDS services to enable diagnostic communication is like an OBD scanner. A battery receives an about 32-based ECU, which measures important battery parameters, such as voltage, current, temperature, SoC, SoH, and SoD, and wirelessly transmits this data to a PC-based diagnostic terminal. It has a Python interface that can be used to visually display the system in real time, show fault severity, and record data offline, with local status feedback via an onboard I 2 C LCD. ASDFM-UDS logic is a layer of supervisory firmware which is adaptively controlled to handle diagnostic sessions, assigns priority to faults based on severity and gives early warnings of critical conditions. The experimental findings demonstrate quality of diagnostic clarity and data traceability even in the case of following UDS communication standards.

title: Design and Implementation of a Dual Antenna Switching System Based on Signal Quality Estimation Using Software Defined Radio
venue: 2026 International Conference on Next Generation Electronics (NELEX)
abstract: Wireless communication systems operating in practical environments are highly susceptible to multipath fading, shadowing, and noise, resulting in significant fluctuations in received signal quality and reduced link reliability. Spatial diversity techniques are commonly employed to mitigate these effects. However, conventional combining methods such as maximal ratio combining require multiple RF chains and increased signal processing complexity. This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-complexity dual antenna selection diversity system using a software-defined radio (SDR) platform. A $2 \times 1$ receive diversity configuration is realized using two spatially separated antennas connected to a dual-channel SDR receiver. Independent baseband processing chains are implemented in GNU Radio, where the Root Mean Square (RMS) value of each received branch is computed in real time as a practical signal quality metric. A custom Python-based selection block dynamically compares the two branches and switches to the antenna with higher received signal strength. Experimental evaluation under varying channel conditions demonstrates that the proposed system effectively mitigates deep fades and improves reception stability while maintaining low hardware and computational complexity. The SDR-based implementation provides a flexible and scalable framework for future extensions toward multi-antenna and adaptive diversity schemes.

title: Design and Implementation of a High-Performance FPGA-bases Digital Instrument for Multi-Channel Time Measurements
venue: 2023 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium, Medical Imaging Conference and International Symposium on Room-Temperature Semiconductor Detectors (NSS MIC RTSD)
abstract: We present a compact and fully programmable instrument designed for high-performance time measurements. The instrument is a comprehensive package of hardware, firmware, and software, including a Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) hosted on a Xilinx 28-nm 7-Series Kintex-7 325T Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The hardware is made up of two modules: an "analog front-end" and a "digital processing stage". The processing unit, which contains the power section and FPGA device, is the instrument core and also manages the time-to-digital conversion by means of a Tapped Delay Line (TDL) Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC), the timestamp processing (i.e., histogramming and time-tagging), and the communication for data readout. The front-end is a plug-in board that converts incoming external time events in Low-Voltage Differential Signals (LVDSs). Thanks to this modular design, the latter stage can be replaced with the most suited input interface (e.g., Constant Fraction Discriminators ), to better meet the specifications of various detectors and experimental setups. The firmware implementation is modular thanks to the use of IP-Core structures, providing maximum flexibility to the instrument. The implemented TDL-TDC supports 16 channels plus an additional one used for synchronization purposes, allowing a resolution (LSB) of 36.6 fs, single shoot precision below 10 ps r.m.s., a dead-time lower than 10 ns, and a differential and integral non linearity of 0.8 ps and 4 ps respectively. Additionally, 16 Hardware Histogramming Modules (HHMs) and a Time Trigger Module (TTM) are implemented in the FPGA. This enables real-time collection of histograms up to 200 Msps using the HHMs, and sending of timestamps up to 60 Msps using the TTM. A C++ library facilitates communication with the board via a Universal Serial Bus 3.0 (USB) connection. To enhance user experience, a Python binding and an intuitive Graphical User Interface are also available.

title: Design and Implementation of a Mobile App for Recreational Suitability Analysis of Beach Locations in India
venue: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of a smartphone application that use the INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) API to provide real-time information associated with the degree of suitability and safety in the beaches. An important objective of this study is to help visiting tourists in India by providing information regarding weather forecasts, water quality, and warnings regarding the hazards at the coastal regions. It offers real-time alerts, support for multiple languages, and access even if the user is not connected to the internet with modern mobile development frameworks like Flutter and React Native in combination with Python and Node.js in the backend. The outcome of the initiative would be that safety to both the tourist and the authorities would be enhanced besides overall improvement in beach experience.

title: Design and Implementation of a Modular Robotic Platform for Adaptive Learning and Research Applications
venue: 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Engineering and Innovation (AISEI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a modular robotic platform intended for educational and research applications, providing a scalable progression from introductory robotics to advanced embedded systems programming. The architecture incorporates dual ESP32 microcontrollers—the ESP32-WROOM for motion control and coordination, and the ESP32-CAM for visual processing and wireless communication—enabling multiple modes of interaction, including QR code recognition, mobile application control, block-based programming, and Python scripting via MicroPython. Mechanically, the platform employs a holonomic drive system with three omni-wheels, allowing precise omnidirectional motion, and is constructed from a combination of laser-cut aluminum, acrylic, and 3D-printed components to ensure modularity and structural robustness. Experimental validation demonstrates the system’s versatility and effectiveness in classroom and laboratory environments. Future work will focus on enhancing autonomy, integrating the Robot Operating System (ROS), and refining user interfaces, thereby reinforcing the platform’s role as a comprehensive bridge between theoretical learning and practical robotics implementation.

title: Design and Implementation of a Multi-Modal Customer Support Agent with Function Calling for Airline Service Automation
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Computing and Intelligent Technologies (ICoECIT)
abstract: The increasing complexity of airline operations and rising passenger expectations demand intelligent, scalable, and real-time customer support solutions. This research aims to develop a multi-modal AI-powered customer support agent for the aviation sector that enhances responsiveness and automation in customer interactions. The proposed system integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), function-calling APIs, and image-text processing to handle both textual and visual inputs, such as queries and boarding passes. A Gradio-based web interface enables seamless user interaction through text or image uploads, while backend Python functions manage core operations including flight status tracking, ticket rebooking, and baggage policy retrieval. The methodology emphasizes modular design and interoperability, allowing deployment with both proprietary (GPT) and open-source LLMs. Experimental evaluations demonstrate high accuracy, reliability, and improved user experience compared to traditional support systems. The study’s key contribution lies in presenting a practical and extensible framework for modernizing airline customer service through multi-modal, real-time AI assistance.

title: Design and Implementation of a Non-invasive Jaundice Detection and Total Serum Bilirubin Measurement System
venue: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Now a days Jaundice is a common disease that occurs in infants or adults when the bilirubin concentration raises in the body. Some underlying condition that causes jaundice are such as acute inflammation of the liver or inflammation of the bile duct. Brain damage or death is some common consequences of this disease. There are several invasive or non-invasive methods are available to detect jaundice. But the drawbacks of existing invasive methods are so much time consuming and real time monitoring is not possible. The existing invasive methods can cause trauma in patients and the non-invasive devices cost thousands of dollars. In order to avoid additional trauma and high cost, we have designed a non-invasive jaundice detection and Total Serum Bilirubin (TSB) measurement system based on yellow discoloration on eye. Here a custom made goggle including camera with customized focal length is developed to capture the image of the sclera. A dedicated algorithm for this work with Open Computer Vision and Python language is used to analyze the image. After calibrating the system with several volunteer patients, the scheme can discern jaundice in the human body. We have tested our system among 25 patients and the test result indicates an accuracy of 90%. This can be implemented as a portable jaundice monitoring system when clinical technologies are inaccessible, which ultimately lessen health care expenditure.

title: Design and implementation of a personal loan default prediction platform based on LightGBM model
venue: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The LightGBM algorithm is used to provide new research ideas for the analysis of customer data information in the practical application of personal loan default models, in view of the fact that financial institutions are not able to reasonably assess the default risk in each lending. By comparing the accuracy, precision, recall and ROC curves, we found that the personal loan default model constructed by the LightGBM algorithm has better prediction results than the personal loan default prediction model constructed by the Random Forest algorithm, with the prediction accuracy reaching Then, based on the personal loan default model constructed by the LightGBM algorithm, a personal loan default system platform was built using the python language and the Flask framework, which was able to achieve real-time input of customer information data to predict the probability of whether the customer would default or not.

title: Design and Implementation of an AI-Powered Autonomous Security Robotic Dog with Integrated Face Recognition
venue: 2026 International Conference on Next-Gen Quantum and Advanced Computing: Algorithms, Security, and Beyond (NQComp)
abstract: Traditional security systems mostly use fixed surveillance cameras, which often result in persistent blind spots and provide little ability to respond in real time to security threats. To address these limitations, we present the design and implementation of an autonomous robotic security dog, which utilizes recent progress in mobile robotics and artificial intelligence. The robot was built on a specially designed, 3D-printed four-legged frame powered by 12 servo motors for flexible movement, all managed by a Raspberry Pi 5 computing unit. Its intelligence centers on a real-time face recognition system, for which we developed and compared two approaches: a lightweight option using Haarcascades with a Python library and a more advanced method based on the Insight Face deep learning framework paired with Facebook’s AI similarity search tools. In our analysis, the Haarcascade system achieved an average recognition rate of 92.4 % when running on a Raspberry Pi 5, whereas the Insight Face solution reached 95% accuracy on a high-end CPU workstation. This study confirms the potential of a modular robotic platform that strikes a practical balance between computational efficiency and recognition performance in active security environments, while also providing a solid foundation for future upgrades, such as autonomous navigation, more sensors, and responsive real-time behaviours.

title: Design and Implementation of Arrow Speed Measurement System based on Camera for Archery Sports
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Electronics Representation and Algorithm (ICERA)
abstract: Accurate measurement of arrow velocity is important in archery training because it is closely related to draw strength, release technique, and shooting consistency. This study develops a camera-based arrow velocity measurement system using the Mixture of Gaussian 2 (MOG2) background subtraction method and centroid tracking. The system utilizes a 1920 x 1080 pixels camera with frame rate 60 fps to record the arrow trajectory. Each video frame is processed using the MOG2 algorithm to separate moving objects from the background, followed by contour extraction and centroid calculation to track the arrow position. The displacement between centroid positions is converted from pixels to meters using a calibration factor and subsequently used to calculate arrow velocity automatically. The system is implemented using the Python programming language and the OpenCV library for image processing and object tracking. Experimental results at shooting distances ranging from 5 m to 10 m show that the system can successfully detect the arrow trajectory and measure average velocity values ranging from 44.56 m/s to 48.19 m/s. The developed system achieved overall average percentage error of approximately 4.84%, with all error values remaining below 10%. These results indicate that the developed system is sufficiently accurate and feasible as supporting tool for archery training performance analysis.

title: Design and Implementation of AUDREY AUV as a Prototype Underwater Robot
venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: AUDREY AUV represents an essential robotic technology designed for underwater exploration. The research and development of AUDREY involve multiple phases, including the design and fabrication of the vehicle’s body, integration of hardware components, and the creation of software to enable fully autonomous operation. The primary objective of AUDREY is to navigate underwater along a predefined path without human intervention, with a secondary capability of avoiding obstacles and retrieving metal objects from the pool floor using ferrite magnets. The system is equipped with a range of sensors, including pressure sensors, an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), an ultrasonic rangefinder, and cameras. Data from these sensors is combined using the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) technique for improved accuracy. Control of the AUV is implemented using algorithms written in Python, utilizing DroneKit and Link libraries, and integrated with OpenCV for real-time image processing to support autonomous maneuvering. In testing, AUDREY achieved a maximum dive depth of 2 meters in a swimming pool and successfully transmitted live underwater video to a monitor. However, further development is required before this AUV can be deployed effectively in open-sea environments.

title: Design and Implementation of Automated Attendance System Using Contactless Facial Recognition
venue: 2024 International Conference on Power, Energy, Control and Transmission Systems (ICPECTS)
abstract: In today's digital age, facial recognition technology holds significant importance across various industries. While it may not boast the same level of accuracy as iris or fingerprint recognition, its widespread adoption is largely due to its non-intrusive and contactless nature. Moreover, facial recognition systems offer a promising solution for streamlining attendance procedures in educational institutions, offices, and other settings. By automating the attendance process, these systems alleviate the time-consuming and burdensome nature of manual tracking while also mitigating the risk of proxy attendance. Essentially, the objective of such a system is to leverage facial detection and recognition algorithms to identify students as they enter the classroom, thereby seamlessly marking their attendance. Libraries such as OpenCV and face_recognition were utilized. The system integrates ESP32 and ESP32-CAM hardware components to capture facial images in real- time, ensuring a seamless and efficient attendance-taking process. Using the Python OpenCV library, an accurate and reliable facial recognition algorithm has been developed, enabling the system to accurately identify and authenticate students. Attendance data is securely stored and managed in a cloud-based database, facilitating real-time access for teachers and students to monitor attendance records. A user-friendly application is designed to provide teachers with attendance management capabilities and students with the ability to track their attendance history, enhancing transparency and engagement in the educational process. The objectives were to enhance recognition accuracy, securely store student data, and ensure system compatibility. The outcomes include improved accuracy, contactless attendance logging, secure data storage, scalability, efficiency gains, and comprehensive documentation.

title: Design and Implementation of Campus Digital Twin System Based on Game Engine
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Sensors, Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICSECE)
abstract: The design and implementation scheme of game engine is proposed for the campus digital twin system. The system integrates various sensor data and three-dimensional models generated by drone tilt photography technology, providing users with a real-time and highly realistic simulation of the campus environment. It mainly uses the WiFi microcontroller ESP8266 to remotely transmit data from current sensors ACS712, smoke sensors MQ2 and MQ135 and immersion sensors by using the MQTT protocol via message queue. On the backend, it uses Python scripts to parse the uploaded data and store it separately in MySQL and Redis databases. It writes the backend programs by using the Springboot framework and provides the corresponding application program interface API. The front-end adopts the advanced Unreal engine 5 for display and uses the VaRest plugin to send HTTP requests to the back-end, so as to obtain the real-time data for rendering. This article provides the detailed introduction to the design, implementation and optimization process of the system and verifies its effectiveness. In addition, it extensively discusses the basic technologies, definitions and methods which are involved in developing the digital twin system.

title: Design and Implementation of Gesture Recognition and Writing Text Virtually Using Finger
venue: 2019 Third International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)
abstract: This paper deals with real time gesture recognition and writing alphanumeric letters over the air using fingertip. The human and machine interaction lays an important role in gesture recognition. The proposed method contains two parts: First, a video camera is used to acquire the image for gesture recognition and then the fingertip is recognized from the live video frames. In this work, the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) algorithm is applied to plot the alphanumeric characters with respect to the finger movement. As a result, we can eliminate the requirements of the input devices like keypad, mouse, stylus, stick, and glove or pen and so on. Using Python language coding, we have obtained the text on the screen. Further, recognition of gesture does not require sensors or any hardware other than a camera. Since, the proposed work is a simulation based approach; hence the developed algorithm executes the recognition task in a simple, fast and lucid manner.

title: Design and Implementation of Multi-Protocol Gateway for Internet of Things
venue: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Industry 4.0, Artificial Intelligence, and Communications Technology (IAICT)
abstract: Heterogeneity is one of the top challenges for Internet of Things. One of the cases is the diversity of communication protocol used in IoT devices. This paper discusses the design and implementation of a multi-protocol gateway that can receive several protocols at once, i.e. WiFi, Bluetooth Low Energy and ZigBee from IoT devices. The gateway is powered by a single board computer which is equipped by required transceiver module. A python script is used to control the process in the backend, along with MySQL for data storage and a frontend user interface built by Lazarus. A dashboard that displays the collected data and the network topology is provided to validate the work of the gateway. As the result, the gateway is able to accept all of the three communication protocols at the same time and display the data in real time in the dashboard. The result also shows that each protocol has different delay and packet delivery ratio. The WiFi protocols is found to have the largest delay which is 362 ms, and also the lowest packet delivery ratio which is 97%.

title: Design and implementation of Polyphase based FHSS modulator using GNU Radio and SDR
venue: 2022 4th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Wireless communication is the fastest-growing sector in the communication industry. The nature of wirelessly transmitted signals makes them prone to eavesdropping and jamming. The intercepting of these signals leads to the leaking of sensitive data and poses a threat. As a result, the security and dependability of wireless systems are jeopardized. Spread Spectrum enables the signal to be spread out over a larger bandwidth before transmission. Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum (FHSS) prevents the transmitted signal from eavesdropping by hopping onto different carrier frequencies. FHSS has been prominently used in military applications and wireless standards such as Bluetooth. The higher the hopping bandwidth, the more immune is the system to interferences. A digital FHSS system based on Polyphase channelizers is designed using Software Defined Radios (SDR). Polyphase channelizers utilize N-point Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) for inverse Fourier transformation, the computational efficiency of using IFFT is discussed. The SDR approach is used to implement Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum as they offer faster prototyping and reliability. Using GNU Radio and Universal Software Radio Peripheral, a digital-based Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum modulator using Polyphase channelizers is designed and implemented in real time.

title: Design and Implementation of Regional Food Distribution Platform Based on Big Data
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Industrial Design (AIID)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of big data has made people's daily life very convenient, and at the same time, tasting all kinds of food has become an important activity for people to travel. Due to the vast territory of China, there are many types of cuisines with great differences, it is very important for travelers to understand the special regional cuisines in the area. This project aggregates regional food data based on big data, and provides tourists with efficient, stable and professional data retrieval and analysis services through a visual data interface, and provides intuitive, accurate, and real-time data support for the decision-making of finding characteristic regional food. This thesis first conducted a relevant understanding of big data and the overall situation of regional cuisine, analyzed the distribution of food in the sub-provincial city of Xi'an, explored the research methods and implementation methods of related projects at home and abroad, based on this, summarized the research of this project the goal. At the same time, the focus of this project is to analyze the price, score and popularity of regional food data analysis in my country, and to summarize, proofread and organize the data obtained before into standard and standardized data. Through the classification of basic information, the visual analysis and display of data is realized, and the key data urgently needed by decision makers are extracted from it. To analyze the needs of decision makers, establish corresponding strategies and measures to improve the quality of data services. The establishment of this system provides a useful supplement and improvement to the existing industry data analysis system. The system is mainly divided into six modules, which are data collection, data review, data summary, and visual data display modules. Among them, data collection includes crawling relevant data from the Internet and retrieving key data. The data audit function includes classifyi

title: Design and Implementation of Regional Identification Algorithm for Highway Pavement Diseases Based on UAV Vision and CNN
venue: 2025 32nd International Conference on Geoinformatics
abstract: With the continuous expansion of highway networks in recent years, the monitoring and repair of road diseases have become one of the important tasks in traffic management. Traditional manual inspection methods are inefficient and prone to missing disease areas. Therefore, a pavement disease detection system based on UAV vision and deep learning algorithms has emerged. The formation mechanism of pavement diseases was first analyzed, and the UAV pavement image acquisition equipment was introduced. Then, a pavement disease identification algorithm using YOLOv8 was constructed. Finally, Python programming was employed to complete the construction of a regional identification model for highway pavement diseases based on CNN, data loading, and model training and testing. The experimental results show that the system exhibits high accuracy and real-time performance in image, video, and real-time camera identification, effectively assisting in the monitoring of highway diseases. This system can significantly improve the automation level of pavement disease detection, reduce manual workload, enhance road management efficiency, and provide strong support for the safety and maintenance of highways.

title: Design and Implementation of Safety Logic with Fine Impulse Test System for a Nuclear Reactor Shutdown System
venue: 2014 27th International Conference on VLSI Design and 2014 13th International Conference on Embedded Systems
abstract: 500MWe sodium cooled Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) is in the advanced stage of construction at Kalpakkam (Tamilnadu), INDIA. PFBR is provided with two independent and fast acting shutdown systems (SDS). Each SDS consists of sensors, signal processing electronics, safety logic (SL) system, drive mechanisms and neutron absorber rods (NARs). The purpose of SDS is to reduce the reactor power rapidly during abnormal events which could otherwise lead to catastrophic situations. During an abnormal event, the NARs are rapidly inserted into the reactor core within a second, in an operation called scram. An automatic and rapid shutdown of a nuclear reactor in response to an abnormal event is known as scram. Safety Logic (SL) system continuously monitors the state of various reactor scram parameters (i.e. the events requiring prompt reactor shutdown), and performs 2-out-of-3 (2oo3) voting on each scram parameter thus enables/disables the flow of current in the Electro-Magnet (EM) coils, which are holding the NARs. During an abnormal event (For example: rapid and uncontrolled increase in neutron flux inside reactor core, core temperature crossing its set limits etc.) SL system initiates reactor shutdown action by de-energizing the EM-Coils causing all the NARs to drop into the reactor core under gravity. The scram parameters are triplicated to achieve high availability and reliability. The design of SL system was carried out using VHDL and targeted to Simple Programmable Logic Devices (SPLDs) and Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGAs) devices. The probable faults in digital logic devices are stuck-at faults (i.e. stuck-at-'0' or stuck-at-'1'). For SL System, stuck-at-'0' is a safe condition whereas stuck-at-'1' is a dangerous condition (i.e. during an abnormal event SL may not be able to initiate reactor shutdown action). title: Design and Implementation of Smart Bin with RFID-Based User Accountability
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
abstract: The persistent challenges of solid waste management in rapidly urbanizing areas require establishing innovative, data-driven systems for effective collection, monitoring, and accountability. This paper outlines designing and developing a Smart Bin with RFID-Based User Identification & Waste Usage Tracking to promote user accountability while improving waste analytics through the Internet of Things (IoT). The proposed system utilizes an ESP32 microcontroller alongside several different sensing modules for user identification (RFID reader), a fill level sensor (ultrasonic sensor), and a waste category identification system (load cell and HX711 amplifier) that accurately measures the weight of the waste. Additionally, the lid of the Smart Bin is automated using a servo motor mechanism, based on verified user identity, to increase hygiene and capability. The data collected from user ID, waste type, weight, fill level, and time are relayed via Wi-Fi to a cloud-based database (Firebase) for real-time analysis and logging. While assisting in creating sustainability standards, transparency is promoted, ecologically acceptable disposal techniques are made accessible to customers, and garbage collection schedules are enhanced for local government official. The inclusion of both RFID and IoT technology presents an intelligent solution for innovative waste management by providing the capacity to trace waste history, make data-driven decisions based on analysis, and promote environmentally responsible waste disposal practices.

title: Design and Implementation of Underwater Acoustic Signal Acquisition and Display Software Based on PyQt5
venue: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In underwater target detection experiments, real-time signal processing and result display of collected underwater acoustic signal data are very important for the experiment. This paper has designed and implemented an underwater acoustic signal acquisition and display software based on PyQt5. This software can control the acquisition device to collect real-time underwater acoustic signal data received by active sonar, and perform relevant signal processing and result display on the data in real time. This software uses a serial port to achieve communication between the software and the acquisition device. It controls the acquisition device by calling the C++ dynamic link library provided by the acquisition device developer. The software obtains real-time underwater acoustic signal data from the acquisition device, and then performs relevant signal processing on the underwater acoustic signal data. The data processing results are displayed in the form of time-domain graphs, spectrograms, and target trajectory graphs. During the experiment, users can also save the experiment data in real time as needed, and replay these experiment data files as needed after the experiment. Through extensive practical testing, this paper has demonstrated that the software effectively achieves real-time acquisition, signal processing, and result display of underwater acoustic signals. It has the advantages of low code volume, high execution efficiency, strong stability, and good scalability.

title: Design and implementation of water quality monitoring for eel fish aquaculture
venue: 2016 International Symposium on Electronics and Smart Devices (ISESD)
abstract: We have designed and implemented water quality monitoring using Raspberry Pi3. This device is made to monitor the water quality of aquaculture, which uses an aeration in the form of a microbubble. Some water quality parameters that used in this monitoring are dissolved oxygen (DO), acidity (pH), and temperature. Data processing devices used Raspberry Pi3 and python program used to create a sensor acquisition program and the program viewer. Tests carried out in two stages, those are sensors reading stability and device monitoring performance. The testing sensor stability conducted in the laboratory and the testing device monitoring carried out in aquariums using microbubble aeration. An implementation held on eel aquaculture using microbubble aeration. The test results also used for examination of microbubble aeration. The device can be used to monitor water quality in the laboratory, aquariums and eel aquaculture. All of the features in this monitoring device can function properly and smoothly.

title: Design and Implementation Path of PBL for Front-End Development Technology Empowered by GAI
venue: 2026 15th International Conference on Educational and Information Technology (ICEIT)
abstract: With the increasingly widespread application of Generative Artificial Intelligence(GAI) in higher education, new opportunities for innovation and transformation have emerged for traditional Project-based Learning(PBL) pedagogy. Aiming at the deficiencies of traditional PBL in front-end development technology—such as the lack of efficient content generation, real-time tutoring, and systematic process management—this study conducted a two-semester tracking investigation. It comparatively analyzed the multi-dimensional impacts of GAI on students’ learning outcomes in PBL for front-end development, including development efficiency, code quality, falut rate, and technical documentation quality. A Mann-Whitney U test was performed using Python, and the results show that GAI significantly improves students’ multi-dimensional competencies, enhances their learning interest, and addresses the shortcomings of traditional PBL. This study demonstrates the necessity of empowering university front-end development teaching with GAI and provides new ideas for the advancement of PBL.

title: Design and Integration of an Embodied Cyber-Physical System for Autonomous Conversational Interaction: A Healthcare Case Study
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Mechatronics Technology and Intelligent Manufacturing (ICMTIM)
abstract: Autonomous human-machine interaction systems are increasingly crucial in service domains requiring structured information gathering, such as healthcare intake. However, existing solutions often lack the tight integration of physical embodiment and real-time control necessary for robust realworld operation. This paper presents the design and integration of an embodied intelligent mechatronic system, the Conversational Patient History Information Record (CPHIR), which automates patient interviewing using a modular cyberphysical architecture. The system employs a host-centric hub-and-spoke topology utilizing ZeroMQ for deterministic coordination between a Python-based Large Language Model (LLM) core and distributed hardware nodes. Key features include perception-driven physical adaptation, where an embedded controller dynamically adjusts the interface height via a linear actuator based on real-time face detection, and multimodal sensing (thermal, SpO2, blood pressure) for comprehensive data acquisition. Evaluation across 15 interaction scenarios with clinical experts $(\mathrm{N}=5)$ demonstrated high system reliability, achieving an overall interaction quality score of $4.33 / 5$ and data integrity of $4.20 / 5$. These results validate the efficacy of coupling conversational intelligence with embodied mechatronic control, offering a scalable reference architecture for intelligent service automation.

title: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Minimal Asynchronous Communication Library for Embedded Systems
venue: 2025 International Technical Conference on Circuits/Systems, Computers, and Communications (ITC-CSCC)
abstract: In recent years, the increasing complexity and multifunctionality of embedded systems have necessitated simple and efficient Inter-Process Communication (IPC) methods. This paper presents the design, implementation, and performance evaluation of a minimal, high-performance asynchronous communication library for embedded systems. Inspired by ZeroMQ, the proposed solution is developed as an easy-to-use, class-based IPC module that supports both Named Pipe and file-based communication methods. The library is designed to enable each process or module to manage its own independent communication channel, thereby enhancing modularity and maintainability. Its asynchronous, non-blocking design facilitates real-time data transmission between processes. Turnaround time evaluation was conducted using the RasPike-ART environment on a Raspberry Pi, wherein a C++ process communicated with a Python process over 15,000 cycles. The results demonstrated that the Named Pipe implementation achieved an average turnaround time comparable to, or even faster than, ZeroMQ—albeit with a slightly higher latency variability—while the file-based approach, though adaptable to systems lacking Named Pipe support, incurred higher delays. The findings indicate that the developed IPC library, despite its minimal design, offers similar performance to ZeroMQ, while being adaptable to a diverse range of embedded environments. Future work is proposed to extend the module’s capabilities to support additional messaging patterns and features such as persistence and guaranteed delivery, thereby addressing limitations observed in current communication libraries.

title: Design and prototype implementation of V2V Communication for Cooperative Emergency Response in ITS
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE)
abstract: This project presents the design and implementation of an Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) utilizing Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication through ESP32 microcontrollers and a Raspberry Pi as the central processing unit. The objective is to enhance traffic safety and coordination by enabling real-time communication between vehicles and infrastructure. Two main scenarios are demonstrated: an Emergency Brake system, where vehicles automatically synchronize braking upon obstacle detection, and an Emergency Vehicle Lane Evacuation, which prioritizes lane clearance for emergency vehicles. The system is developed using Python-based programming, integrating Wi-Fi (ESP-NOW) and Bluetooth for communication. Results show a reliable real-time response, stable motion control, and accurate sensor feedback; however, constraints such as limited Bluetooth range, hardware capacity, and limitations on the number of vehicles were also observed. Overall, the study validates the potential of small-scale V2X-enabled ITS prototypes to improve road safety and efficiency, with future work focusing on 5G integration, machine learning, and enhanced centralized control for intelligent decision-making.

title: Design and Realization of Portable Electrochemiluminescence Detection System Based on Phytium Pi
venue: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This study presents a portable detection device that utilizes the principle of electrochemiluminescence (ECL). The device uses a lithium battery as the electrode excitation source. And the paper-based three electrodes is used as the solution carrier. The image is captured by an embedded camera and processed on a Phytium Pi development version. All above are in the dark room which is completed using 3D printing technology. The user interface of the software is developed using PyQt5 on the Debian system. Additionally, the software includes modules for camera drivers, image acquisition, and preprocessing based on OpenCV. The data validity is detected in real-time using the MobileNetv2 network. The design method can detect melamine concentrations ranging from $10^{-3} \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}$ to $10^{-8} \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}$. This method is significant for the application of ECL detection technology, as it allows for the detection of various substances by prefabricating different calibration curves. It has high potential for widespread use.

title: Design and Research of a Multi-Mode High-Reliability Ground/Open Discrete Quantity Acquisition Circuit
venue: 2026 5th International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Airborne ground/open discrete quantities serve as critical signals for state perception and command interaction of aircraft electromechanical systems. The anti-interference and self-test performance of acquisition circuits directly affect flight safety. Conventional circuits reuse external airborne ground (E-GND) references, which are prone to logical misjudgments caused by E-GND potential differences and conducted electromagnetic interference. Moreover, their single-node architecture delivers poor fault tolerance, and conventional Built-In Test (BIT) interrupts data acquisition, failing to implement full-link online detection during flight. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi-mode high-reliability acquisition circuit. A single-node acquisition architecture with an isolated internal reference ground (I-GND) is adopted to block E-GND ground loop interference. Two independent sampling nodes are arranged to synchronously collect signal levels, and joint judgment of two sampling node signals is used to suppress false triggering induced by single-point interference. A non-intrusive online BIT scheme adopting XNOR logic of dual sampling node levels is proposed to realize periodic full-link fault inspection without signal acquisition interruption, which expands the BIT detection scope of signal links and greatly boosts BIT fault coverage. A simulation platform complying with GJB 151C-2024 is built on Multisim, with power frequency interference, pulse interference and various hardware faults injected for verification. Test results show that the minimum acquisition accuracy of conventional circuits is only 98.44%, while the proposed circuit maintains a stable 100% acquisition accuracy under all interference conditions, and the fault coverage of BIT is remarkably enhanced. This design effectively improves the robustness and testability of key signal acquisition for airborne systems, providing an engineering reference for high-safety avionics interface design.

title: Design and Simulation of an Embedded System-Based Alarm Circuit Using 8051 Microcontroller
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 5th International Conference on Control and Intelligent Robotics
abstract: In the last few years, embedded systems have become paramount in real-time monitoring and safety applications. This study presents the design and simulation of an embedded system-based alarm circuit using the 8051 microcontroller. The main objective is to detect signal interruptions and immediately trigger an audible alert through an efficient fault detection process. The circuit incorporates an optical isolator (PC817) for the integrity of signals and no external noise interference, along with a switch made of a transistor for the buzzer. The system proposed was designed and simulated using Proteus software where functional testing shows that the system has a high reliable ability to detect and respond to signal disruption. Results obtained confirm that the alarm circuit responds well to different scenarios of interruption, therefore making it fit for industrial and safety-critical environments. The study brings out the potential for developing reliable fault detection and alarm solutions based on microcontroller systems, which adds to the advancement of applications of embedded systems.

title: Design and Simulation of Multilingual Intelligent Language Service System for Cross-border Logistics Based on Multilingual Pre-training Modeling
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area International Conference on Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multilingual intelligent service system that integrates dynamic domain adaptation mechanism, constructs cross-language logistics knowledge graph (X-LogisKG), and realizes real-time translation, risk warning and path optimization functions in 12 languages. Design a hybrid multi-task learning framework to improve the accuracy of intent recognition to 87.3% in low-resource language scenarios. Constructed a logistics-language joint simulation model based on AnyLogic, and verified that the system can improve cross-border transportation time efficiency by 31.6% and reduce the error rate to below 2.4%.The results of this research demonstrate the excellent performance and good effect of the system, which supports the intelligent development of cross-border logistics.

title: Design and specification of embedded systems in Java using successive, formal refinement
venue: Proceedings 1998 Design and Automation Conference. 35th DAC. (Cat. No.98CH36175)
abstract: Successive, formal refinement is a new approach for specification of embedded systems using a general-purpose programming language. Systems are formally modeled as abstractable synchronous reactive systems, and Java is used as the design input language. A policy of use is applied to Java, in the form of language usage restrictions and class-library extensions to ensure consistency with the formal model. A process of incremental, user-guided program transformation is used to refine a Java program until it is consistent with the policy of use. The final product is a system specification possessing the properties of the formal model, including deterministic behavior, bounded memory usage and bounded execution time. This approach allows systems design to begin with the flexibility of a general-purpose language, followed by gradual refinement into a more restricted form necessary for specification.

title: Design Development and Analysis of 3-DOF Robotic Arm
venue: 2023 9th IEEE India International Conference on Power Electronics (IICPE)
abstract: The paper presents the arm design, kinematics analysis, path planning, and CAD modeling, enabling the practical use of a low-cost robotic arm as a laboratory model for teaching and learning about robots. The arm design is created using Fusion 360 software and features four servo motors as actuators. Kinematics analysis is performed using the Denavit-Hartenberg convention. The proposed framework encompasses a robotic arm with three degrees of freedom (3-DOF) and employs four DC servo motors for each joint's movement. Arm motion control is based on an Arduino control unit, utilizing a Python-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) with a kinematics algorithm in the backend, providing a user-friendly environment for remotely controlling the robot arm's end-effector. The path planning framework is constructed using cubic splines, taking joint restrictions into account. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through RoboAnalyzer simulation results, demonstrating improved motion accuracy, smoothness, and efficiency. Additionally, this robot arm can operate autonomously for pick-and-place applications with the assistance of an Arduino controller.

title: Design for testability in embedded software projects
venue: 2011 IEEE/AIAA 30th Digital Avionics Systems Conference
abstract: The purpose of this white paper is to focus on design techniques or methodologies that add testability features to embedded software which is an integral and important process for verification of any safety critical system. This paper presents testability in two forms: software testability i.e. testability at code level and design testability: i.e. testability at software requirements level. The two testability forms are further classified into subtypes explained in detail with examples which cite issues that are faced by engineers while performing verification. In this paper I have also come up with metrics which could become an important criterion in calculating the testability of a system considering the number of inputs that can be driven and the outputs that can be observed in the software during the verification process. Practical usage of these metrics may help designers understand how testable the system they have designed is, thus reducing verification effort and project cost. Good testability features, if not present in a system, may lead to increased cost and completion period of the project at a time when cost reduction and deadline chasing is the key to winning future projects. This paper endeavors to provide software developers guidance to incorporate important testability features into the software during the design and coding phase.

title: Design of a Built-in-Self-Test Implemented AES Crypto Processor ASIC
venue: 2020 11th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a (built-in self-test) BIST implemented Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) crypto-processor Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC). Hardware implementation provides higher speed and better physical security than that of software implementation. One of the burning issues is the testability of a complex VLSI chip. This research addresses this problem by implementing a mixed-mode BIST technique into the chip. The ASIC is designed using Verilog Hardware Description (HDL). It works both in normal mode and test mode. In test mode, the test manager enables an LFSR and initializes it with seed value from the memory and generates the desired number of pseudorandom and deterministic test patterns which are applied to the AES ASIC and outputs are compressed into a signature through the output response analyzer (ORA) which is compared with that of the pre-stored golden signature kept in the memory. If both the signatures match each other then the ASIC is ensured as fault-free otherwise it is faulty. The ASIC is simulated in two platforms: Java and ModelSim to ensure its proper functionality which has been verified using NIST provided input and output.

title: Design of a Compact and Reconfigurable Onboard Data Handling System
venue: 2018 IEEE Intl Conf on Parallel & Distributed Processing with Applications, Ubiquitous Computing & Communications, Big Data & Cloud Computing, Social Computing & Networking, Sustainable Computing & Communications (ISPA/IUCC/BDCloud/SocialCom/SustainCom)
abstract: Onboard data handling (OBDH) system is the key to spacecraft avionics. To adapt to the harsh external space environment, traditional onboard data handling system is usually highly expensive, complex and arduous by using high quality components. Design of a compact and reconfigurable onboard data handling system based is proposed in this paper. A NOR Flash with mass storage is designed as the program memory for CPU and SRAM FPGAs. The programs of the CPU and SRAM FPGAs in this system can still be reconfigurable for the launched satellites. Rad-hard designs from the Software and hardware are adopted in the onboard data handling system to realize the performances of high reliability, anti-SEU(single event upset) effect, software reconfiguration with less mass, volume and cost. Some experimental results are shown at last in the system verification.

title: Design of a counter-drone visualisation platform incorporating sensor-data fusion
venue: 2024 15th IFIP Wireless and Mobile Networking Conference (WMNC)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) platform for sensor-data fusion and visualisation.
