Software integrity verification of device swarms is necessary to ensure their correct and safe operation as well as to protect them against attacks. However, current device attestation schemes assume a single prover device and do not scale to swarms. We present SEDA, the first attestation scheme for device swarms. We introduce a formal security model for swarm attestation and show security of our approach in this model. We demonstrate two proof-of-concept implementations based on two recent (remote) attestation architectures for embedded systems, including an Intel research platform. We assess performance of SEDA based on these implementations and simulations of large swarms. SEDA can efficiently attest swarms with dynamic and static topologies common in automotive, avionic, industrial control and critical infrastructures settings.

title: SEED Internet Emulator: An Open-Source Tool for Network and Cybersecurity Courses
venue: Proceedings of the 53rd ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education V. 2
abstract: In cybersecurity courses, it is quite challenging to do hands-on activities that involve many components of the Internet, such as bringing down the Internet, attacking a blockchain, etc. To solve this problem, we have developed an open-source Internet Emulator, which is a Python library, consisting of the classes for each essential element of the Internet, including autonomous system, network, host, router, BGP router, Internet exchange, etc. It also includes the classes for a variety of services, including Web, DNS, Botnet, Darknet, Blockchain, and more are being developed. Using these classes, users can construct a mini-Internet to emulate the real-world Internet. Although it is small, it has all the essential elements of the real Internet. The construction is compiled into Docker container files, and the emulation is executed by Docker on a single machine or on multiple cloud machines. With this Internet Emulator, we can develop hands-on activities for cybersecurity courses, including BGP prefix hijacking, attacks on smart contract, using Darknet to achieve anonymity, launching Botnet and ransomware attacks, etc. While the emulator was initially developed for cybersecurity courses, it can also be used for network courses, for students to learn how the Internet technologies work, such as routing, BGP, IP Anycast, DNS, CDN, and many other interesting technologies.

title: Seeking Time-Composable Partitions of Tasks for COTS Multicore Processors
venue: 2015 IEEE 18th International Symposium on Real-Time Distributed Computing
abstract: The timing verification of real-time single core systems involves a timing analysis step that yields an Execution Time Bound (ETB) for each task, followed by a schedulability analysis step, where the scheduling attributes of the individual tasks, including the ETB, are studied from the system level perspective. The transition between those two steps involves accounting for the interference effects that arise when tasks contend for access to shared resource. The advent of multicore processors challenges the viability of this two-step approach because several complex contention effects at the processor level arise that cause tasks to be unable to make progress while actually holding the CPU, which are very difficult to tightly capture by simply inflating the tasks' ETB. In this paper we show how contention on access to hardware shared resources creates a circular dependence between the determination of tasks' ETB and their scheduling at runtime. To help loosen this knot we present an approach that acknowledges different flavors of time compos ability, examining in detail the variant intended for partitioned scheduling, which we evaluate on two real processor boards used in the space domain.

title: Selecting components: a process for context-driven evaluation
venue: Tenth Asia-Pacific Software Engineering Conference, 2003.
abstract: We describe a process for selecting and evaluating candidates for component based software engineering. The process is aimed at developers sourcing components from third party vendors. Component metadata and a formalised specification of the ideal component, including context information, are used to drive the process. This specification is used to shortlist candidate components from commercial repositories and to generate the tests and adaptations for the candidate components. Metrics from each stage of the selection and evaluation process are then combined to compare and rank components for inclusion in the target application. This approach to component selection, using context information and formal methods, helps address issues with component sourcing, selection and testing of third party components.

title: Selecting Context-Sensitivity Modularly for Accelerating Object-Sensitive Pointer Analysis
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
abstract: Object-sensitive pointer analysis (denoted kobj under $k$k-limiting) for an object-oriented program can be accelerated if context-sensitivity can be selectively applied to only some precision-critical variables/objects in a program. Existing pre-analyses for making such selections, which are performed as whole-program analyses to a program, are developed based on two broad approaches. One approach preserves the precision of object-sensitive pointer analysis but achieves limited speedups by reasoning about all the possible value flows in the program conservatively, while the other approach achieves greater speedups but sacrifices precision (often unduly) by examining only some but not all the value flows in the program heuristically. In this paper, we introduce a new pre-analysis approach, Turner$^{\mathcal{m}}$m (where $\mathcal {m}$m stands for modularity), that represents a sweet spot between these two existing ones, as it is designed to enable kobj to run significantly faster than the former approach and achieve significantly better precision than the latter approach. Turner$^{\mathcal{m}}$m is simple, lightweight yet effective due to two novel aspects in its design. First, we exploit a key observation that some precision-uncritical objects in the program can be approximated based on the object-containment relationship pre-established (from Andersen's analysis). In practice, this approximation introduces only a small degree of imprecision into kobj. Second, leveraging this initial approximation, we apply a novel object reachability analysis to the program by pre-analyzing its methods according to a reverse topological order of its call graph. When pre-analyzing each method, we make use of a simple DFA (Deterministic Finite Automaton) to reason about object reachability intra-procedurally from its entry to its exit along all the possible value flows established by its statements to identify its precision-critical variables/objects. In practice, this new modular ob

title: Self-adaptive IoT architectures: an emergency handling case study
venue: Proceedings of the 12th European Conference on Software Architecture: Companion Proceedings
abstract: Along with the rapid growth of IoT technologies and devices, their solutions are currently being applied on various domains such as health-care, transportation and agriculture, but mainly on crowd monitoring and emergency handling. The latter is a safety critical IoT system based on collecting and analyzing the real-time data to perform proper actuation. In order to engineer such a high quality IoT application, a proper software architecture should be designed. In order for the software architecture to be able to optimize critical requirements such as fault-tolerance, performance and energy consumption, it ought to: i) adapt itself to real-time environment transformation, ii) be designed in a proper level of elements distribution. In this paper, we critically analyze a set of IoT distribution and self-adaptation patterns to identify their suitable architectural combinations. Further, we use our IoT modeling framework (CAPS) to model an emergency handling system. Based on these, we design two quality driven architectures to be used for a forest monitoring and evacuation example and qualitatively evaluate and compare them.

title: Self-Learning Evolutionary Control Networks for Adaptive Energy Optimization in Smart IoT Cyber-Physical Systems
venue: 2026 Sixth International Conference on Advances in Electrical, Computing, Communications and Sustainable Technologies (ICAECT)
abstract: The explosive growth of IoT devices in cyber-physical systems (CPS) has caused tremendous energy consumption issues, requiring intelligent, scalable optimization techniques. Rule-based and static machine learning models do not learn adaptability in dynamic environments and are incapable of generalizing in diverse IoT deployments. The present study introduces a Self-Learning Evolutionary Control Network (SLECN) to obtain adaptive, real-time energy optimization in smart IoT-CPS environments. The architecture combines evolutionary algorithms for policy evolution with reinforcement learning for self-adaptation. It consists of preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and deployment. A private IoT Energy Consumption dataset gathered from smart meters, sensors, and appliances in residential and commercial environments. The hybrid strategy ensures scalability, real-time adaptability, and less energy wastage without compromising system performance. The model attained 56.7 % energy efficiency, 145 ms response time, and $\text{9 5. 4 \%}$ resource utilization. Python was employed for full-stack implementation, which involved preprocessing, model training, and deployment.

title: Self-Optimizing Automated Learning Pipeline for Big Data Exploration and Predictive Intelligence Applications
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference for Convergence in Computing Technology (I3CTCON)
abstract: The rapid increase in big data, which is characterized by volume, velocity, variety, veracity, and value, has placed a highly urgent need on scalable, secure, and automated machine learning (ML) solutions. The traditional ML pipelines may require a lot of manual tuning, do not operate with efficiency in terms of data management and are scaled in a distributed environment. In this paper, the Self-Optimizing Automated Learning Pipeline towards Big Data Exploration and Predictive Intelligence Applications is introduced, which is an end-to-end framework that comprises secure data ingestion, MinIO-based distributed storage, and Parquet-optimized data handling to improve its functionality and efficiency. To reduce human effort, the proposed system is an automated preprocessing, feature engineering model selection, and containerized deployment system based on Python modules. The interface is configurable, with a number of checkboxes, and is capable of supporting heterogeneous datasets and workflows which can be customized. The pipeline supports various ML models, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transformer networks, and classic algorithms, such as XGBoost and Random Forest, that allow it to be flexible to wide range of analytical tasks. Experimental results using large-scale datasets reveal significant performance improvements - Transformer model takes 32% of the time and has 28% better storage efficiency as well as up to 94.8% accuracy and the Transformer modeling model is faster than any other predictive model. Besides, user-owned MinIO buckets improve the privacy of data and facilitate distributed processing that is scaled. On the whole, the suggested system provides an efficient, safe, and high-performance system to big data analytics, setting the base to further developments in federated learning and real-time analytics and autonomy in governing the model.

title: SemOpt: LLM-Driven Code Optimization via Rule-Based Analysis
venue: ACM Trans. Softw. Eng. Methodol.
abstract: Automated code optimization improves program performance through refactoring, and recent studies leverage LLMs for this purpose. Existing approaches mine optimization commits from open-source codebases to build large-scale knowledge bases, then employ retrieval techniques such as BM25 to obtain relevant examples for hotspot code, guiding LLMs in optimization. However, semantically equivalent optimizations often appear in syntactically dissimilar code, so current retrieval methods fail to identify pertinent examples, leading to suboptimal results.To address these limitations, we propose SemOpt, a framework that leverages static program analysis to identify code segments, retrieve optimization strategies, and generate optimized results. SemOpt has three LLM-powered components: (1) a strategy library builder that extracts and clusters strategies from code modifications, (2) a rule generator that produces Semgrep static analysis rules to capture each strategy's applicability, and (3) an optimizer that generates optimized code using the strategy library.On a benchmark of 151 C/C++ and 150 Python optimization tasks, SemOpt shows consistent improvements across different LLMs, increasing successful optimizations by 1.38 to 28 times on C/C++ and 4.60 to 6.33 times on Python versus the baseline. On large-scale projects, SemOpt improves performance metrics by 5.04%–218.07% on C/C++ and 61.77%–479.90% on Python, showing cross-language generalization and practical effectiveness.

title: Sensing, Wireless Transmission, and Smart Processing of Heart Signals
venue: 2021 5th International Conference on Internet of Things and Applications (IoT)
abstract: In recent years, by increasing the number of epidemics, the concept of telemedicine and its combination with the Internet of Things (IoT), has become a more prominent subject in engineering. The purpose of this study is to implement an IoT system that can sense the heart signal and detect the arrhythmia in a heartbeat by using smart signal processing and send them through the internet to a relative of the patient or doctor. In this system, Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are received by electrodes and sent to the AD8232 chip. Then, by connecting to the ESP32 module, information through the Wi-Fi network and Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol, is sent to the broker created on Raspberry Pi. Then, using Python and through the Decision Tree algorithm, the heartbeat's performance is evaluated as a smart process. The accuracy of the algorithm in detecting arrhythmias is over 95%. Finally, with an android application and through the TCP/IP protocol, the health or arrhythmia of the heartbeat will be informed on the doctor's or one of the patient's relative's cell phone, and its real-time display will be provided. Also, the possibility of sending a command from a mobile to the broker has been provided.

title: Sensor-Infused Emperor Penguin Optimized Deep Maxout Network for Paralyzed Person Monitoring
venue: IEEE Sensors Journal
abstract: Paralyzed people must maintain proper posture to prevent respiratory problems, pressure sores, and muscular contractures. A paralyzed person may slip out of their wheelchair several times as a result of poor sitting position. To overcome these challenges, a novel Emperor Penguin optimized sensor-Infused wheelChair (EPIC) framework has been proposed to constantly monitor the real-time posture of the paralyzed person’s health state. The proposed model aims to monitor wheelchair posture and health in real time, which can automatically detect posture issues, providing timely alerts and feedback to the user via a mobile application. The proposed framework utilizes the emperor penguin optimizer (EPO) algorithm for feature selection to improve the accuracy of posture detection. A deep maxout network (DMN) analyzes the features to predict the posture of the wheelchair user patient. The proposed EPIC framework has been assessed using a Python simulator. The effectiveness of the proposed EPIC framework has been determined using evaluation metrics, such as precision, specificity, accuracy, and sensitivity. The proposed EPIC technique advances the overall accuracy by 10.1%, 7.73%, and 2.84% better than posture recognition, graphic user interface (GUI), and independent component analysis-kantorovich distance (ICA-KD), respectively.

title: Sensorless Control of Low Inductance Coreless AFPM Machines for Fault-tolerant Operation of Propulsion Systems
venue: 2024 IEEE Transportation Electrification Conference and Expo (ITEC)
abstract: In motor-drive systems utilized in safety-critical applications and demanding conditions like electric aircraft propulsion systems, the reliability of the system is greatly affected by position sensors, given their susceptibility within the motor-drive system. Consequently, there is a need to eliminate sensors in vector-controlled motor drives to decrease overall hardware complexity and expenses, bolster the mechanical durability and dependability of the drive system. In this paper, a fault-tolerant sensorless control system for low inductance coreless axial flux PM (AFPM) machines, integrated into electric aircraft propulsion systems, is introduced. The proposed control system spans a wide operating range, from zero to ultra-high speed, all without the need for a position sensor, enhancing fault tolerance. The system is capable of accelerating the motor from standstill to a certain speed where fundamental signals become available for a flux observer. This observer estimates the rotor position and speed, which are then fed into a field-oriented control scheme. The effectiveness of the introduced control scheme was experimentally verified using a prototype coreless AFPM machine with a PCB stator as a case study.

title: Sentiment Analysis for Twitter Tweets: A Framework to Detect Sentiment Using Naïve Bayes Algorithm
venue: 2022 4th International Conference on Computer Communication and the Internet (ICCCI)
abstract: In today’s society, people communicate through social media. Digital life has expanded dramatically. Twitter is a social media platform where users can post tweets. The researchers used sentiment analysis, a popular research topic in recent years. Correctly identifying sentiments is critical since it opens up a world of possibilities. The researchers used the Twitter API and the tweepy python module to extract real-time tweets from Twitter. To imprive the rigor of this study, we used a Kaggle dataset to create a model that using Naïve Bayes Algorithm to recognize sentiments better. The researchers also compared different algorithms to identify the best algorithm for the data. In addition, the researchers collected and obtained information from credible sources to assess the trained model’s correctness and reliability. The analysis of the result highlights the implication of our studies.

title: Sentiment Analysis on Amazon Alexa Reviews Using NLP & Classification
venue: 2022 4th International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication Control and Networking (ICAC3N)
abstract: many firms and manufacturers, knowledge on public opinion is critical. They frequently want to know what consumers and the general public think of their products and services in real time. However, personally reading every post on the website and extracting important viewpoint information is not feasible. The frequency of data is very high to do it manually. Sentiment analysis enables for efficient and cost-effective data processing on a wide scale. We investigated the application of sentiment analysis in business to better understand its strengths and limits in order to learn more about it. Using Python and Machine Learning Algorithms, this project created a representation to forecast the response of a remark given the observation declaration using a dataset of Amazon Alexa reviews.

title: Sentiment Analysis on Indian Government Schemes Using Twitter data
venue: 2019 International Conference on Data Science and Communication (IconDSC)
abstract: People use social media for entertainment, fetching information, news, business, communication and many more. Few of such social media applications are Facebook, Twitter, WhatsApp, Snapchat and so on. Twitter is one among the micro blogging websites. We are using Twitter mainly because it has gained a lot of media attention. The text written is referred to as tweets, where a common man can tweet or can write their hearts out. We would be fetching the direct responses from the public and hence the data is more real-time. First step is to fetch the tweets on a particular scheme using python language code followed by the cleaning process then comes the creation of bag of words. Later these bags of words are given as an input to the algorithms. Finally, after training the algorithms, we will be getting the sentiment of the public on that scheme.

title: Sentinela-OT: A Frugal Passive System for Network Visibility and Unauthorized Access Detection in PLC-Based Industrial Control Systems
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The increasing convergence of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) has exposed industrial control systems (ICS) to cyber threats traditionally confined to enterprise networks. While continuous network monitoring is recommended by standards such as IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) lack the financial and technical resources required to deploy commercial OT security platforms. This paper presents Sentinela-OT, a frugal, and passive system designed to provide network visibility and unauthorized-access detection in PLC-based industrial environments. The proposed architecture combines open-source software (Suricata and Python) with low-cost embedded hardware (Raspberry Pi 5) and managed-switch port mirroring to monitor OT traffic out of band, ensuring zero interference with control operations. Detection is based on whitelist-driven identification of authorized communication endpoints, leveraging the deterministic and static nature of industrial networks to identify unapproved devices attempting to access PLCs. Real-time alerts are delivered through a lightweight Telegram-based notification interface, enhancing operator situational awareness without requiring complex dashboards or centralized infrastructure. The system was validated in a physical laboratory environment using real PLCs and industrial protocols (Modbus/TCP and Profinet). Experimental results demonstrate reliable detection of unauthorized access attempts, sub-second alert latency, and stable resource utilization on embedded hardware, with no observable impact on PLC communication performance. Sentinela-OT demonstrates that meaningful OT network visibility and access monitoring can be achieved using affordable, reproducible components, making it suitable for SMEs and resource-constrained industrial settings as a complementary layer to existing cybersecurity frameworks.

title: Sequence-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive L1 Cache Replacement
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computing Theory and Wireless Communications (ICCTWC)
abstract: Cache misses makes the pipeline to pause and push the system to extract data from main memory, which usually takes a lot of time. This results in processors slowing down. When workloads are constant and expected, traditional caching methods like LRU (Least Recently Used) and LFU (Least Frequently Used) work neat. Nevertheless, they many times find it difficult to get adjusted to dynamic or mixed memory access patterns where data usage changes with time. In order to represent access patterns, this paper investigates a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) method for L1 cache replacement that uses only three basic features: stride, frequency, and recency. To make eviction decisions in real time, a custom Python simulator incorporates a tabular Q-learning agent. We evaluate this RL policy on a range of synthetic workloads, such as strided, sequential, and random-locality traces, and compare it with LRU, LFU, Random, and the optimal Belady policy. According to the results, the RL approach maintains a small, implementable design while improving cache hit rates by up to 5 % over LRU in mixed workloads. These results imply that even simple RL models can offer significant flexibility with little overhead, despite their preliminary nature.

title: Sequential Anomaly Detection using Inverse Reinforcement Learning
venue: Proceedings of the 25th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining
abstract: One of the most interesting application scenarios in anomaly detection is when sequential data are targeted. For example, in a safety-critical environment, it is crucial to have an automatic detection system to screen the streaming data gathered by monitoring sensors and to report abnormal observations if detected in real-time. Oftentimes, stakes are much higher when these potential anomalies are intentional or goal-oriented. We propose an end-to-end framework for sequential anomaly detection using inverse reinforcement learning (IRL), whose objective is to determine the decision-making agent's underlying function which triggers his/her behavior. The proposed method takes the sequence of actions of a target agent (and possibly other meta information) as input. The agent's normal behavior is then understood by the reward function which is inferred via IRL.We use a neural network to represent a reward function. Using a learned reward function, we evaluate whether a new observation from the target agent follows a normal pattern. In order to construct a reliable anomaly detection method and take into consideration the confidence of the predicted anomaly score, we adopt a Bayesian approach for IRL. The empirical study on publicly available real-world data shows that our proposed method is effective in identifying anomalies.

title: Server-Side Decryption of Secure Shell Traffic
venue: 2026 30th International Conference on Information Technology (IT)
abstract: The Secure Shell (SSH) protocol is a cornerstone of network security, providing confidentiality and integrity for remote administration and data transfer. While its encryption is critical for protecting data in transit, it creates an opaque environment for real-time security monitoring and forensic analysis. This paper introduces a novel methodology for the extraction of keys and the live decryption of SSH sessions by leveraging modern in-kernel observability technologies. Our approach utilizes the extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and its high-level tracing language, bpftrace, to perform noninvasive, dynamic instrumentation of a running OpenSSH server process. We demonstrate a technique that attaches a user-level probe to the kex derive keys function, a critical stage in the SSH key exchange protocol where session keys are generated and stored in memory. By reading process memory at precise offsets, we successfully extract the encryption keys for both client-to-server and server-to-client data flows. These intercepted keys are then passed to a Python application which uses the PyShark library to capture the corresponding encrypted network packets and decrypt their payloads in real time. This work provides a practical framework for introspection into encrypted protocols, showcasing the power of eBPF as a tool for advanced security auditing and live forensics without altering the target applications source code or configuration.

title: Set Up a Local Video Streaming Server that Streams Video to Clients in a LAN
venue: 2025 9th International Conference on Computational System and Information Technology for Sustainable Solutions (CSITSS)
abstract: In this paper, we describe a video streaming system implemented in real-time using Python sockets and OpenCV, with an emphasis on measuring frame-level latency and performance analysis. The system captures video frames from a video camera at the sender, sends them over a TCP socket, then reconstructs and displays them at the receiver. During each frame's capture, reception, and display, timestamps are recorded to measure latency and frames per second (FPS). The results show the performance under local testing conditions, display latency trends, and point to real-time processing limitations.

title: Shadow Zone Analysis in Banda Sea Region Based on Profiling Float Data
venue: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The Banda Sea is an essential part of the Indonesian Archipelago Sea Lane (ALKI) III, which is strategic but still minimally explored. The crucial position of the Banda Sea in international shipping lanes and maritime defense operations requires a more in-depth oceanographic study related to underwater defense strategies. In this study, the Arvor I profiling float operated by BMKG provides real-time data with Iridium satellite communication to observe oceanographic parameters such as temperature, salinity, and depth. This study aims to analyze the shadow zone, which has essential implications for underwater acoustic operations, especially submarine navigation. The research methodology includes analysis of vertical temperature and salinity profiles to identify the thermocline layer. The speed of sound is calculated using the McKenzie equation by considering variations in temperature, salinity, and sea depth. Acoustic propagation simulations were performed using the spherical spreading model approach to map the distribution of the shadow zone. The analysis results indicate the presence of a thermocline at a depth range of 44.7 to 1016.4 meters, with a minimum point of sound speed at a depth of around 992 meters. Understanding the distribution of this shadow zone can significantly contribute to the optimization of underwater acoustic operations in the Banda Sea region, including in supporting submarine operations and other acoustic monitoring activities.

title: Shelf Optimization Technology
venue: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: This work introduces an advanced automated billing system for retail environments, leveraging Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to revolutionize the shopping experience. By integrating load cells, RFID modules, and Arduino microcontrollers, the system ensures a smooth and efficient checkout process. Load cells precisely measure product weight, RFID modules verify item authenticity, and Arduino boards handle data collection and processing. The system's functionality is enhanced through connectivity with Google Sheets via an ESP8266 module, enabling real-time updates on inventory and transactions. A user-friendly interface, designed using Flutter Flow, offers an engaging shopping experience for customers. This work exemplifies how IoT can transform retail operations, delivering a scalable, secure, and customer-focused solution.

title: Sign Language Translation
venue: 2020 6th International Conference on Advanced Computing and Communication Systems (ICACCS)
abstract: Sign language is the way of communication for hearing impaired people. There is a challenge for common people to communicate with deaf people which makes this system helpful in assisting them. This project aims at implementing computer vision which can take the sign from the users and convert them into text in real time. The proposed system contains four modules such as: image capturing, preprocessing classification and prediction. By using image processing the segmentation can be done. Sign gestures are captured and processed using OpenCV python library. The captured gesture is resized, converted to grey scale image and the noise is filtered to achieve prediction with high accuracy. The classification and predication are done using convolution neural network.

title: Sign Language Translation in WebRTC Application
venue: 2023 7th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)
abstract: Communication has been an essential part of human life. Different languages are present around the world for communication. Still, people who have lost their hearing and speaking ability by accidents and genetic birth often face difficulty in communication. Auditory-impaired people have found sign language helpful in communicating with others. Hearing-impaired people must always have a personal interpreter available for translations whenever they need to communicate. People with disability of hearing impairment find it challenging to interact with others on social media and the internet to form new relationships on their own. An open-source video-conferencing application that can translate sign language is quite helpful for the hearing impaired. Sign language recognition (SLR) has drawn a lot of attention as a way to close the enormous communication gap. However, sign language is far more complex and unpredictable when compared to other activities, making it challenging for reliable recognition. The Speech-to-Text API enables speech-impaired people who can read to comprehend others. The Sign Language Translation Application (SLTA) allows them to communicate by translating their sign language into text that others can understand. The proposed method uses python, the MediaPipe Framework for gesture data extraction, and the Deep Gesture Recognition (DGR) Model to identify the sign motion in real-time. The proposed method achieves the highest accuracy of 98.81% using a neural network comprised of Long-Short Term Memory units for sequence identification.

title: Sign Language Translation Using Image Processing to Audio Conversion
venue: 2024 Third International Conference on Intelligent Techniques in Control, Optimization and Signal Processing (INCOS)
abstract: Sign language has long been a fundamental mode of communication for deaf and mute individuals, serving as a crucial tool for inclusivity and interaction. Nonetheless, communication barriers persist as many individuals outside of these communities struggle to comprehend and utilize sign language effectively. A ground-breaking system known as hand gesture recognition using image processing to audio conversion has emerged to address this issue. This innovative system aims to develop an application capable of translating sign language and hand gestures into text and audio, thereby facilitating communication between deaf and mute individuals and the wider society. This system enables the detection and classification of hand gestures by employing computer vision techniques, such as CNN algorithms for image processing and the MediaPipe framework for hand gesture identification in real-time video streams. Subsequently, the system utilizes audio signals to provide immediate feedback by converting the detected gestures into corresponding sounds. The feature extraction CNN algorithm is implemented in Python, while the execution takes place on a Raspberry Pi connected to an external camera utilizing OpenCV libraries. Through this comprehensive approach, the system endeavours to bridge the communication gap and enhance the inclusion of deaf and mute individuals in various social settings.

title: Sign Language Translator for Deaf Communication
venue: 2026 International Conference on Sustainable Engineering and Digital Innovation (ICSEDI)
abstract: Signs of Hope is an interactive system aimed at enhancing communication between the deaf and hearing communities. The initiative provides two primary features. The first enables users to input English text, which is immediately translated into American Sign Language (ASL) through visual representations for each letter, or full-word signs when applicable. This functionality assists learners and those unfamiliar with sign language in grasping how to convey words using ASL hand gestures.The second feature permits users to perform hand signs in front of a camera, where the system analyzes the captured gesture against a pre-existing image database. Upon finding a match, the corresponding letter is presented as text on the screen. This facilitates clearer communication of messages for deaf individuals to those who do not comprehend sign language.The system is developed using Python, featuring a straightforward and user-friendly interface that shows sign images in real-time.It fosters accessibility and inclusion by providing a visual connection between sign language and written English. Signs of Hope prove particularly beneficial in educational environments, customer service, and everyday interactions, rendering them a significant resource for both learning and assistance. The overarching aim is to promote awareness and cultivate more inclusive communication for everyone.

title: Sign Speak Communicator for Deaf and Dumb People
venue: 2024 5th International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)
abstract: Communication challenges for deaf-mute individuals can be significant, especially in everyday interactions where verbal communication is the norm. Globally, approximately 466 million people, including 34 million children, are affected. Interactions between deaf and hearing individuals are notably more challenging compared to those between blind and sighted individuals. Sign language, a gestural form of communication prevalent among deaf communities worldwide, serves as a vital bridge. This paper is aimed at enhancing communication accessibility between deaf and hearing individuals. This project entails the development of a comprehensive system capable of converting sign language gestures into both audio and text formats. By leveraging advanced machine learning and computer vision techniques, the system accurately interprets sign language gestures in real-time, enabling seamless communication for deaf individuals. Additionally, the Sign Speak Converter offers the functionality to convert spoken language into text, facilitating comprehension for deaf individuals through visual representation of auditory content. This dual operation of the system addresses the communication barriers faced by both deaf and hearing individuals, fostering inclusivity and understanding in diverse social interactions. The Sign Speak Converter project represents a significant advancement in assistive technology, empowering individuals with hearing impairments to engage more effectively with the broader community while also enabling hearing individuals to better comprehend and communicate using sign language. Through its innovative approach and practical utility, this project contributes to the promotion of inclusive communication environments and the advancement of accessibility initiatives in society.

title: SignVision: An AI-Powered Educational Video Generation for Deaf and Dumb Learners
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computing, Communication, Security and Intelligent Systems (IC3SIS)
abstract: SignVision was developed to support students who do not have easy access to sign language interpreters. Existing tools only provide pre-recorded content and cannot respond to questions or adapt to a student’s learning needs. This make it difficult for learners to fully understand and engage with the material. The videos captured on webcams goes through MediaPipe Holistic (Python 3.10, MediaPipe 0.10.3) to extract 3D skeletal and hand-joint coordinates. These are assembled into 20-frame windows and classified by a Bidirectional LSTM trained on ASL Citizen keypoints. The recognized sign is paired with a plain-language explanation and demonstrated back to the user via a 3D avatar with captions. End-to-end inference runs at 22 to 27 ms per window on an Intel Core i5 with no GPU, which was fast enough for comfortable real-time use in our testing.

title: Silent television: S_TV
venue: 2016 23rd Portuguese Meeting on Computer Graphics and Interaction (EPCGI)
abstract: This paper presents a solution that allows the users of a certain place to hear the sound of a TV, even if they are in a noisy environment. This gives the users a more efficient way to hear the sound of televisions in places where the volume of noise is high. The solution, named "s_TV" comprises two modules: the transmitter and the receiver. The transmitter module is composed by equipment to capture and transmit sound from the TV to smartphones/tablets Android. This equipment is connected to the TV and a router and transmits the sound through a network to Android devices. It can also transmit other types of information, such as the TV settings. An application was also developed to allow the configuration and handling of the servers that emit the sound of televisions. The receiver module resulted in a mobile application that allows the user to choose in a very simple and intuitive way, a particular TV channel and, subsequently, receive and play the sound on the mobile device, in real time. In addition, other features are available such as recording the sound played and sharing it on social networks. The tests conducted indicate that the solution may also be used in real-world scenarios with a scalable number of users, without compromising the services available on existing Wi-Fi networks.

title: SimIC: Designing a New Inter-cloud Simulation Platform for Integrating Large-Scale Resource Management
venue: 2013 IEEE 27th International Conference on Advanced Information Networking and Applications (AINA)
abstract: 'Simulating the Inter-Cloud' (SimIC) is a discrete event simulation toolkit based on the process oriented simulation package of SimJava. The SimIC aims of replicating an inter-cloud facility wherein multiple clouds collaborate with each other for distributing service requests with regards to the desired simulation setup. The package encompasses the fundamental entities of the inter-cloud meta-scheduling algorithm such as users, meta-brokers, local-brokers, datacenters, hosts, hyper visors and virtual machines (VMs). Additionally, resource discovery and scheduling policies together with VMs allocation, re-scheduling and VM migration strategies are included as well. Using the SimIC a modeler can design a fully dynamic inter-cloud setting wherein collaboration is founded on meta-scheduling inspired characteristics of distributed resource managers that exchange user requirements as driven events in real-time simulations. The SimIC aims of achieving interoperability, flexibility and service elasticity while at the same time introducing the notion of heterogeneity of multiple clouds' configurations. In addition it accepts an optimization of a variety of selected performance criteria for a diversity of entities. The crucial factor of dynamics consideration has implemented by allowing reactive orchestration based on current workload of already executed heterogeneous user specifications. These are in the form of text files that the modeler can load in the toolkit and occurs in real-time at different simulation intervals. Finally, a unique request is scheduled for execution to an internal cloud datacenter host VM that is capable of performing the service contract. This is formally designed in Service Level Agreements (SLAs) based upon user profiling.

title: Simple Multiplexing Headers for the JRMP Stream Subprotocol
venue: IEEE Latin America Transactions
abstract: This article deals with a simple optimization for a level-5 protocol called JRMP (Java's Remote Method Protocol), which is used in a distribution model named Java's RMI (Java's Remote Method Invocation). The main JRMP subprotocol, namely Stream, has been enhanced with a simple and direct multiplexing mechanism that offers the possibility of transferring several parallel request-response interactions without opening new TCP/IP connections. The overhead required to process headers and the advantages stemmed from the approach in terms of response-time are explored on a switched-ethernet benchmark application.

title: Simple Way for Base Station Monitoring. Part 1. Software Emulation
venue: 2025 Wave Electronics and its Application in Information and Telecommunication Systems (WECONF)
abstract: This paper presents a method for monitoring base stations in the Open Radio Access Network architecture using a Near-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller-based application. The development focuses on collecting and visualizing key radio network performance metrics, such as data transmission latency, throughput, and resource block availability. The application implementation is written in Python. The emulation was conducted on a virtual testbed comprising simulated user equipment, simulated base stations, an open-source 5G core network, and an O-RAN Software Community Near-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller. The work demonstrates the potential of using open technologies to create flexible and scalable monitoring systems in 5G networks.

title: Simulating Magnetized Plasma using an Accelerated Finite Element-Boundary Integral Code
venue: 2023 XXXVth General Assembly and Scientific Symposium of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI GASS)
abstract: This paper describes an accelerated finite element-boundary integral code with support for complex media. The code is implemented in Python using several open source packages, and uses Numba just-in-time compilation for improved performance. To accelerate the boundary integral part of the code, a multilevel implementation of the adaptive cross approximation is used. As a numerical example, scattering against a magnetized plasma is demonstrated. For this example, compression of boundary integral matrices is achieved to 9 % of the memory required for full matrices.

title: Simulation and Application of Simpson's Rule on ESP32 for Differential Protection of Renewable-Integrated Transmission Lines
venue: 2025 16th IEEE International Conference on Industry Applications (INDUSCON)
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis between Simpson's Rule and the Trapezoidal Rule for numerical integration applied to the differential protection of transmission lines integrated with renewable energy sources. With the increasing penetration of solar and wind power, traditional protection systems are facing challenges related to frequency deviations, harmonic distortions, and electrical noise. A simulation framework developed in Python was used to model the differential current signals, including artificial pulses and Gaussian noise to emulate real-world disturbances. Integrals were calculated using both methods and compared against a predefined protection threshold. The results show that Simpson's rule achieves superior numerical accuracy and robustness, effectively distinguishing internal faults from noncritical anomalies and reducing false positives. In contrast, the Trapezoidal Rule showed a higher sensitivity, triggering incorrect trips in borderline cases. To validate the proposed approach in a real-time embedded context, Simpson's rule algorithm was implemented on an ESP32 microcontroller. The experimental results confirmed consistency with the simulations, demonstrating the feasibility of using Simpson's rule for realtime protection in smart grids with high renewable energy penetration.

title: Simulation Design of Continuous Linear Multiple Intersection Intelligent Traffic Light
venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Machine Learning and Machine Intelligence
abstract: At urban intersections, traffic congestion often occurs. Currently, most of the traffic signal lights in China adopt fixed timing schemes, lacking intelligence, which leads to severe traffic congestion in cities. This study focuses on continuous linear multiple intersections, taking into account the characteristics of road network structure and traffic flow. Based on the correlation between intersections, multiple intersections located on the same straight road are connected together. Using a collaborative simulation method based on Python and Vissim, real-time control of each intersection is conducted to reduce the average queueing time, average number of stops, and the average time required to pass through all intersections. This aims to improve the traffic capacity of the road network and alleviate urban road congestion.

title: Simulation of a Railway Control System: Dynamic Analysis of Scoped Memory Consumption
venue: 2011 UkSim 13th International Conference on Computer Modelling and Simulation
abstract: Scoped memory management in RTSJ (Real-time Specification for Java) achieves a level of predictability not found in applications that use garbage collection techniques. However, using scopes in the development process is a difficult task. Deciding on the appropriate number of scopes and which objects or threads should be allocated into them require assisting tools. This paper presents a simulation of railway control system executed in RTS2.2 virtual machine. Different scoped memory design models can be implemented in this simulation to measure the memory consumption for each overtime. Data obtained by the simulation when different scoped memory models implemented showed that the developer can compare and choose the most appropriate scoped memory design model that achieves the least memory footprint.

title: Simulation of planar I/F networks with delayed connections
venue: IJCNN'01. International Joint Conference on Neural Networks. Proceedings (Cat. No.01CH37222)
abstract: Studies the synchronization characteristics of a locally connected, planar network of (leaky) integrate-and-fire (I/F) neurons after Hopfield and Hertz (1995). Simulations were conducted using both the Java programming language and the MatLab prototyping language in order to detect implementation errors. Further, two different algorithms were used in the simulations. The first method was a standard numerical simulation using Runge Kutta methods. The second method was an event-driven algorithm generalized from Campbell et el. (1999). Both algorithms yield the same results. Visualizations were included to make qualitative behaviors visually apparent. We replicated the original Hopfield et al. simulation results in which periodic synchronous firing emerged. The Java software displays the activation level of each unit in the planar grid in real time. The software also displays the number of units firing per time step. Since the software runs in real time, the user can observe a movie of the network evolution simply by running the simulation. The main result obtained is that when small delays are introduced, synchronized firing takes the form of a traveling wave across the grid. When axon transmission was instantaneous, it was possible to achieve complete synchrony, but when small delays were introduced the largest amount of synchrony possible as less than 10 percent. With larger delays, the synchrony disappears entirely.

title: Simulation Study on Environmental Temperature of Civil Aircraft EE Compartment in Complex Scenarios
venue: 2024 10th Asia Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Aerospace Engineering (MEAE)
abstract: The electronic equipment of civil aircraft is centrally installed in the Electronic Equipment (EE) compartment, and providing a suitable EE compartment environment temperature is crucial to ensure the normal operation of electronic equipment. Analyzing and evaluating the environmental temperature of the EE compartment not only requires considering the thermal load of electronic devices, the air cooling performance of the aircraft, and the thermal properties of the aircraft structure, but also is related to various complex operating scenarios such as flight altitude, climate, air source, and air conditioning system status. This paper innovatively proposes a complex and multiple scenario EE bay environmental temperature simulation model based on the air flow and dynamic thermal balance, and verifies the accuracy of the model is compliant with the test result. The model was used to analyze the environmental temperature and electronic equipment adaptability of the EE bay of a certain civil aircraft, and through the analysis result the temperature is validated to comply with the requirement. This article provides a reliable analysis and verification method for the design of ventilation systems for electronic equipment in civil aircraft, which is of great significance for guiding the design and safe operation of civil aircraft.

title: Simulation-Based Energy Optimization Using Rule-Based Occupancy and Environmental Control
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Energy consumption in modern buildings keeps increasing because of the inefficient operation of lighting, heating, and cooling systems that are unable to adapt to real-time occupancy and environmental variations. Traditional automation systems are inflexible and very often result in wasted energy by acting according to static time schedules. To alleviate this issue, a rule-based control simulation will be developed that can optimize energy consumption while maintaining occupant comfort and indoor air quality. This proposed framework will integrate temperature, humidity, light, CO2 concentration, and occupancy to actuate lighting, ventilation, and HVAC operations through a set of predefined deterministic if-then rules. This simulation is implemented in Python using Pandas and Matplotlib on the Kaggle Room Occupancy dataset. It includes comfort models based on PMV/PPD and computation of energy-cost. Experimen- tal analysis reveals a reduction in energy consumption by 40.41% with respect to the fixed baseline schedule and maintains safe levels of CO2 for approximately 77.7% of the operating period. In any case, the results prove that the proposed approach is a lightweight, explainable, and reproducible framework.

title: Simulation-Optimization of Digital Twin
venue: 2021 Winter Simulation Conference (WSC)
abstract: With rapid advancements in Cyber-Physical manufacturing, the Internet of Things, Simulation software, and Machine Learning algorithms, the applicability of Industry 4.0 is gaining momentum. The demand for real-time decision-making in the manufacturing industry has given significant attention to the field of Digital Twin (DT). The whole idea revolves around creating a digital counterpart of the physical system based on enterprise data to exploit the effects of numerous parameters and make informed decisions. Based on that, this paper proposes a simulation-optimization framework for the DT model of a Beverage Manufacturing Plant. A data-driven simulation model developed in Simio is integrated with Python to perform Multi-Objective optimization. The framework explores optimal solutions by simulating multiple scenarios by altering the availability of operators and dispatching/scheduling rules. The results show that simulation optimization can be integrated into the Digital-Twin models as part of real-time production planning and scheduling.

title: Simulators, Emulators, and Test-beds for Internet of Things: A Comparison
venue: 2019 Third International conference on I-SMAC (IoT in Social, Mobile, Analytics and Cloud) (I-SMAC)
abstract: In the last few years, the world has seen extensive growth in the field of IoT in both research & deployment and adoption of the Internet of Things (IoT). The number of IoT devices is increasing multi-fold each year. So, the state of IoT is under rigorous research & deployment by several researchers across the globe to develop new algorithms, techniques, and protocols to secure IoT networks further. In this paper, we compare sixteen simulators (IOTSim, IoTIFY, Bevywise-IoT, etc), four emulators (Cooja, NetSim, MAMMotH, NCTUns 6.0), and six test-beds (MBTAAS, FIT IoT-LAB, etc) for IoT on the basis of Scope, Type, Programming language, IoT layers, Scale of Operation, IoT Standards, API Integration, Cyber Resilience, Service Domain, and Security Measures. Its comparison helps for modeling techniques, proper simulation, and testing for algorithm validation/proof-of-concept implementation in IoT. This comparison will help to support researchers and developers for choosing suitable tools for their application. We have also discussed Vertical & Horizontal Analysis of existing Simulators, Emulators, and Test-beds. This will help in testing the research ideas before moving towards live implementation.

title: SIS-IDAI System in the Performance of Vehicle Counting in Different Road Scenarios in the City of Huancayo
venue: 2024 IEEE 14th Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference (CCWC)
abstract: The study of vehicle counting is of importance, since it directly affects the analysis of vehicular traffic for the development of efficient road infrastructures for users and at the same time for the control of vehicular traffic. This work presents the proposal of an automatic counter system based on videos, for which we used the Python programming language and libraries such as OpenCV for system programming, whose techniques consisted of registration, detection and finally the counting of vehicles. In the experimentation, we collected and processed data in different scenarios in the main roads of Huancayo, in order to evaluate the counting framework. Therefore, the proposed vehicle counting system is able to count efficiently at 95% in scenarios suitable for its application.

title: Sista: Saving Optimized Code in Snapshots for Fast Start-Up
venue: Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Managed Languages and Runtimes
abstract: Modern virtual machines for object-oriented languages such as Java HotSpot, Javascript V8 or Python PyPy reach high performance through just-in-time compilation techniques, involving on-the-fly optimization and deoptimization of the executed code. These techniques require a warm-up time for the virtual machine to collect information about the code it executes to be able to generate highly optimized code. This warm-up time required before reaching peak performance can be considerable and problematic. In this paper, we propose an approach, Sista (Speculative Inlining SmallTalk Architecture) to persist optimized code in a platform-independent representation as part of a snapshot. After explaining the overall approach, we show on a large set of benchmarks that the Sista virtual machine can reach peak performance almost immediately after start-up when using a snapshot where optimized code was persisted.

title: Sistema Integral para la Gestión de la Diabetes: DCMS
venue: 2025 IEEE Colombian Conference on Communications and Computing (COLCOM)
abstract: Este trabajo describe el diseño y desarrollo del Diabetes Control and Monitoring System (DCMS), un sistema integral enfocado en mejorar la gestión de la diabetes mediante herramientas tecnológicas avanzadas. El sistema combina dispositivos portátiles, como el smartwatch E500, con software basado en Python, bases de datos en tiempo real y aplicaciones móviles para ofrecer monitoreo continuo, alertas automáticas y recomendaciones personalizadas. Este enfoque holístico busca optimizar el manejo de la enfermedad y facilitar el apoyo familiar.This paper describes the design and development of the Diabetes Control and Monitoring System (DCMS), a comprehensive system focused on improving diabetes management through advanced technological tools. The system combines wearable devices, such as the E500 smartwatch, with Python-based software, real-time databases, and mobile apps to provide continuous monitoring, automated alerts, and personalized recommendations.

title: SKE: emulation of on-board computer environments in operational simulators
venue: 2025 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: SKE is a software application for general-purpose Linux host servers that allows to emulate the partitioned environment designed for computers on-board satellites running mixed-criticality systems that require time and space partitioning and fault detection and isolation. The benefits of using SKE are manyfold, from helping to develop in Linux environments the mentioned systems that will run on top of the XtratuM/NG (XNG) hypervisor, up to be exploited by operational simulators to run on-board computers faster than real time. In this latter context, this paper shows how SKE is being integrated in the CNES’s KOSMOS framework to provide the on-board computer environment inside a full numerical simulator of a swarm of satellites. SKE is aimed to provide the expected functionality of the XNG hypervisor, offering faster-than-real-time performances when executing the flight software and still keeping a good level of representativity in terms of functional behaviour.

title: Sky Scout Modern Weather Software with Air Quality Information and Voice Interaction
venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Advancing Sustainable Solutions through Technologies (ICASST)
abstract: Sky Scout is a state of the art weather software intended to give users real time weather forecasts and air quality information, with a clean desktop interface. It was developed using Python and CustomTkinter. This software uses the OpenWeatherMap APIs to provide live data on weather and air quality. The user interface presents this data in an easy to use and attractive design. The Sky Scout software provides unique opportunities for using a 7 day weather forecast, live Air Quality Index, and a hands free city search using voice. The design of the application was created in a responsive manner and optimized with creative and dynamic backgrounds and hover tooltips to make the program easier to use. This research section will cover the program architecture, workflow development, and data presentation for streaming data in order to visualize data that would be of interest to users in some manner; namely, live, accurate, relevant, useful, and actionable environmental information. User surveys indicated that prior to seeing and using the interface that all users were very supportive of the long term use of the Sky Scout interface, the clarity of information presented, and the ease of interaction. Sky Scout could be a viable idea that is useful for the user interacting with Sky Scout to gain a better understanding of the environment in which they live for the day or the long term environment quality.

title: Sky vote: elevating elections to the cloud
venue: 2026 IEEE 1st International Conference on Intelligent Technologies for a Sustainable and Inclusive Future (ICITSIF)
abstract: With increasing requirements for secure, transparent, and scalable voting mechanisms, cloud-based voting solutions have become the necessity of the day in contemporary elections. Sky Vote offers a state-of-the-art cloud-based voting system to guarantee security, accuracy, and real-time vote tracking. Built on Amazon Web Services (AWS), the system utilizes multiple cloud-based technologies to guarantee voter authentication, secure data storage, and easy vote management. Sky Vote utilizes Amazon Cognito to perform secure user authentication and authorization, keeping qualified voters out of the system. Amazon RDS provides a secure database to keep voting data, including event information, vote totals, and voter information. The system effectively checks counted votes and tallies up results in real- time. Amazon API Gateway enables users to cast votes and view results from RDS through a secure and scalable API layer. For effective deployment and global reach, Amazon CloudFront provides speedy delivery of content. AWS Lambda, which is coded in Java, processes core functionalities, including submitting votes, data verification, and live calculation of results.

title: SLACC: Simion-based Language Agnostic Code Clones
venue: 2020 IEEE/ACM 42nd International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
abstract: Successful cross-language clone detection could enable researchers and developers to create robust language migration tools, facilitate learning additional programming languages once one is mastered, and promote reuse of code snippets over a broader codebase. However, identifying cross-language clones presents special challenges to the clone detection problem. A lack of common underlying representation between arbitrary languages means detecting clones requires one of the following solutions: 1) a static analysis framework replicated across each targeted language with annotations matching language features across all languages, or 2) a dynamic analysis framework that detects clones based on runtime behavior. In this work, we demonstrate the feasibility of the latter solution, a dynamic analysis approach called SLACC for cross-language clone detection. Like prior clone detection techniques, we use input/output behavior to match clones, though we overcome limitations of prior work by amplifying the number of inputs and covering more data types; and as a result, achieve better clusters than prior attempts. Since clusters are generated based on input/output behavior, SLACC supports cross-language clone detection. As an added challenge, we target a static typed language, Java, and a dynamic typed language, Python. Compared to HitoshiIO, a recent clone detection tool for Java, SLACC retrieves 6 times as many clusters and has higher precision (86.7% vs. 30.7%). This is the first work to perform clone detection for dynamic typed languages (precision = 87.3%) and the first to perform clone detection across languages that lack a common underlying representation (precision = 94.1%). It provides a first step towards the larger goal of scalable language migration tools.

title: SlideX: LLMs & Web Scraper in Slide Creation
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Communication Systems (ICKECS)
abstract: The increasing reliance on digital presentations across academic, corporate, and research domains has highlighted the inefficiencies of manual slide creation. This paper introduces an automated, full-stack AI-powered presentation generator that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with modern web technologies to automate end-to-end slide creation. Unlike conventional tools that only assist with design, this system performs keyword extraction using Groq LLM, retrieves factual content via Wikipedia API, applies multi-stage Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques for summarization, and generates slides automatically using python-pptx. The backend (Flask) manages AI processing, slide generation, and optional image retrieval via Pixabay, while the React-based frontend enables real-time editing, previewing, and downloading. The novelty of this system lies in its hybrid architecture, which merges AI-driven content understanding with automated slide structuring. Our experimental results demonstrate that AI-driven automation can significantly reduce human effort in presentation creation while maintaining professional quality.

title: SlimeUI: Exploring Non-Newtonian Fluid as a Deformable Interface for Digital Musical Expression
venue: Companion Publication of the 2026 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
abstract: SlimeUI explores slime, a non-Newtonian fluid, as a novel substrate for deformable digital musical instruments (DMIs). Prior materials for deformable DMIs often support only limited behaviors. For example, stretchable fabric interfaces can deform elastically but usually preserve fixed topology and cannot be sculpted or divided during performance. Clay can be shaped, separated, and manually rejoined, but it tends to retain imposed forms and does not naturally recombine into a continuous medium. Slime bridges these categories by flowing under slow manipulation, stiffening under rapid impact, and allowing topological changes such as separation and recombination within one material. Through a formative study of slime interaction, we observed associations between material behavior and musical control, including stretch for pitch and amplitude, sculpting for timbre, and separation or recombination for sound instantiation and chord formation. We implemented a computer vision system and prototypes that translate these mappings into real-time musical control.

title: Slope Considered Online Nonlinear Trajectory Planning with Differential Energy Model for Autonomous Driving
venue: 2025 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Mobility, Operations, Services and Technologies (MOST)
abstract: Achieving energy-efficient trajectory planning for autonomous driving remains a challenge due to the limitations of model-agnostic approaches. This study addresses this gap by introducing an online nonlinear programming trajectory optimization framework that integrates a differentiable energy model into autonomous systems. By leveraging traffic and slope profile predictions within a safety-critical framework, the proposed method enhances fuel efficiency for both sedans and diesel trucks by 3.71% and 7.15%, respectively, when compared to traditional model-agnostic quadratic programming techniques. These improvements translate to a potential $6.14 billion economic benefit for the U.S. trucking industry. This work bridges the gap between model-agnostic autonomous driving and model-aware ECO-driving, highlighting a practical pathway for integrating energy efficiency into real-time trajectory planning.

title: SlopsGuard: A Defense Tool Against AI-Hallucinated Package Attacks in Software Supply Chains
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
abstract: The proliferation of AI-assisted code generation tools has introduced a novel attack vector termed slopsquatting, where malicious actors register package names that Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently hallucinate. This demo paper presents SlopsGuard, designed to detect and prevent slopsquatting attacks in software supply chains. SlopsGuard implements a multi-layered detection pipeline integrating Levenshtein distancebased similarity analysis, Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) generation, and Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) vulnerability scanning. It combines project detection across multiple programming language ecosystems (Python, JavaScript, Java, Rust, Go, Ruby, PHP, C\#, Swift, Dart, Kotlin, and more) with cross-registry validation for all major platforms (PyPI, npm, Maven Central, crates.io, NuGet, Packagist, RubyGems). We demonstrate how SlopsGuard intercepts malicious dependencies before installation, providing actionable risk assessments with Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) compatible exit codes. The tool is available as both a command-line utility and containerized service for seamless integration into development workflows.

title: Smart Animal Monitoring System for Farms using YOLO and OpenCV
venue: 2025 International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
abstract: Animal detection in agricultural environments is a crucial component of modern farming practices, enabling farmers to monitor livestock, enhance security, and optimize resource management. This paper proposes a solution for animal detection in farm settings, leveraging the speed and accuracy of the You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection algorithm and the versatile computer vision capabilities of the Open-Source Computer Vision Library (OpenCV). Utilizing the YOLO algorithm, recognized for its real-time object detection capabilities, enables the identification and localization of animals in farm images or video frames. OpenCV complements this process by providing a robust framework for image processing, enabling tasks such as image preprocessing, feature extraction, and camera interfacing. Integrating YOLO and OpenCV aims to create an efficient and reliable system for realtime animal detection, offering farmers valuable insights into livestock activities and facilitating prompt decision-making. The proposed approach helps to enhance farm management applications, contributing to increased productivity and addressing challenges related to animal monitoring in agricultural areas. The proposed work has been implemented using a Python tool, and the results gained 98% accuracy.

title: Smart Assistive Communication Device using Heart Rate And Gesture Recognition For The Speech Impaired
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
abstract: Speech-impaired people usually have major problems with expressing their needs and emotions in everyday communication. The current means of communication, including sign language, camera-controlled gesture recognition and text-to-speech, need trained interpreters or controlled settings, and cannot be used in real-time. The paper will provide a smart assistance communication device designed on the gesture recognition principle, as a wearable glove that will be used by speech-impaired users. The suggested system will combine an accelerometer, touch keys and sound sensor to accurately identify hand position and gesture patterns. An Arduino Nano then interprets the data sensed and sends it wirelessly to a mobile app on Bluetooth. The software on the mobile device does the gesture recognition and translates the gesture recognized into text and speech in real time. The system will be made lightweight, portable and cheap with low energy consumption, which would ensure that it can be used in the daily routine. The experimental evaluation shows the high-quality gesture recognition with the lowest latency and better communication efficiency. The suggested solution will improve user autonomy, decrease dependency on interpreters, and offer an efficient assistive technology that will make the social interaction and quality of life of speech-impaired people better.

title: Smart Attendance and Emotion Monitoring System using Face Detection with CCTV Integration
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics (ICMCSI)
abstract: In this study, the authors offer a proposal of an AI-based system that is used to track and resolve the problem of student attendance and classroom attendance in schools. CCTV cameras are where students are captured by the cameras placed at the entrance of the school and at the inside of the classes; after the deepface and FaceNet model the images of the faces of the students are captured; these images are processed automatically by the FaceNet model and automatically identify the attendance. Entry-point captures make a success as compared to classroom captures in detecting proxy attendance and also indicate dropout of classes. Moreover, the system has a facial emotion recognition module that assesses the engagement level by evaluating the expression of attentive, confused, or bored expressions and therefore offers real-time feedback on the classroom dynamics to the teachers. Here, the attendance record and engagement metric visualization and alerts on an interactive dashboard are shown that allow appropriate involvement in time. Python, OpenCV, and SQLite/csv are the selected languages that are used to develop the proposed system.

title: Smart Attendance Management System Using Face Recognition
venue: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Managing attendance in educational institutions is often a time-consuming and error-prone task, with traditional methods like roll calls or sign-in sheets being inefficient and susceptible to proxy attendance. This paper presents a Smart Attendance Management System that leverages facial recognition technology to automate the attendance process. By using cameras to capture images of students, the system recognizes their faces and marks their attendance in real time. Developed in Python, the system employs the K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm for accurate face recognition. Once attendance is recorded, it is stored in a CSV file and can be visualized using the flask web application. The proposed system significantly reduces manual effort, ensures accuracy, and operates efficiently in real-time environments.

title: Smart Authentication Process for Human and Vehicles Using AI Techniques : An Approach for making better life in 21st Century Smart Cities
venue: 2022 4th International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication Control and Networking (ICAC3N)
abstract: The Entry detection system as the name suggests detects entry attempts. Till date entry to organizations like schools and colleges are provided by the guards that do not map entries and exits to the premises very efficiently which is a serious security concern and also it is not humanly possible to identify each student and stop outsiders who might be disguised from entering. Ours is a face detection and facial recognition system which detects faces from a live video feed recorded from a camera installed at the gates, recognizes the face using the data set of registered staff and students of the college and opens the gates to allow entry.It also maintains a record of entry and exits along with time in a database for security purposes. OpenCV is used for facial and vehicle no. plate detection which forwards to the dlib library that is used for deep metric learning and extracting facial embeddings and finally is face recognition library that displays the real time name of the person. This helps in authorized entry by correct identification along with a record of entry and exit times. The system meets the requirement as it forwards the result from the recognizer to the connected sensors and effectors for providing/restraining entry in required cases.

title: Smart Basket Automated Shopping Experience with IOT Technology
venue: 2025 10th International Conference on Information and Network Technologies (ICINT)
abstract: People often perceive grocery shopping as a tedious task, especially during peak hours, as traditional checkout systems struggle to keep up with demand, leading to extended wait times and customer dissatisfaction. The Smart Basket solution introduces an innovative shopping technology that utilizes IoT and RFID technology to create a seamless "Shop, Drop, Go" experience. Built on Event-Driven Architecture, it integrates RFID sensors, Python programming, and a Raspberry Pi microcontroller to optimize the shopping process. Real-time data processing through Raspberry Pi edge computing enables efficient local operations before synchronizing with retail servers. Python facilitates real-time product adjustments, instantly displaying updated cost data on an LCD interface upon RFID sensor detection. At checkout, the system generates a QR code containing transaction details, allowing for quick and error-free scanning. By automating transactions through RFID technology, the Smart Basket enhances operational efficiency, transaction accuracy, and customer satisfaction, ultimately driving greater business productivity.

title: Smart Cities Solutions for More Flood Resilient Communities
venue: 2019 Systems and Information Engineering Design Symposium (SIEDS)
abstract: There is evidence that flooding events are becoming more frequent and intense as a result of climate change. This problem is especially prevalent in Norfolk, VA which has the second highest rate of sea level rise on the east coast. Model and sensing innovations are needed to produce high-resolution flood warnings in real-time to improve public safety. New sensing approaches are also needed to accurately measure the extent of flooding during storm events so this data can be used to calibrate models. Our methodology creates an end-to-end modeling system for Norfolk, VA to provide real-time flood forecast information to users.
