Our process begins with data collection through our group's water level sensor. This device relies on an ultrasonic sensor to measure how its distance from the ground changes as water levels rise. Readings are then filtered before they are transmitted to a persistent database. The data from this sensor, combined with historical flood data, are stored in a locally-hosted relational SQLite database and a cloud-hosted InfluxDB database. The locally-hosted database can be used for further development of flood prediction models. The cloud-hosted database can store data as it is collected for real time analysis. Currently, the sensor has accurately recorded changes in distances of up to ten feet in the lab and successfully transmitted these readings. For future testing, measurements will be sent to a static URL hosted on Heroku. A Python function has been written that reads the URL in JSON format and transmits the data to the Influx database. Another Python function has been written that reads a csv containing historical data and transforms it to the proper format, then inserts it into SQLite.

title: Smart Control System with NodeMCU-Controlled Relays and MobileNet-SSD for Person Detection
venue: 2026 International Conference on Signal, Systems, and Computing for Next-Gen Automation (ICSSCNA)
abstract: The inception of intelligent context-aware systems has been made possible over the past decade by the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Internet of Things (IoT) devices. This study describes a real-time, vision-based human detection system to autonomously operate numerous electrical appliances utilizing AI and IoT hardware. The proposed system uses a laptop webcam to continuously record video data, which is then analyzed by OpenCV in Python using a pretrained Mobile-SSD deep learning model to identify human presence. Upon recognizing a person, the control commands were delivered via serial-communication to an ESP8266-based NodeMCU microcontroller integrated on a Kiwi-IoT V1 development board. This board connects with a 4-channel relay module that operates a 12V DC fan, serial lamp and a submersible pump. A 3-cell LiPo battery powers the system, and an L298 motor driver controls the power distribution. For smart environments such as homes, farms and industrial areas, this proposed integrated architecture provides a low-cost, portable solution by enabling smooth interaction between AI-based detection and physical control of electrical equipment. The experimental results demonstrate high reliability and responsiveness in real-time scenarios, making the system a promising model for intelligent automation using edge AI and Internet of Things convergence.

title: Smart Defect Detection and Sortation through Image Processing for Corn
venue: 2020 IEEE REGION 10 CONFERENCE (TENCON)
abstract: This research aims to develop smart defect detection and sortation for corn with the use of image processing. This project helps to speed up manual inspection to improve productivity and reduce the time consumed by farmers in sorting. The defect detection process is done through image processing using an open computer vision library and Python. The corn is manually placed in the roller conveyor, passing under a camera acquiring the real-time image. The sorting process eliminates the damaged corn from those that were in good condition. The system acquires real-time image data from a camera feed to a computer for analyzing purposes. Images were scanned as the corn ear was traveling through the conveyor. A program that effectively analyzes acquired corn images' required features was developed in Python using the Open Computer Vision (OCV) library. A conveyor that comes with a built-in corn sortation mechanism was controlled by Raspberry Pi that directs the corn to its desired group. On the evaluation of the accuracy of the system, a series of trials were conducted. The result of the evaluation yielded a 92% success rate in terms of defect detection and sortation. Revisions were made after the initial testing of the project. Problems and its causes were identified to improve the performance of the whole system.

title: Smart Detection of Defects in Railway Tracks Using Ultrasonic Sensor
venue: 2026 International Conference on Recent Advances in Electrical, Electronics, Ubiquitous Communication, and Computational Intelligence (RAEEUCCI)
abstract: Trains are an indispensable medium of transportation for people and goods, and their effective maintenance is therefore very important. One of the main reasons for train accidents is track faults or hidden cracks, which usually lead to derailments. Detection of such faults at an early stage can greatly mitigate the chances of accidents. Traditional manual techniques of inspection are time-consuming, manpower intensive, and have limited coverage, and therefore automated methods are imperative. This paper describes a lightweight, rail-guided testbed with ultrasonic sensors and motors for self-locomotion. The ultrasonic sensor measures the variations in distance between sensor and rail surface. Surface level anomalies such as dents, gaps, and visible cracks produce abrupt changes in the measured distance, that can be visualized as spikes in the real-time distancetime plots generated using Python. The prototype provides an efficient, cost-effective, and reliable means of crack detection, thus facilitating smarter rail maintenance and enhanced safety. Experimental evidence supports its ability to detect simulated cracks with accuracy. The proposed prototype is only designed to detect surface-level anomalies and discontinuities rather than subsurface fatigue cracks within the rail material.

title: Smart Diet Planner:An AI-Powered Web Application for Personalized Nutrition Management
venue: 2025 International Conference on Future Technologies (ICFT)
abstract: A healthy and balanced diet is needed to maintain fitness, prevent diseases, and generally keep the body fit and healthy, unlike most traditional diet planners who do not address specific needs, resulting in poor compliance. To fill this vacuity, we introduce the Smart Diet Planner, which is an AI-based web application that provides individualized, flexible, and objective nutrition management. It takes into account user preferences (vegetarian, vegan, or non-vegetarian), allergies, dislikes, health objectives (weight loss, maintenance or gain), and budget to create personalized meal plans. The proposed model, unlike traditional systems, provides an AI-based adaptive substitution mechanism to replace the disliked or allergenic foods with alternatives with a similar nutritional content and maintain balance. There are also other features such as calorie and nutrition tracking, water tracking, and a dashboard that shows the daily, weekly, and monthly trends in the diet visually. It is powered by Node.js, Firebase with real-time storage and authentication as well as Python-based AI/ML modules to deliver personalized recommendations. The experimental findings indicate that meal plans are generated with 98 percent accuracy and 85 percent adherence rate, which proves to be more personalized and satisfying. The Smart Diet Planner is a powerful solution combining the advantages of AI personalization, live adaptation, and full visualization to overcome the shortcomings of conventional diet planning software and promote healthy lifestyles.

title: Smart Energy Optimization in Electric Drives Using AI-Driven PWM Control
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abstract: As the global cognizance intensifies on strength conservation and wise automation, the call for smart electric drive structures has in no way been more. Electric vehicles, which can be at the coronary heart of modern machinery and electric powered cars, often suffer from electricity inefficiencies due to traditional Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) strategies that operate on constant parameters, irrespective of real-time load variations. This paper offers a singular technique to improving energy efficiency and performance by using integrating an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) primarily based controller into the PWM manipulate loop of an electric powered drive gadget. The proposed machine uses a feed forward neural community educated on numerous load situations to predict the most efficient PWM responsibility cycle dynamically. Input capabilities encompass actual-time present day, voltage, motor temperature, and former torque values. The ANN procedures those parameters to adaptively modify the PWM output, ensuring minimal power loss and smoother motor operation. Simulation research carried out in MATLAB/Simulink and Python exhibit that the ANN-controlled device considerably outperforms conventional PWM strategies in terms of power financial savings, responsiveness, and decreased switching losses.

title: Smart EV Charging Locator and Queue Management
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The fluctuating lineups and wait times at charging stations are one of the key issues facing exponential growth in electric vehicles. They seriously interfere with the user's convenience. The present work proposes a web-based platform that enables users to pre-book specific cable slots, assists EV drivers in searching for nearby charging stations, and predicts wait times using a machine learning model. The system retrieves station and cable port information by querying OpenChargeMap and partner APIs, utilizes browser geolocation to determine the position of the user, and showcases alternatives on a Google Maps interface. The backend, which is built using Node.js and a MySQL database, is utilized along with a separate Python-based machine learning module that generates forecasts of waiting time, using XGBoost and Scikit-learn. For each station, users can see the estimated wait time and the journey time. Moreover, they can see and book the available cable time slots. We compare four strategies: (1) naive nearest-station (based only on distance), (2) journey-time aware, (3) queue-aware, and (4) booking + wait + travel. Simulations across multiple test zones show that the combined strategy decreases the average total time- travel plus waiting- by 23 % and increases cable use. The paper contributes by presenting a waittime prediction model, a comparison of decisionmaking techniques, mapping, machine learning, and slot booking. It further discusses possible future improvements, such as dynamic pricing and IoT-based real-time updates.

title: Smart Fall Detection and Emergency Alert System for Human Safety Using OpenCV
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Electronics, Materials Engineering & Nano-Technology (IEMENTech)
abstract: This writing conveys the concept and actualization of a device that would forever watch people at the exact moment to realize a drop and send help without needing any human intervention. Such a system is designed to be very useful and mainly focused on elderly people and, generally, people who are prone to risks. Our method, unlike typical ones, employs a computer vision pipeline that uses Gaussian Mixture, Based Background Subtraction and contour analytics on live video to identify changes in posture ratios that reflect a fall. The most remarkable attribute of the present system is its two, mode location scheme; initially, it obtains the user's consent to get accurate GPS coordinates, and if the user refuses, the system uses IP, based geolocation. The coordinates fetched from the device are then sent to the reverse, geocoding server to get the exact address along with the link to the interactive Maps. The notification system is very robust in that it can send the information about the incident and the exact location to the people on the list of the ones to be informed through the custom, made email client simultaneously. The prototype, which is made using a Python stack that combines OpenCV and Flask, demonstrates the feasibility of an end, to, end autonomous surveillance, accurate identification, and context, aware alert system, thus it is a great source for the enhancement of safety regulations and the reduction of the critical incident response time.

title: Smart Goggles for the Visually Impaired
venue: 2024 International Conference on Power, Energy, Control and Transmission Systems (ICPECTS)
abstract: The goal of this project is to develop AI-powered smart glasses that will help people who are blind or visually impaired navigate and interact with their surroundings more successfully. The smart goggles combine cutting-edge natural language processing and computer vision technologies to offer text-to-speech conversion, face recognition, and real-time object detection. The glasses' built-in ultrasonic sensor determines how far away the subject must be from the object that will be the subject of the captured image in order to take a sharp picture. We have used Tinkercad, Proteus, and Python to simulate this.

title: Smart Harness Design for Blind and Impaired Visually People
venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Embedded & Distributed Systems (EDiS)
abstract: This work relates to an artificial vision embedded system intended to improve the autonomy of blind and visually impaired people by providing audio descriptions of texts and surrounding scenes. The proposed Smart Harness offers a new solution for guiding this category of society by introducing technologies that enable them to read text and detect obstacles in their environment. The system uses a Raspberry Pi with a camera to capture images, which are then processed by advanced technologies such as OpenCV to improve image quality, Tesseract OCR and eSpeak for text recognition, and TensorFlow for object detection. The extracted information and descriptions are converted to audio via eSpeak and transmitted to the user through a connected audio device. This system provides real-time audio descriptions, helping visually impaired people navigate their environment, thereby increasing their independence and quality of life.

title: Smart Health AI Assistant with Blood Network
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Communication Systems (ICKECS)
abstract: The Smart Health AI Assistant with Blood Network functions as a digital health platform which combines predictive health analytics with its capability to track blood donors in real time. The platform processes vital user data which consists of blood pressure measurements and glucose levels and heart rate data and pre-extracted vocal measurement parameters (MDVP features). The system uses supervised learning models which include Logistic Regression and Random Forest and SVM to identify potential health conditions through analysis of the obtained data. The system generates an AI-powered health evaluation together with a customized health management program which helps users deal with their new health challenges. The system includes an automated Blood Network which provides emergency situations with quick access to suitable blood donors for emergency needs. Users complete a personal profile when they register. The section contains demographic details which include blood type and age and current health status and lifestyle indicators and location. The system uses its geo-intelligent matching engine to find nearby donors who match with the required criteria during emergency situations. The system provides an efficient method to establish contact between donors and recipients. The system comprises AI inference pipelines together with automated report creation and database functions which utilize location data for their operations. The development team created the solution through Python and Flask and React and MongoDB which enables secure and scalable system operation while providing simple user access. The Smart Health AI Assistant with Blood Network transforms digital health into an integrated, data-driven, community-oriented health information system by effectively combining prevention-oriented health analytics with real-time emergency coordination.

title: Smart Hospital Robotic Process Automation (RPA) System Integrating Ranking Algorithms, Reinforcement Learning, and Fuzzy Logic for Optimal Task Allocation
venue: 2026 ICEENG International Conference for Innovations in Intelligent Computing and Cybersecurity (IICC)
abstract: The paper is a simulated and detailed system of the management of robots’ movement and task allocation in a smart hospital setting, known as Robotic Process Automation (RPA) of Smart Hospitals. The given system is designed based on three interrelated modules i) the Robot Finding Module (RFM), ii) the Recharge Control Module (RCM) and iii) the Route Selection Module (RSM). The main aim is to improve the efficiency of the operations by choosing the optimal robot to match a task of a patient, the optimal time to charge the robot, and the optimal and safe route to reach the destination. It is made possible with the help of a new combination of well-developed AI methods, such as a new Robot Ranking Algorithm (RRA), a Q-Learning dynamic matchmaking, and Fuzzy Logic intelligent battery management. The efficiency of the system is proved by the fact that a real-time simulation is used in Python. The graphical interface enables visualization of real-time behavior of robots, assignment of tasks, and control of battery condition, which allows tracking the system decisions and verifying them with ease.

title: Smart Laundry Reservation System for University Dormitories
venue: 2025 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a web-based application for digitalizing and optimizing the reservation of shared resources in university dormitories, focusing on laundry facilities. Traditional methods, typically relying on handwritten lists or informal agreements, are prone to overlapping bookings, unauthorized modifications, and lack of accountability. The proposed solution leverages the Django framework (Python) and a relational database to provide students with a responsive interface where they can view availability in real time, reserve machines through a weekly calendar, and manage their bookings. Dormitory administrators are provided with a dedicated control panel for managing dormitories, machines, schedules, and student accounts. Additional features include automated warnings, temporary user blocking, and the ability to disable machines while automatically canceling related reservations. A key novelty of the system is the integration of a priority-based reservation mechanism that ensures equitable access for students with urgent needs, combined with an automated misuse-prevention system. Security and authentication are enforced via institutional Google accounts using the OAuth 2.0 protocol, while the modular architecture of the application allows for scalability and future extensions to other dormitory services. By combining ease of use with robust backend logic, the platform enhances transparency, reduces conflicts, and contributes to the digitalization of campus life.

title: Smart Meter Consumption Pattern Analysis for Fraud Detection Using Decision Tree Learning
venue: 2026 International Conference on Multidisciplinary Innovations For Smart & Sustainable Future (MISSF)
abstract: Theft of energy is a significant issue worldwide. It not only strains distribution networks but also results in huge losses for power companies. For example, in India, developing countries, non-technical losses due to theft contribute to $20-30 \%$ of electricity distribution losses. Manual inspections and rule-based systems, which are the traditional theft detection methods, are slow, expensive, and ineffective against the new theft detection methods. With the integration of digitalized power systems and smart meters, new possibilities for applying machine learning to identify theft in real-time and with greater precision arise. In this work, a framework based on Decision Trees (DTs) to detect electricity theft using smart meters is discussed. Analysed data consists of 20,000 simulated meter readings with attributes: Voltage, Current, Power, Energy, Power Factor, Load Consumption, and Loss. Preprocessing stages included missing value treatment, normalization, and, again, feature extraction. A 70:30 split was used to create training and testing subsets. A Decision Tree Classifier, using the entropy criterion, was developed in Google Colab using the Scikit-learn and Pandas Python libraries. Exceptional results were achieved, with 99.96% accuracy along with almost flawless precision, recall, and F1-score. The confusion matrix only indicated two misclassifications during the test, which illustrates both the proposed method's effectiveness and the validation of the test. This framework surpasses comparable accuracy, interpretability, and computational efficiency in traditional approaches, as well as in the most advanced studies deployed in machine learning. For these reasons, it becomes extremely efficient and reasonably expected in contemporary smart grid implementations.

title: Smart Metering System
venue: 2021 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The paper demonstrates the wired and wireless mode of communication for transfer of data from smart meter to a server. The communication is a diverse topic and there are many techniques available nowadays which allow smooth data transfer between users or machines or among the combinations. This work carry outs the machine to machine communication system where electrical parameters of a network are interpreted by a smart meter which displays it on the LED display, along with that it transmits the data via RS485 port over Modbus protocol to the receiver. The data transfers from smart meter to computer/server through a serial converter or wi-fi converter. Additionally, in wireless mode, all devices should be connected in the same LAN network. The computer/server uses the ‘python’ programming language to collect the data from smart meter. The program interprets the data received classifies it into various parameters and stored into database.

title: Smart Microgrid Operation via Demand Dispatch Approach on Dimmable Dispatchable LEDs
venue: 2019 International Power System Conference (PSC)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to optimally operate the FUM microgrid to face minimum operation cost using a dedicated demand dispatch method on dimmable dispatchable lighting system of the microgrid. The FUM microgrid is practically implemented in PSRES laboratory of engineering faculty of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. Cost of electricity purchased from grid, life reduction of batteries, battery energy loss, users inconveniency rooted from dispatching lighting system and sensitivity of microgrid users to environment brightness are considered in the optimization problem. In the long-term study, solar generation and microgrid load are estimated and best energy sharing is obtained through an optimization problem. In short-term study, control procedure stabilizes microgrid energy flow during stochastic behavior of solar generation and load, while load can be dispatched within some constraints. Day-ahead and real time operation of the microgrid are attained using Python Software with the method of Sequential Least Squares Programming (SLSQP) and MATLAB software.

title: Smart Mirror Monitoring using Raspberry Pi
venue: 2023 4th International Conference on Electronics and Sustainable Communication Systems (ICESC)
abstract: Numerous smart devices that improve our daily lives have been developed as a result of the quick development of technology. One such innovation is the smart mirror, which blends digital capabilities with the functioning of a conventional mirror. The smart mirror monitoring system suggests in this project makes use of a Raspberry Pi, allowing for real-time monitoring and interaction with various data and apps. This project’s main goal is to create and put into use a smart mirror that can show a variety of data, including the time, weather updates, calendar events, news feeds, and social network notifications. A Raspberry Pi, a two-way mirror, a display screen, and different temperature sensors are the hardware necessities for this project. The central processing unit, or Raspberry Pi, is in charge of collecting data from sensors, locating pertinent information on the internet, and displaying it on the surface of the mirror. Python will be used to create the smart mirror software system, together with libraries for image processing and data visualization like Open-CV and API for obtaining outside data. Graphical user interface (GUI) frameworks will be used to develop the mirror’s user interface in order to make it simple and easy to use.

title: Smart Multi-Modal Animal Deterrent System
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovations in Emerging Technologies for Sustainable Development (ICIETSD)
abstract: Rodent infestations in cars and elephant intrusions in farming and forest areas lead to major economic losses, safety risks, and environmental issues. This article presents a new, IoT-enabled multi-modal detection and deterrent system aimed at protecting vehicles and defending territories. The system uses an ESP32-CAM for real-time image capture and a YOLOv8 deep learning model for smart object classification. For car security, the system identifies rodents and activates variable ultrasonic sounds and vibration deterrents. To tackle territorial intrusions, the setup is designed to detect elephants, triggering a specialized relaydriven inverter and coil that produce electromagnetic (EM) waves, forming a non-lethal repellent barrier. Experimental tests of the base system show high detection accuracy, quick response times, and effective deterrence while consuming low power. By integrating the Internet of Things (IoT) with Python-based automation, this dual-mode system provides a reliable, low-power solution for effective automotive pest control and wildlife deterrence.

title: Smart Notification and Automated Reboot System for Cloud-Hosted Bitbucket Server
venue: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Computing and Communication (ETCC)
abstract: The seamless integration of development and operations is fundamental to the principles of DevOps, which are essential for maintaining the functionality of Information Technology (IT) infrastructure in a rapidly evolving technological landscape. This work focuses on creating an automated monitoring system for a Bitbucket server hosted on an Amazon Web Services (AWS), Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) Linux instance. The system leverages tools such as Jenkins, AWS CloudWatch, and Simple Notification Service (SNS) to facilitate real-time monitoring and alerting. Through automation, the system will provide insights into the health of the IT infrastructure and promptly notify stakeholders in the event of any malfunctions.

title: Smart Object Detection Using ESP32-CAM Based on YOLO Algorithm
venue: 2024 Second International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
abstract: In the present research work, a system is developed that can detect objects in real-time using a combination of the ESP32 CAM module and Python programming. The goal was to show how affordable hardware and free software can be used to make a system that recognizes objects quickly and accurately. By using computer vision and machine learning tricks, the proposed system can figure out the different objects with great precision. The setup process involves putting some code onto the ESP32 CAM module, finding its IP address, and then making it work smoothly with Python. The proposed system was tested in different situations, like watching for things in surveillance, making tasks easier with automation, and helping out in assistive technologies.

title: Smart Object Recognition with Audio-Visual Feedback for Enhanced Accessibility Using ESP32
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
abstract: Vision loss presents substantial barriers to autonomy, employment, and routine activities. With over 2.2 billion individuals globally affected by some form of visual impairment, even basic tasks like navigation or reading become difficult. This study introduces a smart object recognition system tailored for visually impaired users, utilizing real-time image processing. The framework leverages Python with OpenCV for image analysis and an ESP32 microcontroller for system coordination. Auditory feedback is delivered via the DFPlayer Mini, while an OLED display provides on-screen visual cues. Upon detecting an object with the camera module, the system identifies it and communicates the result through synchronized voice and text outputs. Efficient integration between components is achieved through the ESP32, ensuring smooth operation. The system combines artificial intelligence and IoT to create a responsive, affordable, and portable assistive device, aiming to enhance independence and accessibility for users with visual challenges.

title: Smart Parking System
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Circuits, Power and Intelligent Systems (CCPIS)
abstract: Growing demands for effective parking management in the urban context demand intelligent solutions. The current paper describes an IoT, and machine learning-capable intelligent smart parking system intended to boost parking operations using automation and processing of real-time data. The system is configured in two modes: a convenient web platform for booking and payment and an IoT-integrated parking lot for smart vehicle monitoring and slot management. It uses sensors, a camera module, and Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for license plate detection, with Python-based algorithms for real-time validation. By facilitating automatic slot allocation, gate control, and dynamic fare calculation, the system enhances user convenience while avoiding urban issues like congestion and inefficiency.

title: Smart phone application development for monitoring epilepsy seizure detection based on EEG signal classification
venue: 2017 IEEE 8th Annual Ubiquitous Computing, Electronics and Mobile Communication Conference (UEMCON)
abstract: Automated epilepsy seizure detection is the solution to the limitation and time consuming of manual epilepsy monitoring and detection using EEG signals. In this paper we developed a technique for epilepsy seizure detection using EEG signals. The signal will be pre-processed and filtered using multiple filters. Then, the filtered signal will be decomposed into sub-bands. Furthermore, feature extraction is applied; we developed a combined feature consists of combining three features into one. Finally, we used well-known classifiers such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and K-Nears Neighbor (KNN) to differentiate between epileptic and non-epileptic signals, and we achieved an accuracy of 97%. Furthermore, we developed an Android-based smartphone application for monitoring epilepsy detection based on the classification results of the EEG signal. A notification will be sent to the patient, doctors, and family members when an epilepsy seizure occurs. Once the EEG signal is classified as epileptic, the App will display a visual notification indicating that Epileptic Seizure has been detected. Moreover, it will trigger an alarm and send a message notification to all associated phone numbers, and the EEG signal will display on the App. Although we are using an EEG signal from a dataset, we have generated both normal and epileptic EEG signals using a waveform generator, and we have displayed those signals on the spectrum analyzer for future real time detection using our Android App.

title: Smart Pillbox: Healthcare Assistance for Dementia Patients
venue: 2025 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Given that the world population of older persons is increasing dramatically, appropriate adherence to medication by people with dementia has emerged as a significant public-health dilemma. Neurocognitive impairment results in missed doses or double doses, adverse health consequences, and caregiver burden. This study concerns the design of a smart pillbox to enhance medication adherence in dementia management through real-time ingestion authentication. Leveraging lowcost embedded hardware (Raspberry Pi Zero, Arduino UNO, camera module, buzzer, LCD) and Python-based computer vision, our system issues timely audio-visual reminders, captures post-reminder images of the pill compartment, and employs OpenCV pre-processing alongside a YOLOv5 object-detection model to determine whether pills have been removed. During a several-day trial with eight participants (84 medication events), the device had a 92 % adherence rate and 96 % detection accuracy, verifying its effectiveness in minimizing missed doses and offering objective compliance feedback. These results prove that an inexpensive, portable, and open-source smart pillbox can significantly improve medication management in dementia patients, providing a scalable solution for independent living and reduced caregiver burden.

title: Smart Stitch: A Mobile App for Personalized Garment Customization and Stitching Guidance
venue: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Smart Stitch is an innovative mobile app aimed at easily facilitating both beginners and experts in garment making. Integrating real-time 3D visualization, dynamic simulation of fabrics, and interactive stitching guides, this app allows the user to enter his measurements and visualize customized garments with utmost accuracy. The users have to choose the designs from Kurtis, Anarkali, and blouses while uploading fabric images to see realistic previews of how the chosen materials and patterns will appear on the selected garments. A further advantage of Smart Stitch is step-wise animated sewing instructions and the estimation of materials required for the garment along with costs determined through its estimation tool. The back end of the app engages modern technology such as Three.js, WebGL, and Blender, for real-time rendering, and Python for fabric optimization and cost computation. Future improvements entail the integration of AI-based fabric suggestions, as well as augmented reality for virtual try-ons of garments. Smart Stitch wants to transform the way one does garment creation at home: quickly producing personally tailored, well-fitted garments with ease and accurately fitting pieces.

title: Smart Supply Chain Management with Attribute-Based Encryption Access Control
venue: 2023 IEEE 13th Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference (CCWC)
abstract: The traditional supply chain management process is becoming more automated with the use of cutting-edge blockchain technologies. This helps in reducing the time taken for various processes and also helps in reducing the overall cost. In this paper, we developed a framework for tracking the progress of the supply chain process. The framework uses a variety of technologies to track the status and the progress of products in transit. Raspberry Pi 400 is used to track the progress of products at each chain level using Radio-frequency Identification (RFID) tags as well as other sensors. The tracking data collected by the Raspberry Pi is stored on the blockchain. A decentralized storage network (DSN) is used to store the encryption of Intellectual Property (IP) data (e.g., blueprints, design choices at each production stage, etc). Attribute-based encryption is used to allow access to the data only to authorized stakeholders who have the appropriate attributes. We leverage smart contracts and Node.js to develop a decentralized application (DApp) for monitoring the supply chain process. The DApp is hosted on the decentralized Ethereum platform, which provides security and transparency for all transactions. Our security analysis demonstrates that the system is secure against data theft and the results obtained from our experiments show that our proposed framework is scalable and efficient.

title: Smart Surveillance Camera Using AI
venue: 2024 Second International Conference on Advances in Information Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The Python script recognizes faces in real-time webcam video by using computer vision algorithms. For face detection, facial feature encoding, and face comparison with known faces, it makes use of the Open CV and face recognition packages. When the script detects a familiar face, it adds the name and the current time to a CSV file, indicating the person's attendance. In a similar manner, it records attendance for unidentified faces as “unknown.” It also takes pictures of faces you don't recognize and saves them for later review or identification. The program repeatedly scans the video stream for faces, identifying them and cross-referencing them with a database of recognized faces. After a brief pause, if an unknown face is identified, a second face recognition procedure is started to either validate the identity or label the person as unknown. The script shows the promise of computer vision techniques in a variety of applications, such as security, identity systems, and attendance monitoring. It offers a straightforward but efficient approach for real-time face recognition and attendance tracking.

title: Smart Surveillance for Blinds: A YOLOv5-Based Assistive Vision System
venue: 2025 20th International Conference on Emerging Technologies (ICET)
abstract: People with visual impairments reduce an individual’s ability to navigate their surroundings safely to keep them-selves from hazards. Recent researchers have made advancements in computer vision and deep learning which can help them in routes life. The proposed work presents a smartphone-based Smart Surveillance System for the Visually Impaired (SSFB) application for blind users which improves nearby environmental alertness through real-time object detection and with voice feedback. The SSFB uses the YOLOv5 object detection model, which trained on a custom dataset with four target labels: stairs, doors, electrical switches, and roads. LabelImg software was used to label the data custom datasets and trained the model in Python via transfer learning techniques to improve accuracy and improve performance for mobile applications. The SSFP application integrates with Python and JavaScript API for text-to-voice conversion to give a voice signal to users in real-time obstacle detection. Obtained results display that the SSFB attains accurate object detection and fast audio feedback, making it an effective, low-cost, and practical solution to support safe and independent navigation for visually impaired individuals.

title: Smart Surveillance Object Detection System
venue: 2024 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence For Internet of Things (AIIoT)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated Internet of Things based approach to smart surveillance and urban parking management systems, emphasizing robust object detection and precise parking occupancy monitoring. Our solution adopts cost-effective hardware like the ESP32 CAM module, leveraging its built-in camera and powerful processor for real-time image processing. For surveillance applications, we implement a custom object detection model built with OpenCV, a renowned Python library. This model, finely-tuned for efficient person detection, runs directly on the ESP32 CAM, eliminating the need for external processing units. Additionally, the ESP32 CAM’s Wi-Fi connectivity enables seamless integration with existing networks, simplifying deployment. This integrated approach, combining the cost-effectiveness of ESP32 CAM modules with the image processing capabilities of OpenCV, offers a comprehensive solution for smart surveillance and urban parking management. By utilizing readily available hardware and open-source software, the system promotes widespread adoption and affordability, making it a valuable tool for creating smarter and more sustainable cities.

title: Smart Traffic Intersection Management System for Efficient Urban Mobility
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on New Frontiers in Communication, Automation, Management and Security (ICCAMS)
abstract: This project presents a hybrid traffic management system integrating Python-based image processing and Verilog-based traffic signal control through socket-based communication. The system utilizes real-time traffic data, process vehicle density, and detect violations such as red-light crossing and overspeeding. The extracted data is transmitted to an FPGA-based traffic controller, which dynamically adjusts signal timings to optimize traffic flow. The real-time adaptability of the system enhances traffic efficiency, minimizes congestion, and improves road safety, making it a scalable solution for smart city applications.

title: Smart Traffic Management System
venue: 2019 15th International Conference on Electronics, Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Millions of vehicles pass via roads and cities every day. Various economic, social and cultural factors affect growth of traffic congestion. The effect of traffic congestion has major impacts on accidents, loss of time, cost, delay of emergency, etc. Due to traffic congestions there is a loss in productivity from workers, people lose time, trade opportunities are lost, delivery gets delayed leading to increasing cost. In providing solutions to these congestion problems, a new robust and smart solution that is based on Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) technology capable of addressing road accident and traffic management in Nigeria's mega cities is proposed. In this paper, the proposed system serves as an alternative to the existing traffic management system with an intersection control station that communicates with vehicles approaching the intersection through the V2I network. The vehicles are equipped with Dashboard Traffic Light (DBTL) sensors that communicate with the infrastructure. A Safe-to-Pass-First (SPF) algorithm was designed that considered real time speed, vehicle position and data to decide when to allow the vehicle to pass through the intersection. The algorithm checks the status of conflicting lanes to ensure that vehicle pass the intersection safely. This method has been found to be more efficient than the existing methods as the average waiting time at the intersection is reduced by 23% and improved throughput recorded, Python code and SUMO were used for the simulation.

title: Smart Traffic Management: Optimization and Analysis Using YOLOv8
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Networks and Soft Computing (ICNSoC)
abstract: Effectively managing traffic flow is of paramount importance, particularly for emergency vehicles such as ambulances that require expedited passage through roadways. In numerous urban environments, this system fails to operate efficiently. The process of altering traffic signals requires a significant amount of time, which can result in delays for ambulances. A prior research study employed the YOLOv3 model for traffic management based on vehicle density; however, its accuracy was found to be suboptimal. In contrast, the project utilizes the YOLOv8 model, which provides enhanced accuracy and expedience in ambulance detection. The development of the project was carried out using the Python programming language. The findings indicate that YOLOv8 surpasses YOLOv3 in terms of accuracy and prioritizing emergency vehicles, thereby facilitating faster arrival times for ambulances. The infrastructure of smart cities is being advanced by this program. Traffic lights are set up to change automatically when an ambulance is successfully detected, giving the vehicle an unobstructed path while minimizing delays.

title: Smart Video Surveillance System with Intruder Identification and Behavioural Anomaly Detection using YOLOv8
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
abstract: The smart video surveillance system with intruder identification and behavioural anomaly detection using YOLOv8 aims to enhance security monitoring through intelligent automation. Traditional surveillance systems require manual observation, making them inefficient and prone to human error. Existing methods often fail to accurately detect intruders or analyse unusual behaviour in real time. To overcome these limitations, this project integrates YOLOv8, a state-of-the-art deep learning object detection model, for precise and rapid identification of people and intruders. The system will also include behavioural anomaly detection using motion tracking and pattern analysis to recognize suspicious activities. Implementation involves real-time video streaming, object tracking and alert generation using Python and OpenCV. The model will be trained on security datasets to improve detection accuracy. The expected outcome is an automated, high-accuracy surveillance system that minimizes false alarms and enhances situational awareness in security-sensitive environments.

title: Smart Voice Controlled Wheelchair With Automated Navigation
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Circuit, Power & Computing Technologies (ICCPCT)
abstract: The problem of independent movement is an essential problem for people with severe motor disabilities, as the conventional hand-operated or joystick-operated wheelchairs demand hand dexterity beyond the capability of people with severe motor disabilities. The proposed project is based on the development of a voice-operated autonomous wheel Chair System based on the triple Node Concept. The triple node concept divides the task into: Vision Node, Python Node, and Actuator Node, thus enabling high-speed responses to the user inputs and smooth movements in an indoor environment.The proposed system makes use of digital markers referred to as ArUco markers, which enable precise determination of the position of the markers. The Breadth-First Search Algorithm is used for the determination of an optimum path between the nodes in the room. A deterministic 6-State Machine is used for the determination of movement from target detection to target arrival. The proposed system includes the Safety Reflex Mechanism for the safety of the user through hardware-level ultrasonic sensors. The proposed project is a solution that enables people with severe motor disabilities to take control of their movements using the natural interface of vision and voice.

title: Smart Walking Cane for the Specially Abled People
venue: 2022 International Conference on Communication, Computing and Internet of Things (IC3IoT)
abstract: Vision deprived individuals with strolling dysfunctionalities or optically weaken, often find it very arduous to perform errands independently in their daily chores. Activities like walking down the road, knowing and recognizing the presence of an obstacle in front of them, reading road signs etc. Such activities and tasks are easy for us unimpaired people but for them these are the major hurdles of their lives and not being able to do them makes them feel emotionally low which increases their stress levels and affects their health. The suggested project is an effort to outline and build a smart walking cane for the blind to help them perform their daily errands independently and henceforth, over the time improving their morale. This work is split into two constituents with the hardware and software. The hardware constituent involves building a physical cane with Raspberry Pi, ultrasonic sensor and the software constituent involves the use of written programs based on Python and OpenCV to process images for object recognition in real time.

title: Smart Warehouse Monitoring System for Collaborative Character Recognition Platform Research
venue: 2024 8th Asian Conference on Artificial Intelligence Technology (ACAIT)
abstract: Hazardous chemical warehousing is highly hazardous, highly specialized and highly regulated, requiring professional warehousing equipment and personnel, while the state and local regulatory requirements for this strict, industrial upgrading of hazardous chemical warehousing supervision is imperative. Current related research includes safety inspection robots, RFID and UWB, etc. Although it can realize the detection and positioning of goods, it still exists problems such as high cost, poor portability, poor real-time, etc. The system described in this paper is based on the character interaction behavior recognition algorithm through the monocular RGB camera, structured light camera and the unmanned inspection vehicle to achieve the detection of human behavior and the state of the goods, which reduces the system's Based on the point cloud difference algorithm, the relative position of the boundary line through the edge detection of the goods to achieve the goods pressure line alarm, to improve the portability of the system to deal with different warehouse scenarios; based on the python language, through the Vue + Django system architecture to achieve the real-time monitoring of the hazardous chemical warehouse and the approval of the status of the goods, to enhance the ability of the warehouse to deal with the real-time situation. The ability of the warehouse to handle real-time conditions is enhanced.

title: Smart Warehouse Monitoring System using Internet of Things (IoT)
venue: 2023 2nd International Conference on Vision Towards Emerging Trends in Communication and Networking Technologies (ViTECoN)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) technology is used in smart warehousing, a monitoring system. Crops are stored and preserved in some ideal state after harvest. IoT sensors gather information on the warehouse climate and take prompt action in response to the farmers' input. Using Arduino and sensors, this system gives farmers access to real-time information about their products or goods. Fruits and vegetables can be kept fresh for longer by using proper air conditioning. In this approach, crop preservation is achieved by smart warehousing, which controls warehouse variables like temperature and humidity while retaining ambient conditions and room climate. Also, our sensors let us know if any thefts are occurring in our warehouse.

title: Smart Wheelchair Controlled by Head Movements
venue: 2024 International Conference on Power, Energy, Control and Transmission Systems (ICPECTS)
abstract: This paper introduces overview of smart wheelchairs controlled by head movements, an emerging technology aimed at improving mobility and independence for individuals with motor disabilities. Traditional wheelchair control interfaces often pose challenges for users with limited hand dexterity, necessitating innovative solutions to enhance accessibility and ease of navigation. The core of the system lies in the real-time processing of video input captured by a camera mounted on the wheelchair. By leveraging computer vision algorithms, such as open-cv python and motion tracking, the system identifies and tracks the user’s head movements with high accuracy and responsiveness. This information is then used to generate control commands (like Forward, Backward, Right, Left) for the wheelchair, allowing users to navigate smoothly and intuitively. In additionally, the smart wheelchair system offers various features to enhance user experience and safety. These include obstacle detection and healthcare parameters, as well as customizable control parameters to accommodate individual user preferences and mobility needs. By leveraging the power of computer vision, the system offers a more intuitive and accessible means of wheelchair navigation, empowering users to navigate their environments with greater freedom and independence.

title: SmartDine: A Comprehensive System for Enhancing Customer Satisfaction and Optimizing Business Operations in the Restaurant Context
venue: 2024 6th International Conference on Advancements in Computing (ICAC)
abstract: This research explores the integration of real-time video analysis, deep learning techniques, and advanced data processing tools to enhance customer satisfaction and operational efficiency in restaurant management. Leveraging CCTV footage, along with tools such as Python,PyTorch, OpenCV, and advanced models like YOLOv10 for object detection and YOLO-pose for key point extraction, the study focuses on optimizing key aspects such as food satisfaction analysis, customer engagement and wait time reduction, optimal use and planning of resources. Custom models, including an LSTM network, analyze detected key points to identify customer actions and estimate time spent on various activities. Data augmentation techniques enhance model performance, with metrics like precision and recall used for evaluation. The study further aims to provide restaurant managers with a dynamic dashboard that tracks real-time insights, including table turnover rates, preferred menu items, and optimal resource allocation. This research contributes to data-driven restaurant management by offering a robust framework for real-time operational analysis, ultimately improving decision-making and enhancing the dining experience.

title: SmartSight Assist: A Guardian-Connected Blind Assistance System Using AI and IoT
venue: 2026 13th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
abstract: In this project, we have developed SmartSight Assist, which is a system that assists blind people in navigating safely and is connected to a guardian. We have a wearable IoT technology, deep learning, and a mobile application integrated into our system. An ESP32-CAM module has been attached to two glasses that we have used to telecast real-time images of the surroundings. The photos are then sent to a Python backend server, which, in turn, uses the YOLO model to identify objects such as people, cars, doors, and other obstacles. The information is then sent to a Flutter application that has a Text-to-Speech (TTS) module that provides voice prompts to the user. Our system is a dual-mode design, which is its most significant aspect. It has a Blind User mode for navigation and a guardian mode that lets family members track the user's GPS location and what they are detecting at the moment. Our proposed system is highly portable and cost-effective, which makes it feasible for everyone. We have tested our system in both indoor and outdoor environments, and the results demonstrate that our system operates with low latency and high accuracy. By integrating wearable sensors and AI, this project enables visually impaired individuals to be more aware of their surroundings and feel safer.

title: Snake in the Grass: A Hybrid Detection Method Targeting Malicious PyPI Packages
venue: IEEE Transactions on Reliability
abstract: As an increasing number of reusable packages are available in software development, package ecosystems are becoming more mature. Python is one of the most popular programming languages today. PyPI, as the primary repository of Python packages, serves a critical role in Python software development. While PyPI enables registered users to publish open-source packages, attackers can disguise themselves as developers to distribute malicious packages. We present a hybrid malicious python package detection framework named PCPD, which combines static anomaly detection and dynamic running analysis to detect lurking malicious packages. Using PCPD, we analyze a real-world dataset containing 414 880 PyPI packages and successfully narrow the inspection scope to 324 suspicious packages, reducing the manual review workload for repository managers by 99.48%. We have identified 121 packages with malicious behavior using PCPD and made all samples publicly available for security researchers to help mitigate these risks and protect the community. In addition, we discover potential factors that enable malicious packages to evade scrutiny from repositories and associated threat signals.

title: SoC engineering trends as impacted by new applications and system level requirements
venue: Sixth international symposium on quality electronic design (isqed'05)
abstract: Summary form only given. The SoC increasing integration scale as well as the system and customer requirements are important factors for a complete revisit of the development models for electronic products. New customer models ask for software driven electronics. Software engineering is moving to a component-based and MDA development approach to be applied to embedded applications. Hardware engineering is moving to SSDI system level development and reuse methodologies. The two approaches have now to be further developed and combined for next generation SoC to get high quality and adaptable designs at a reasonable development cost. New application-level quality standards have also to be part of the complete development flow. We demonstrated through several examples these new methodologies: system engineering methodology on software radios (UML, PIM (platform independent model) and PSM (platform specific model)) and its current extension to the hardware parts (SCA, OCP potential extensions), system engineering in line with the common criteria development and qualification process for new security products (PP (protection profile) and ST (security target)), development and validation methodology in line with DO254 standard for new safety products in avionics (formal verification). Impacts on SoC architectures and design techniques are discussed.

title: Social Engineering Threat Detection on Reddit Using OSINT and Transformer-Based NLP Model
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovative Trends in Information Technology (ICITIIT)
abstract: With the rise of deceptive job offers, financial scams, and grooming on platforms like Reddit, safeguarding users against social engineering threats has become increasingly critical. Traditional moderation methods often fall short due to the scale and evolving nature of such attacks. To address this, we present a hybrid Open-Source Intelligence - Natural Language Processing (OSINT-NLP) pipeline that automates the detection of suspicious Reddit posts. High-risk subreddits in this study were defined as communities that have been reported or observed to facilitate activities such as online grooming, human trafficking, exploitation, fraudulent recruitment, and other forms of malicious social engineering. The system collects data via the Python Reddit API Wrapper (PRAW API), targeting high-risk subreddits and keywords. Posts are preprocessed using spaCy and regular expressions to extract entities like emails, phone numbers, and URLs. A rule-based engine provides initial risk scores (Low, Medium, High), which are refined by a fine-tuned DistilBERT classifier. For deeper threat attribution, the pipeline integrates Maigret, enabling the profiling of usernames across over a hundred online platforms. The system is deployed via a Streamlit dashboard for real-time monitoring and a Flask app for structured analysis. Tested on about 5000 posts, it achieved 93.7% accuracy, with significant improvement in High-risk F1 scores. Our results show that blending heuristics, deep learning, and OSINT offers a scalable, explainable solution for automated threat detection and digital safety enforcement.

title: Software Architecture Recovery Augmented With Semantics
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
abstract: The architecture of software systems evolves along with their upgrades and maintenance, inevitably creating a gap between the defact architecture and the designed one. To perceive and fix the discrepancy, clustering-based architecture recovery methods have been developed to re-engineer the real-time system architecture from the code implementation. However, existing solutions still face several limitations. They underutilize both code-level and architecture-level semantics underlying the source code. Moreover, they overlook implicit structural dependencies that complement explicit ones to reflect code interactions. To address these challenges, we propose SemArc, an architecture recovery method that utilizes large language models to comprehend both implementation-level and architecture-level semantics, supported by well-established canonical architectural patterns as a knowledge base. SemArc also incorporates both implicit and explicit dependencies to complete the system behavior representations. Additionally, SemArc introduces a component-as-anchor guided clustering algorithm to improve the clustering process. We evaluated SemArc on 15 software systems written in C/C++, Java, and Python, using five different metrics. The results demonstrate that SemArc outperforms seven baseline methods by an average of 32 percentage points. We also examined how three factors—code semantics, architectural semantics, and implicit dependencies—as well as different levels of architectural semantic descriptions, influence recovery accuracy. A case study on the Bash project indicates that SemArc has the potential to yield even more precise recovery results than those labeled by humans.

title: Software code base conversions
venue: 2007 IEEE/AIAA 26th Digital Avionics Systems Conference
abstract: Current and future military avionic systems require real-time embedded software based on the latest technological advances in software tools, capabilities, and languages. However, the development time and lifecycle of avionic systems is so long, that the tools, processes, methodologies, and languages used by the system developers are often obsolete by the time the systems need significant upgrades or replacement. Hence, software obsolescence is a major issue faced by many avionic systems. Previously, avionics programs have tackled software obsolescence using different approaches. These approaches have included code conversions by hand, which are costly and time consuming, scripting tools/languages which have scalability problems, emulators which involve re-engineering of the peripheral code base and retention of the obsolete code engineering environment, and software wrappers which are not costly but hinder future modifications to the legacy software that is accessed by the software wrappers. Each of these approaches has its own liabilities. For our research and development effort we chose to upgrade our legacy code base with a specially developed code refactoring transformer, the Boeing migration tool (BMT). Specially developed code transformers based on new technologies and more powerful computers are scalable, capable of converting almost the entire code base, allow for future development on the updated code base with the latest tools, processes, methodologies, and languages, and are less costly than updating code by hand. This paper details the inputs, the code transformer itself, the outputs, and how well the code transformer performed its task for updating a software code base. This work was performed for the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) program composition for embedded systems (PCES) program. The resulting code base generated by the code transformer could be updated with the most recent tools, processes, and languages. DARPA's objective w

title: Software development tools for embedded systems
venue: Proceedings of 14th Digital Avionics Systems Conference
abstract: Software quality and availability (completion) is highly impacted by the tools used in each stage of development. By focusing on tools issues, this paper increases the developers' focus to formulating a sound software development environment. The starting point of system software development is requirement analysis and design. Once the system is defined, its functions are allocated to distinct hardware or software items, and interfaces between these items are defined. Software requirement analysis is the process of specifying software function, performance, interfaces and design constraints. The next stage is preliminary design. This is followed by detailed design that may be represented graphically or in a combination of programming language. The design is then taken up for implementation which involves writing code for all units and testing them individually. The final stage is integration and software component level testing. Tools for embedded system development include: cross compilation systems, in-circuit tools, simulators, debuggers etc. The features, benefits and tradeoffs of these tools, and how they apply to each stage of software development, are examined. This will provide the designer with a comprehensive suite of software development tools that support embedded designs.

title: Software Environment for Automated Experiments with DC/DC Converters
venue: 2024 12th International Scientific Conference on Computer Science (COMSCI)
abstract: The paper details the architecture of an automated measurement system application developed in Python. It leverages packages such as PyVISA, Pandas, and PyQt6 for its graphical user interface. The application is utilized in power electronics to measure the efficiency of DC/DC converters. The structure and key functions of the virtual instrument's code are presented and analyzed. Notable features include real-time plotting of results, safety feature buttons in the GUI for critical situations, a faster and more flexible measurement setup, and multi-platform compatibility, thanks to the use of open-source software.

title: Software implementation of common criteria related design patterns
venue: 2013 Federated Conference on Computer Science and Information Systems
abstract: Writing evidence documents for evaluation and certification processes according to the Common Criteria security standard is a very difficult, time-consuming and complex task. Nowadays there are only a few, limited solutions based on templates and software tools which can efficiently support developers in preparing evaluation deliverables. This paper describes the results of an R&D project whose aim was to work out a computer-aided tool with built-in design patterns. Firstly, according to all security assurance requirements the design patterns in a paper version were prepared. Secondly, they were verified and validated by the developers in order to make some amendments and improvements. The conclusions were used as the source of functional requirements for a computer-aided tool. As a result a complete computer system was designed which implements the design patterns, knowledge base, evaluation methodology, and additional external supporting software. That solution facilitates and speeds up the development of the evidence documentation.

title: Software Integrated Instruction of Solid Mechanics
venue: 2024 IEEE Frontiers in Education Conference (FIE)
abstract: This paper presents the role of JupyterLab, a web-based, free Python coding platform, in solving and analyzing complicated problems of solid mechanics in real-time during classroom lectures. The objectives of using JupyterLab are five-fold: (a) to address the difficulty in explaining the interconnection of multiple variables that affect the solution to solid mechanics problems from a holistic standpoint, (b) to discuss the core concepts of solid mechanics using a set of generalized problems and their solutions with easily modifiable input parameters, (c) to help students attain the ability to critically think about the course concepts and apply them to analyze complex problems, (d) to test students' ability to apply the concepts covered in class to problems that are outside the scope of the course topics, and (e) to promote awareness of outlier situations wherein traditionally taught tools are inapplicable. The ultimate goal is to amplify the learning outcomes of the course and actively engage students in the learning process, helping them prepare for the growing AI-inclined job market in the engineering sector.

title: Software Interference Prevention and SWaP-C Minimization in Cyber-Physical Systems Using Hypervisor Technology
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology, Informatics, Management, Engineering and Environment (TIME-E)
abstract: Currently, hypervisor technology is an emerging topic of research. Virtualization technology, especially hypervisors and virtual machines (VM), has been widely studied but is still little applied in the cyber-physical systems (CPS) field. A hypervisor, or VM monitor (VMM), is a software program used to run multiple VMs on a single physical machine through space and time partitioning in a real-time operating system. This paper discusses the hypervisor technology to prevent software interference and to minimize size, weight, and power-cost (SWaP-C) in cyber physical systems, as well as, the application of hypervisor technology in the aerospace, automotive and control fields. By partitioning, a hypervisor can increase software safety because application programs with different criticality levels do not affect each other in failure when run in partitioned VMs.

title: Software Performance Prediction with a Time Scaling Scheduling Profiler
venue: 2011 IEEE 19th Annual International Symposium on Modelling, Analysis, and Simulation of Computer and Telecommunication Systems
abstract: We present a new approach to software performance analysis that aims to extend conventional profiling with some of the predictive capabilities of a performance model. The idea is to execute programs in virtual time, which allows hypothetical time scaling of the constituent parts of an application to be explored in advance of any speculative redevelopment aimed at improving performance. Virtual time execution works via a virtual time scheduler that controls execution by wrapping the underlying (real time) system scheduler and enforcing a thread schedule that takes account of time scaling. The necessary instruments to achieve this are added automatically to the profiled program at load time. We present VEX, a generic low-level kernel for supporting such a `scheduling profiler' in this sense and JINE, a specific instrumentation framework for the Java programming language, that builds on VEX. An evaluation of the VEX/JINE framework with a wide range of standard benchmarks shows that the prediction error is less 10% on average and the execution time overheads less than a factor of two on average, for the benchmarks tested. We also illustrate various time scaling experiments, which yield results that are quite different to those predicted from conventional profiling measurements.

title: Software safety analysis of a flight guidance system
venue: Proceedings. The 21st Digital Avionics Systems Conference
abstract: An aircraft's flight control system provides the capability to stabilize and control the aircraft. Two key elements of a flight control system are the flight guidance system that generates guidance commands and the auto-pilot that executes them. The flight guidance system is a software function composed of flight control laws, that determine the roll and pitch values needed to achieve the desired flight characteristics, and mode logic that selects the appropriate flight control law for the given situation. We developed a formal, executable model of the requirements for the mode logic of a flight guidance system and conducted a comprehensive software safety analysis on the model. We provide an overview of the safety analysis conducted on the software and summarize progress made to date in the use of formal methods to verify the presence of the required safety properties in the software itself.

title: Software/hardware co-design of a Java-based 32bit microprocessor for mobile multimedia applications
venue: 2003 IEEE Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (IEEE Cat. No.03TH8668)
abstract: A 32bit Java-based processor is designed for mobile multimedia applications to run MIPS-compatible local instructions and some application-specific Java bytecodes in a RISC-like architecture. In Java-mode, some Java bytecodes employed in the specific application are decoded into local instructions by VLSI implementation. With VHDL simulation tools, SW/HW co-design verified that Java bytecodes could be executed on the processor with a local thread for a real-time visual processing. Furthermore, the design was synthesized to physical layout according to 1.2 /spl mu/m standard CMOS technology and the simulation shows that the processor can run at a frequency of 20 MHz.

title: Solution for Autonomous Vehicle Parking
venue: 2021 International Symposium ELMAR
abstract: With the advancement of technology, there is a significant development in automotive industry, where the vehicle itself performs more and more driving functions. The number of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADASs) has been rising significantly. In this paper, the solution for autonomous vehicle parking is proposed. Firstly, an algorithm that detects parking spaces (PSs) and classifies them only by processing frames received from the camera placed on the side of the ego vehicle was developed. Furthermore, an algorithm for performing the autonomous vehicle parking in different ways (forward/backward, left/right side of the road) at detected free PS is developed. The solution was developed using Python programing language and OpenCV library and tested in CARLA simulator. Test results show that the algorithm correctly detects and classifies PSs in 100% of test cases, whereas after that the success of the parking process itself was 88%. The algorithm is capable of processing 10 frames per second, thus allowing real-time operation for typical vehicle speed during parking process.

title: Solving the Family Traveling Salesperson Problem in the Adleman–Lipton Model Based on DNA Computing
venue: IEEE Transactions on NanoBioscience
abstract: The Family Traveling Salesperson Problem (FTSP) is a variant of the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), in which all vertices are divided into several different families, and the goal of the problem is to find a loop that concatenates a specified number of vertices with minimal loop overhead. As a Non-deterministic Polynomial Complete (NP-complete) problem, it is difficult to deal with it by the traditional computing. On the contrary, as a computer with strong parallel ability, the DNA computer has incomparable advantages over digital computers when dealing with NP problems. Based on this, a DNA algorithm is proposed to deal with FTSP based on the Adleman-Lipton model. In the algorithm, the solution of the problem can be obtained by executing several basic biological manipulations on DNA molecules with  ${O}$ ( ${N}^{{2}}$ ) computing complexity ( ${N}$  is the number of vertices in the problem without the origin). Through the simulation experiments on some benchmark instances, the results show that the parallel DNA algorithm has better performance than traditional computing. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by deducing the algorithm process in detail. Furthermore, the algorithm further proves that DNA computing, as one of the parallel computing methods, has the potential to solve more complex big data problems.

title: SOS: Standard-Compliant and Packet Loss Tolerant Security Framework for ADS-B Communications
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
abstract: The Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B) technology, already deployed by the major avionics companies (e.g., QatarAirways and AmericanAirlines), will become mandatory on board of civil and military aircraft flying in Class A, B, and C airspaces by 2020, enabling direct airplanes communications and enhanced flights monitoring. However, ADS-B has been designed without security considerations, thus being vulnerable to a variety of attacks, including message injection and messages order manipulation attacks, that can be easily performed via widely available commercial Software Defined Radios. To address these threats, we present Securing Open Skies (SOS), a standard-compliant, backward-compatible, loss-tolerant, and bandwidth efficient security framework to secure ADS-B communications. SOS leverages the real deployment of densely distributed, participatory ADS-B sensor networks such as OpenSky Network and Flight Radar, and provides message authentication and integrity security services on a time-slot basis, without resorting to any public key cryptography mechanism. Experimental performances obtained through a realistic proof-of-concept, deployed using commercial Ettus Research X310 Software Defined Radios, demonstrate the viability and effectiveness of our solution, even in presence of uniformly at random or burst packet loss events characterizing the ADS-B frequency band. For instance, SOS allows the verification of the authenticity of ADS-B messages requiring less than 50 percent of bandwidth overhead, with a percentage of verifiable slots above 80 percent, even in an highly lossy environment, characterized by a single packet loss probability of 60 percent-the process requiring less than one second: almost one tenth of similar approaches published in the literature. Finally, a thorough comparison against state of the art solutions in the literature highlights the unique security and reliability features enjoyed by SOS, as well as its practical viabili

title: Space Debris Tracking Using Intelligent Distributed Satellite Systems for Point-to-Point Suborbital Space Flights
venue: 2025 AIAA DATC/IEEE 44th Digital Avionics Systems Conference (DASC)
abstract: Suborbital space tourism and transport is projected to generate $1.1 billion for the commercial space industry by 2032. The rapid advancement in sub-orbital transport technology necessitates innovative solutions to ensure the safety and reliability of such missions traversing the congested near-Earth space environment. Point-to-point Suborbital Flight (P2PSF) is the next step in commercial space transport and is envisioned to be commercially viable by 2030. While suborbital flights generally avoid the most congested regions of Low Earth Orbit (LEO), which start around 160 km, the risk of encountering space debris still exists at altitudes between 100 km to 200 km, which are considered suitable altitudes for P2PSF missions. Debris at these altitudes includes smaller fragments from disintegrated objects and meteoroid remnants. At the high velocities typical of suborbital flights, even small debris can cause significant damage. It is essential to track the total number of objects in space, continuously estimate their trajectories, and assess the probability of collisions for efficient Space Traffic Management (STM). This article proposes an innovative trajectory estimation algorithm through Data Fusion from multiple Electro-Optical Sensors (EOS) performing Space-Based Space Surveillance (SBSS) that shall contribute to elevating the overall safety of sub-orbital transport missions. The proposed tracking algorithm is validated through a comprehensive P2PSF verification case study.
