abstract: Indian Sign Language (ISL) serves as a vital communication medium for the hearing- and speech-impaired community, yet effective real-time translation systems remain limited. This paper proposes a real-time ISL translation framework based on a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture to capture both spatial and temporal characteristics of hand gestures. A landmark-based preprocessing technique is employed to isolate hand regions and minimize background interference. The proposed model is evaluated on a custom ISL dataset consisting of 25 gesture classes performed by multiple signers under varied conditions. Experimental results demonstrate a recognition accuracy of 92% with an end-to-end latency of 200 ms, confirming the suitability of the system for real-time assistive communication applications.

title: Sign Language-to-Emotion-Specific Text Translation: A Review
venue: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Computing and Renewable Systems (ICACRS)
abstract: Communication barriers significantly impact the deaf and mute community, who rely on Sign Language—a system of visual gestures and facial expressions—to interact. However, the lack of accessible translation tools hinders their full social participation. Existing solutions primarily focus on converting text or audio into sign language or translating fingerspelling, often neglecting the emotional context of the communication. This project proposes an AI-based system to address this gap by translating sign language into text and detecting and translating the text specific to the signer’s emotions. The system will utilize Deep Learning and Computer Vision techniques, specifically MediaPipe for real-time hand and pose tracking, Temporal Convolutional networks (TCNs) for Sign Language Recognition(SLR) which captures temporal dynamics of gestures and T5(text-to-text transfer transformer) for Sign language translation(SLT) of the text that is specific to an emotion. The dataset will include videos of sign language in American Sign Language (ASL) focusing on everyday vocabulary. The outcome is to enhance communication for the deaf and mute by providing real-time, context-aware translations, including emotional nuances. It would contribute to greater inclusivity and empowerment, ensuring that the voices and emotions of the deaf and mute population are accurately represented and understood in various social interactions.

title: SIGN SCHOOL-An interactive website to promote Indian Sign Language
venue: 2022 Fifth International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Technologies (CCICT)
abstract: Hand gestures are one of the nonverbal communication modalities used in sign language. It is most typically used by deaf and dumb persons who have hearing or speech issues to communicate with each other or with non-deaf people.Dumb people are frequently denied regular communication with other members of society, and normal people often struggle to understand and communicate with them. These individuals must rely on an interpreter or some form of visual communication to communicate. It is unlikely that an interpreter will be available at all times, and visual communication is often difficult to comprehend. In this paper, we are proposing a solution by which people can learn and practice the Indian sign language easily. We are proposing a YOLOv5 model which is lightweight, fast and is more accurate than other technologies used. We have achieved around 99.8 percent accuracy which is high enough to detect several gestures in the Indian sign Language. This paper also proposes a creation of an interactive website which will allow the users to easily navigate them through their journey to learn the Indian Sign Language.

title: Sign the Voice: An Embedded Software for Voice to Sign Language Translation
venue: 2024 2nd International Conference on Computing and Data Analytics (ICCDA)
abstract: This qualitative research study entitled Sign the Voice: An Embedded Software for Voice to Sign Language Translation aimed to bridge the communication barriers between hearing teachers and auditory-challenged students. This explored the current technologies used in the development of systems for Persons with Disabilities particularly the Deaf Community. This study aimed to develop an embedded software to translate in real-time a human's voice to sign language, making communication accessible between them. The researchers conducted interviews, focus groups, observation, and case studies. This study investigated the design process and usability of embedded software. Software testing and thematic analysis will then be conducted to test its effectiveness. The researchers considered the diverse needs of auditory-challenged students, real-time processing, and the accuracy of the translation to make sure the communication process is effective between hearing teachers and auditory-challenged students. Preliminary findings suggested promising results in terms of user satisfaction, highlighting the potential of the proposed embedded software to provide accessible communication between the hearing teachers and auditory-challenged students. The implications of this study will provide more IT opportunities for these auditory-challenged students, give diversity in the IT industry, and could lead to more opportunities for applied research by developing improved technological solutions. The cultural, societal, and ethical impacts of this proposed system were of high consideration.

title: Sign-Speak
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Advances in Intelligent Computing and Applications (AICAPS)
abstract: People who use American Sign Language (ASL) often rely on it as their primary way of communicating with each other. When they find it hard to express themselves verbally, it can sometimes be challenging for them to share their feelings or emotions in a way that others easily understand.. And since the vast majority of the population does not use American Sign Language (ASL), there is a significant communication barrier between hearing impaired and hearing communities. The purpose of our SIGN-SPEAK application is to provide a web application that will translate sign language into text from video uploaded and back into sign language from uploaded video in real time. Computer vision via Media Pipe is used to detect hand movements, along with a Random Forest Classifier to provide validation of accurately recognizing specific signs (or gestures). Media Pipe captures 21 unique key points on both hands to render an accurate representation of the gestures made; additionally, Random Forest uses the captured data to identify the patterns of signs. This helps the system recognize letters,numbers, and words in real time. The prototype achieves 96 percent accuracy on four static gestures. Processes at 30 frames per second with less than one second of latency. Our application connects users with disorders to the outside community,making communication easier and more inclusive. Testing shows that the system detects and translates signs effectively, making it useful for schools, hospitals, and public services.

title: SignaSpectrum: AI-Driven Dynamic Sign Language Detection and Interpretation
venue: 2024 11th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (Trends and Future Directions) (ICRITO)
abstract: Sign Language, the vibrant language of silent grace woven by the deaf and hard-of-hearing community, can sometimes find its flow tangled in the everyday threads of communication. Signaspectrum, a groundbreaking AI-powered system, aims to unravel these knots and build a seamless bridge through real-time, dynamic sign language detection and interpretation. Fueled by the fire of deep learning in the fields of artificial intelligence, it navigates the flowing river of gestures like thank you, goodbye, I love you. These seemingly common sign language gestures may be very common language for the people that are able to speak and hear but when it comes to those who are not able to hear and speak, they use these gestures to express their daily life common greetings. A powerful deep neural network then deciphers these treasures, translating them into spoken language or text in real-time, allowing sign language to flow freely from hands to eyes. Unlike a static dictionary, this dynamic system has not only one but six different gestures or human greetings which helps you to expand your knowledge and get a grip on the sing language detection using Deep Learning.

title: SignChatAI-Generative AI for Deaf-and-Mute Community using Indian Sign Language(ISL)
venue: 2024 International Conference on Computing and Intelligent Reality Technologies (ICCIRT)
abstract: SignChatAI is a advanced generative AI chatbot aimed at revolutionizing communication for deaf-and-mute individuals in India through the use of Indian Sign Language (ISL). This paper addresses the need for advanced communication solutions that facilitate interactions between the deaf community and hearing individuals, thereby fostering inclusivity. By equipping deaf-and-mute individuals with this AI-driven communication assistant, SignChatAI aims to create a more inclusive society, where users can communicate freely and confidently. This initiative aims to improve the quality of life for its users and promote participation in social, educational, and professional environments. Overall, our proposed SignChatAI represents a significant advancement in bridging the communication gaps and promote equitable opportunities for interaction within the deaf-and-mute community.

title: SignEnd: An Indian Sign Language Assistant
venue: 2022 IEEE Region 10 Symposium (TENSYMP)
abstract: Communication is an essential day-to-day activity that human society thrives on. Indian Sign Language (ISL) is one form of oral communication among the deaf-mute community in India. As the general public usually tends to be unaware of this form of interaction, daily conversations are strenuous for a deaf-mute person. Previously created systems focus on detecting alpha-numeric signs pertaining to users with five fingers solely. This paper describes an ISL system that can recognize the alpha-numeric hand signs of its users with five and six fingers and translate them into their corresponding text equivalences. A custom dataset is created that explicitly tailors to these requirements. Additionally, this system can convert entered text (letter, number, word, sentence) into corresponding sign equivalences. Sign-to-Text conversion is achieved by using Mediapipe-Hands Machine Learning (ML) model to detect hand signs for deaf-mute people with five fingers. Similarly, an Object Detection Application Programming Interface (API) is implemented to detect hand signs for users with six fingers. Presently, the proposed system has an average accuracy of 90 percent.

title: Signer-Independent Indian Sign Language Recognition Via Deep Vision Transformers
venue: 2026 5th OPJU International Technology Conference (OTCON) on Smart Computing for Innovation and Advancement in Industry 5.0
abstract: Real-time sign language recognition and translation systems can often suffer from degraded performance when exposed to new, unseen signers due to differences in hand morphology, skin tone, motion dynamics, and the style of signing. These challenges severely limit the ability to deploy the system across heterogeneous user populations. In this work, we propose a signer-independent, real-time Indian Sign Language recognition and translation framework, which translates gestures directly into text and speech. The proposed architecture integrates pose-based skeletal feature extraction along with appearance normalization with adversarial feature disentanglement and spatiotemporal Transformer modelling to facilitate robust generalization across diverse signers. Our architecture uses a dual-stream input: a pose stream, encoding geometric motion as hand, facial, and upper body key points, while an appearance stream captures the non-manual cues from RGB frames. The extensive data augmentation and adaptive normalization mimic the signer diversity of the real world. Moreover, a gradient reversal adversarial branch adds invariance to the signer identity of the learned embeddings. It is further enhanced by the contrastive loss function, which aligns the representations of identical signs across subjects. The core neural architecture is based on a spatiotemporal Transformer encoder decoder that decodes the sequential features into textual glosses, synthesized into speech using a TTS module. Extensive experimental evaluation on strictly signerindependent protocols demonstrates superior recognition accuracy, robustness to visual variation, and low latency in inference, therefore underlining the framework for real-world applications in inclusive communication for the Deaf and Hardof-Hearing community.

title: SignFlow: Multilingual ISL Paragraph Translator with Virtual Assistant
venue: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Computation-Based Sensor Application (ICAIQSA)
abstract: Effective communication between the hearing-impaired community and the wider population is often hindered by limited understanding of Indian Sign Language (ISL).Current systems are usually only able to recognize single words or sentences; they are unable to process continuous gestures and produce outputs that make sense. This research presents SignFlow, a real-time multilingual ISL paragraph translator with an integrated virtual assistant. The system recognizes sequential ISL gestures from webcam input, creates coherent English paragraphs, and translates them into Hindi and Marathi using computer vision techniques (MediaPipe Hand Landmarks, Dynamic Time Warping, LSTM) and natural language processing. To ensure accessibility across various modalities, outputs are offered in speech, text, and captions. Sign-to-sign Q&A is further made possible by an interactive assistant, which improves usability and inclusivity. testing demonstrates >87% gesture recognition accuracy with low-latency performance, validating the feasibility of deploying such systems in real-world communication, education, and healthcare contexts. Future work aims to expand vocabulary, integrate larger ISL datasets, and support additional regional languages for broader accessibility.

title: SignGlass: First-Person View Comprehensive and Generalizable ASL Translation Using Wearable Glass
venue: Proceedings of the 38th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
abstract: Communication barriers between Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) individuals and hearing individuals remain a major challenge, highlighting the need for technologies that enable seamless sign language interpretation. However, current American Sign Language (ASL) recognition and translation systems face key limitations, including poor portability, complex usage settings, incomplete capture of essential components, and weak generalization, reducing practicality and user acceptance. To address these challenges, we present SignGlass, the first smart glasses equipped with three wearable cameras for comprehensive capture of both manual and non-manual ASL markers, supported by advanced algorithms for real-time recognition and translation into English. Specifically, SignGlass integrates a jitter-aware spatio-temporal attention mechanism for robust recognition of hand movement patterns. Complementing this, a dual-camera, temporally-aware facial module captures the subtle facial expressions essential for ASL comprehension. To support diverse signing styles across individuals, we further introduce a cascaded data augmentation strategy to improve model generalization. In a user study with 14 Deaf participants, SignGlass achieved high translation accuracy and was well-received, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging communication gaps. This work highlights the promise of multi-camera wearable systems in advancing ASL translation and promoting more accessible communication.

title: SigNify: A Camera-Based Device for Interpreting Filipino Sign Language
venue: 2025 IEEE Integrated STEM Education Conference (ISEC)
abstract: SigNify aims to aid the communication barrier between the deaf and the non-deaf individuals in the Philippines. In addition, there is a scarcity of Filipino Sign-Language interpreters, our camera-based device serves as an alternative. SigNify is a camera-based device that can interpret Filipino Sign Language with a sign-to-speech feature to deliver the message. It is powered by a Raspberry Pi 5 and a Raspberry Pi camera.

title: SignParser: Empowering Dual-Handed Sign Language Translation with a Single Wearable
venue: IEEE INFOCOM 2025 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications
abstract: Sign language translation (SLT) is essential for promoting communicative equity and social integration for hearing-impaired individuals. However, computer-vision-based and wireless-signal-based SLT solutions mainly involve inconvenient operation, poor portability, and susceptibility to interference. Recently, wearable-device-based methods have emerged as a potential alternative, offering services anytime and anywhere. However, these methods fall into two extremes: employing complex device combinations to achieve dual-handed SLT or opting for single-device solutions that compromise comprehensive data capture from both hands. Consequently, such a dilemma constrains the widespread adoption of wearable devices in the field of SLT. In this paper, we propose SignParser, a unique dual-handed SLT system leveraging a single IMU sensor in commercial smartwatches. SignParser is superior to other wearable-device-based approaches in i) exploiting large-scale labeled virtual IMU data to achieve generalization capability across different users, ii) enabling single-device solution for dual-handed SLT via estimating non-dominant hand IMU data, and iii) ensuring real-time, contextual-guided, and unseen sentence-adaptive SLT by a lightweight sign spotter network integrated with large language models. Extensive experiments with 27 participants show that SignParser can achieve the average word error rate of 4.8% and 8.3% for new users and unseen sentences, respectively. The excellent performance demonstrates the SignParser's effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

title: Signvoice – Sign and Speech Communication Web Application
venue: 2025 International Conference on Data Science and Business Systems (ICDSBS)
abstract: This study has proposed a real-time web-based communication system that aims to bridge the communication gap between deaf and dumb people and the hearing population. It has two main modules. The first module is the speech to text module, which translates the spoken language into the text and generates the images for each letter of the spoken words. The second module is the sign language recognition module, which captures the hand signs from a live video feed and translates the same into text. This system uses WebRTC for live video communication and WebSockets for real-time data transfer, so that the communication can be in real-time. The backend is built with FastAPI, so that it can process the audio input and relay the text and the images to the frontend. CNN is used to identify and translate sign language motions. The frontend is built with React.js, so that it can provide real-time voice and sign processing and an easy user interface. This system is built in such a way that it is cheap, can run on any platform, and is completely independent from the database and other paid services, and it can operate only in English. The system has been tested and it has been found that it has higher accuracy, lower latency, and real-time adaptation, so it can improve the accessibility of communication for everyone.

title: SignXchange System
venue: 2023 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: An extensive communication hole among speech and hearing impaired people and different people exists, and it's crucial that this hole be closed. The accuracy of hardware gloves which use sensors are very low. The present records uses convolutional neural network models to increase the accuracy. The scope was limited and the data sets were not diverse, thus a new diversified data set was made and the model was further enhanced. The new model can anticipate practically every letter with a very high degree of accuracy. We expanded our data set with a number of additional gestures that included various hand gestures. This model has enormous promise since, given the right data, it can decipher every gesture used in a variety of sign languages. The data-set can be further customized by the user by adding other motions. Additionally, the information is delivered to a program that will turn the received hand gesture into text. The technology is bidirectional, meaning that text may also be translated into sign language, in order to close the communication gap. First the hand gesture is given as the input and transformed to text, response of the other user for that is given as text and it is taken directly as the input and translated to the appropriate gesture in accordance with the practical sign language.

title: SilentCare: A Trust-Aware and Explainable AI Companion for Mental Health Support Through Adaptive Multichannel Dialogue Management
venue: 2025 10th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Using natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, and machine learning technologies, a comprehensive chatbot system named SilentCare was developed. The technical architecture of SilentCare includes and integrates speech-to-text components, realtime sign language recognition through gesture-based CNNs, emotion scrutiny using an enhanced LSTM model, and multilingual text reception for optimal interaction with the user. Assistive technologies tend to emphasize facilitating the disabled and mute limbs through singular interfaces, often neglecting the comprehensive requprw.microsoft.com/emotional-mental-health-careservices for the deaf and mute, mental health support, and other specialized services. SilentCare utilizes multimodal representations including texts, audio, sign languages, and customized healthcare services using emotional sentiment analysis to fill the void left by other technologies [1], [14]. A new LSTM-based emotion recognition algorithm that offers real-time accuracy and response speed in low-resource environments has been proposed. Compared to traditional models, SilentCare outperformed in emotional intent classification and user satisfaction evaluation, thus advancing the boundaries and scope of accessible assistive communication technologies.

title: SiMoS: Sistema para monitoramento de plataformas de poços de petróleo através de dispositivos móveis
venue: 2010 9th IEEE/IAS International Conference on Industry Applications - INDUSCON 2010
abstract: The popularization of the Web and the advent of new information and communication technologies of mobile devices make possible new aspects for management, interaction and information sharing. In petroliferous area, monitoring systems on mobile devices have been used for process optimization, data monitoring, reporting, alarm generation and identification of failures in real-time on oil wells platforms. However, there are few systems that identify efficiently problems due the fact they do not use techniques of real-time systems. This paper proposes the new system, SiMoS, a real-time system for remote monitoring oil wells platforms through mobile devices.

title: Simple Digitizing Circuit for Resistive Sensors in π-Network Form
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This article presents a detailed discussion on the design and performance verification of a digitizing circuit for a special type of resistive sensor—the resistive  $\pi $ -network model. The proposed circuit digitizes the output without requiring an additional analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and boasts several positive features, such as a simple architecture with a single reference voltage, wide-range measurements, and good linearity. Moreover, the circuit can measure the input quantity independent of sensor elements and a few other error sources. The article clearly explains the working mechanism of the circuit and examines the impact of dominant error sources. Furthermore, it details the circuit’s performance through simulation and experimental studies. The maximum measured nonlinearity is lower than 0.14% for a range of 40 dB. This demonstrates the linearizing capability of the circuit for a wide range of inputs.

title: Simple experiment integration into modular online laboratory enviroment
venue: 2017 4th Experiment@International Conference (exp.at'17)
abstract: The paper contributes to the area of remote laboratories. It describes an implementation of a particular remote laboratory system and reviews its design and key features. The paper discusses several adopted technologies and the motivation behind their use. To emphasize the advantages of a modular remote laboratory application, the paper illustrates the process of adding a new remote experiment by connecting a real device to the system. This process is broken down into several steps and each is explained in more detail. The paper concludes with a rundown of other additional features which increase the overall user-friendliness of this web application.

title: Simplified Digitizing Interface-Architectures for Three-Wire Connected Resistive Sensors: Design and Comprehensive Evaluation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This article describes the design, analysis, and performance verification of simple digitizing interfaces for different types of three-wire resistive sensors. The proposed interface uses an efficient resistance-to-time conversion technique that charges an internal capacitor, between two reference levels, through selected resistive-sensor paths. A simple analog circuit controlled using a digital timing unit realizes the aforementioned technique. This approach is adaptable for various resistive sensor configurations and does not depend on the effect of connecting wire resistances and various other non-ideal parameters (e.g., threshold voltage and pin resistance of microcontroller, offset voltage of comparator, etc.). In addition, the proposed schemes utilize its digital unit (e.g., microcontroller) only for control and timing operations, thus saving on power. The detailed working principle of the proposed interfaces and their error analysis are discussed in the article. Later, performance verification is carried out using simulation as well as emulation studies. These studies clearly show that the presented digitizing interfaces provide linear digital transfer characteristics with maximum nonlinearity of 0.17% and wire resistance compensation. Further, tests are conducted with various remotely located commercial sensors. The outcomes of these studies are reported and compared with the state-of-the-art works.

title: Simulated Ensemble Performance Partners: Exploring the Integration of Generative AI and Virtual Reality for Collaborative Rehearsals
venue: Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing
abstract: Ensemble musical performances demand both technical precision — such as exact fingerings, intonation, and tempo—as well as higher-order skills such as active listening, real-time responsiveness, and emotional expression. This study explored the ways that generative AI and VR could be used to facilitate this complex interplay of cognitive and expressive demands. We conducted a needs-finding pilot study with four advanced viola students who rehearsed in a gallery-style virtual concert hall accompanied by a smartphone-based AI partner. Post-rehearsal interviews underwent thematic analysis to identify key system requirements for simulating an effective ensemble partner. Three core needs emerged: (1) faithful interpretation of score arrangements to support expressive nuance, (2) adaptive sensory feedback to enhance VR immersion, and (3) pre-rehearsal exchange of emotional intent. The insights gained in this study could guide the development of AI/VR systems aimed at augmenting ensemble practice, supporting iterative rehearsal in immersive environments that complement human musicianship.

title: Simulation environment for investigating crowd-sensing based urban parking
venue: 2015 International Conference on Models and Technologies for Intelligent Transportation Systems (MT-ITS)
abstract: This paper introduces a simulation environment developed for analyzing crowd-sensing based applications in the Smart City application domain. As a case study, an urban parking application scenario is investigated and presented. In this scenario, smart citizens collect and share parking related events, such as leaving or occupying a free parking spot. These events can be presented on a real-time city map and used in navigation software, thereby helping others alleviate parking related issues, such as the time spent while cruising for parking. The simulation environment, implemented in Java, allows to investigate and assess the critical user base of crowd-sensing based smart city applications, and the requisites (benefits, challenges) of introducing such applications. Our simulation results show that considerable gain (approx. 15%) can be achieved in the cruising time even with relatively low (30%) user base in a medium size city (Novi Sad, Serbia). Moreover, the proposed simulation environment can be used also in real field measurements by replacing/extending input data from real users.

title: Simulation Model of a Railway Crossing for Capacity Evaluation
venue: 2022 Systems of Signal Synchronization, Generating and Processing in Telecommunications (SYNCHROINFO)
abstract: In this paper, a simulation model for estimating the capacity of a regulated railway crossing at the same level as a highway is developed and its results are compared with a mathematical model. The mathematical model is a single-channel queuing system with an unreliable device. The simulation model is constructed using a graphical interpretation of real objects and their geographical reference. The study of the capacity of railway crossings at the same level will reduce the formation of congestion before crossings, reduce the statistics of road accidents at crossings and ensure optimal distribution of traffic flows along routes. The result of the work is a method of translating abstract mathematical concepts into real physical units.

title: Simulation of PKI-enabled communication for identity management using CyberCIEGE
venue: 2010 - MILCOM 2010 MILITARY COMMUNICATIONS CONFERENCE
abstract: CyberCIEGE is a sophisticated network security simulation packaged as a video game and used by educators around the world to enhance information assurance education and training at universities, community colleges, within the DoD, and in other government agencies. The CyberCIEGE game engine was recently expanded to include Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) features including certification authorities, selection of installed roots and cross certification. CyberCIEGE Virtual Private Network (VPN) gateways, VPN clients and email clients were then extended to incorporate the new PKI features. CyberCIEGE PKI abstractions are described in terms of player configuration choices and the consequences of these choices on network management and vulnerabilities. The CyberCIEGE game engine modifications include modeling of chains of trust and risks of cross certification schemes. The benefits of these enhancements include coherent integration of identity management technologies, ranging from the human interface through to the supporting distributed infrastructure, into scenarios. Benefits also include support for recent new scenarios focused on the PKI infrastructure, identity management, or both; and the ability to tie both identity management and PKI to concepts of identification, authentication, provenance, and access control.

title: Simulation of speech by identifying and classifying dynamic gestures
venue: 2015 International Conference on Smart Technologies and Management for Computing, Communication, Controls, Energy and Materials (ICSTM)
abstract: A reliable system which identifies the gestures of sign language is currently non-existent. Most common alternative for these speech and hearing impaired people is the utilization of an interpreter who voices out their opinions as these underprivileged people make gestures. Although there are devices such as Text to Speech Converters and Speech Generating Devices, they are restricted by their absence of speed which mostly results in prerecorded speeches being simulated rather than real time speeches. With the need for a system that processes gestures in real time for deployment in environments like auditoriums and classrooms being justified, the system under proposal hopes to achieve the same. To bring about such a system with an acceptable level of accuracy, the current proposal advocates the utilization of Microsoft Kinect, a depth sensor, introduced initially for entertainment purposes like gaming but now being deployed in large various industrial and medical applications after its game changing potential has been spotted. For identifying gestures in real time, the proposed system utilizes context specific and trigger based mapping for identifying dynamic gestures in real time.

title: Simulation workshop and remote laboratory: two Web-based training approaches for control
venue: Proceedings of the 2000 American Control Conference. ACC (IEEE Cat. No.00CH36334)
abstract: This paper presents two Web-based training approaches carried out at the Control Laboratory of Grenoble on a classical "ball and beam" experiment. This experiment allows comparing the effects of different digital controllers (PD, PID, RST) either with respect to set point changes or to disturbances. It shows, in special cases, an interesting feature due to a negative zero cancellation, giving rise to an oscillatory control signal. This experiment is simulated within a highly interactive Web-based workshop. It is also accessible remotely thanks to an Wincon-assisted Simulink-based real-time controller. The first part of the paper presents the complementary pedagogical aspects and the user possibilities of the two Web-training tools: the simulation workshop and the remote access system. The second part describes the software/hardware design of the two environments. Finally, examples of practical use of the two network-based training tools at the National Polytechnic Institute of Grenoble are presented and future developments are discussed.

title: Simulation-Based Analysis of an IoT-Enabled Dynamic Tolling System for Intelligent Urban Traffic Management
venue: 2025 IEEE Colombian Caribbean Conference (C3)
abstract: Urban traffic congestion is an increasing global concern with serious socioeconomic and environmental implications. Traditional toll systems, based on static pricing and physical toll booths, are insufficient to manage dynamic traffic conditions and often exacerbate congestion during peak hours. This paper proposes an IoT-enabled dynamic tolling system designed to adjust rates in real time based on vehicle density and traffic flow, aiming to improve road efficiency. The system architecture relies on traffic data collected from virtual sensors integrated within a SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) environment, managed via the TraCI interface. Through a digital twin model, various tolling strategies are simulated under different traffic scenarios, and their impact on vehicle performance, waiting times, and emissions is analyzed. The results demonstrate that dynamic tolling significantly reduces congestion levels compared to static pricing schemes, validating the effectiveness of the proposed system. This study provides a replicable simulation framework for evaluating intelligent transportation policies prior to realworld implementation.

title: SimulSense: Sense-Driven Interpreting for Efficient Simultaneous Speech Translation
venue: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: How to make human-interpreter-like read/write decisions for simultaneous speech translation (SimulST) systems? Current state-of-the-art systems formulate SimulST as a multi-turn dialogue task, requiring specialized interleaved training data and relying on computationally expensive large language model (LLM) inference for decision-making. In this paper, we propose SimulSense, a novel framework for SimulST that mimics human interpreters by continuously reading input speech and triggering write decisions to produce translation when a new sense unit is perceived. Experiments against two state-of-the-art baseline systems demonstrate that our proposed method achieves a superior quality-latency tradeoff and substantially improved real-time efficiency, where its decision-making is up to 9.6× faster than the baselines.

title: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping for Forest Harvesters
venue: Proceedings 2007 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
abstract: A real-time SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) approach to harvester localization and tree map generation in forest environments is presented in this paper. The method combines 2D laser localization and mapping with GPS information to form global tree maps. Building an incremental map while also using it for localization is the only way a mobile robot can navigate in large outdoor environments. Until recently SLAM has only been confined to small-scale, mostly indoor, environments. We try to addresses the issues of scale for practical implementations of SLAM in extensive outdoor environments. Presented algorithms are tested in real outdoor environments using an all-terrain vehicle equipped with the navigation sensors and a DGPS receiver.

title: Simultaneous Multiple Cameras Monitoring and Streaming Based on Auto-layout and Analyzer
venue: 2022 3rd International Conference on Big Data, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Engineering (ICBAIE)
abstract: This paper provides a novel implementation method to develop a simultaneous monitor and visual streaming toolkit for multiple cameras. The implementation of the research of this paper uses the four main libraries to implement: FFmpeg, OpenCV, PIL and Tkinter. This streaming toolkit can implement the visible monitoring and streaming for multiple cameras simultaneously. Moverover, this streaming toolkit can achieve the function of arranging the visual display layout windows of multiple cameras. The inside interpreter of this streaming toolkit can intelligently analyze the input text of the streaming URL string and find out the correct protocol for camera streaming. Furthermore, enough experiments have been taken to test the monitoring and streaming performance and efficiency of this toolkit. This monitoring and streaming toolkit is able to gain the multimedia equipment information of the computer and make the corresponding configuration.

title: Simultaneous Trajectory Optimization and Force Control with Soft Contact Mechanics
venue: 2020 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
abstract: Force modulation of robotic manipulators has been extensively studied for several decades but is not yet commonly used in safety-critical applications due to a lack of accurate interaction contact modeling and weak performance guarantees - a large proportion of them concerning the modulation of interaction forces. This study presents a high-level framework for simultaneous trajectory optimization and force control of the interaction between manipulator and soft environments. Sliding friction and normal contact force are taken into account. The dynamics of the soft contact model and the manipulator dynamics are simultaneously incorporated in a trajectory optimizer to generate desired motion and force profiles. A constrained optimization framework based on Differential Dynamic Programming and Alternative Direction Method of Multipliers has been employed to generate optimal control inputs and high-dimensional state trajectories. Experimental validation of the model performance is conducted on a soft substrate with known material properties using a Cartesian space force control mode. Results show a comparison of ground truth and predicted model based contact force states for multiple Cartesian motions and the validity range of the friction model. The proposed high-level planning has the potential to be leveraged for medical tasks involving manipulation of compliant, delicate, and deformable tissues.

title: SiPhyR: An End-to-End Learning-Based Optimization Framework for Dynamic Grid Reconfiguration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: Distribution grids are rapidly transforming with increasing penetration of distributed renewable generation, storage, and electric vehicles. These devices introduce new dynamic signatures including intermittency and changing demand patterns. To maintain a safe and reliable power grid, new operating paradigms are required for fast and accurate decision making. It is in this regard that we leverage machine learning for grid operations. We propose SiPhyR, a physics-informed machine learning framework that accomplishes end-to-end learning-based optimization for distribution grid reconfiguration. The reconfiguration problem optimizes the topology of the grid and power flows from distributed devices to reduce line losses, improve voltage profiles, and increase renewable energy utilization. To address the computational complexities of NP-hardness of binary decision variables, we propose a physics-informed rounding approach that explicitly embeds discrete decisions into an end-to-end differentiable framework. This enables Grid-SiPhyR to learn to simultaneously optimize grid topology and generator dispatch with certified satisfiability of safety-critical constraints. Our results are shown on three canonical distribution grids.

title: SketchAI: A "Sketch-First" Approach to Incorporating Generative AI into Fashion Design
venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
abstract: Generative AI technologies are increasingly being incorporated into creativity support tools. However, most generative AI tools rely on text-based prompting, requiring users to translate visual ideas into linguistic descriptions. This approach is misaligned with the sketch-driven workflows of creative professionals. To address this gap, we introduce SketchAI, a novel sketch-first interface for diffusion models that allows practitioners to use real-time sketching on a tablet computer to guide model outputs. Through a qualitative study with 29 fashion design apprentices, we explored the interface’s potential impacts on creative workflows. While some participants identified use cases where SketchAI streamlined routine tasks, others expressed concerns about its potential to undermine creative agency and exploration. These findings unearthed hidden complexity: while generative AI can support some aspects of creativity, its core capabilities may challenge the central identity of creative practitioners. While SketchAI does not resolve this problem, it does take a meaningful step towards reconciliation.

title: SkillNet: Human Actions Assessment via Human-AI Collaboration
venue: ACM Trans. Multimedia Comput. Commun. Appl.
abstract: Intelligent human motion analysis is essential for developing next-generation IoT and AR/VR systems that enable automated, interpretable, and fine-grained performance assessment. Motivated by the need for real-time, explainable, and transferable skill evaluation, we propose a wearable sensing framework to assess human performance by tracking skill progression and minimizing injury risk. We use live badminton gameplay and workout exercises as representative use cases, where motion dynamics, postural stability, and limb coordination are critical to success. Both activities demand optimal posture and synchronized limb movements, while improper actions or suboptimal technique can lead to decreased performance and higher injury susceptibility. We introduce SkillNet, a multi-task learning framework that extracts shared representations across all limbs while preserving limb-specific motion signatures. The architecture employs task-specific regressors to detect subtle inter-limb dissimilarities and distinctive traits, enabling collective inference in a body sensor network (BSN) environment. To holistically measure performance, we formulated a weighted performance indicator (PI) that fuses AI-driven scoring with domain-expert evaluations, providing a robust metric for both qualitative and quantitative assessment. We evaluate SkillNet on three diverse datasets Badminton Activity Recognition (BAR), Multi-Modalities Dataset of Sports (MMDOS), and Daily and Sports Activities (DSADS) capturing a broad spectrum of motion types and skill intensities. Results show that SkillNet achieves an R ({

title: SkyMedic:The Lifesaving Autonomous Ducted UAV
venue: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: "SkyMedic: The Lifesaving Autonomous Ducted Drone" represents a groundbreaking innovation in the field of emergency medical response and aerial technology. This autonomous drone has been meticulously designed to cater to medical emergencies by swiftly and safely delivering vital supplies and medical assistance to remote or hard-to-reach locations. Equipped with advanced ducted propulsion, the drone ensures enhanced stability, agility, and safety during its operations. The core objectives of SkyMedic are to provide rapid response times during emergencies, enhance the efficiency of medical aid delivery, and bridge the gap in critical healthcare services. This abstract outlines the key features and capabilities of the SkyMedic drone, highlighting its robust and versatile design, autonomous flight capabilities, and payload delivery systems. Furthermore, it discusses the potential impact of this innovative technology in saving lives during critical medical emergencies, disaster relief efforts, and challenging rescue operations. SkyMedic’s integration of cutting-edge technologies, such as obstacle avoidance systems, real-time monitoring, and medical payload compatibility, ensures that it can effectively navigate complex environments and deliver essential medical supplies with precision. The autonomy of the drone minimizes human error and response time, ultimately improving the chances of survival for patients in need.

title: SKYNET: A platform for maximizing career opportunities
venue: 2021 4th Biennial International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Professional networking interfaces provide a significantly improved exposure and likelihood of job opportunities as well as career-related resources. Multiple availability of such platforms lead to a lack of standardization and thereby can result in a false sense of security. A massive profile pool has also statistically incremented the probability of overlooking suited candidate profiles at a global level. This paper presents a university-level individualized professional networking platform - SKYNET for enhanced prospects of job acquisition. SKYNET proved to be a successful amalgamation between career and academia which fundamentally aims on facilitating an enhanced job recommendation system based on individual professional skills. It is a Web application that smoothens the process of hiring and significantly improves an individual's chance of securing jobs and internships. It helps students to get a reality check to see where they stand among their peers as well, considering various parameters such as certifications and work experience. It will provide a customized preview of student and company profiles based on needed skills and expertise. The corresponding system also supports ranking and filtration based on the job profile and description which was achieved by a custom-designed algorithm. Results helped not only student candidates to find internships and jobs while pursuing primitive professional education which helped them work in a professional setting and apply the grasped knowledge in real-time. Furthermore, made it simple for collaborating recruiters to pick the perfect student-job-role match in a timely manner.

title: SLIT: Achieving Fast Bandwidth Isolation Across Virtual Machines
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
abstract: Network performance guarantee in the cloud is one of the hottest research topics recently. However, current approaches either lack scalability or fail to achieve high performance. To avoid the hard tradeoff between the scalability and performance, we adopt a hybrid approach to get the best of both worlds. In this paper, we follow the stateless design principle and propose SLIT, which provides fast VM-level network performance isolation and maintains core-stateless characteristics. Specifically, at the end host, we develop a novel network-adaptive labeling mechanism and it computes the correct scheduling priority for each hop. At the switch, packets are scheduled based on their labels and we develop a novel straggler detection algorithm to find the new incoming flow. Our evaluation results show that SLIT can approximate the optimal performance of Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ) effectively.

title: SLRMPCMC: Sign Language Recognition using Mediapipe and Cross-model Comparison
venue: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computing Technologies (ICEECT)
abstract: Sign language is key for the deaf or hearing-impaired, but traditional reliance on interpreters presents limitations in both availability and precision. Historical methods for sign translation faced unique challenges from the visual-spatial aspects of sign languages, often failing to accurately recognize gestures or adapt to varying contexts and necessitating instant translation. This caused constraints in usability and hindered the application on diverse platforms such as mobile devices due to high computational requirements. This research introduces a sophisticated framework for sign language recognition, integrating the Mediapipe Landmark system with ab combination of machine learning models—Long Short-Term Memory networks, Convolutional Neural Networks, and Random Forest— to enhance the precision of detecting hand signs and movements in real-time and across different settings. The study outlines the processes for data gathering, preprocessing, and classifying gestures and static signs, advancing communication technologies for those with hearing impairments.

title: Smart Aquaponics with Disease Detection
venue: 2019 Conference on Next Generation Computing Applications (NextComp)
abstract: The vision of the Mauritian's Ministry of Agro- Industry and Food security is to further develop the agricultural sector and to promote the agro-industry by focusing on safety, supply, quality, innovation and new technologies. This research work attempts to develop a smart aquaponics system that combines conventional aquaculture with hydroponics. The system uses the Internet of Things to continuously sense and control the environment and to provide real-time feedback and alerts to the owner through a mobile application. It features a camera surveillance system that enables live streaming of the aquaponics setup and also allows for further image processing. Through the captured images, the system performs leaf recognition identifying the type of the leaf. Moreover, the system also performs disease detection that identifies if the leaf, and consequently the plant, is suffering from a specific disease. If the system detects a disease, it automatically generates a report which is sent to the owner through the mobile application. The prototype has been tested and looks very promising. We hope that this work paves the way towards a smart aquaponics system that detects, identifies and notifies the owner of possible diseases at early stage before their propagation.

title: Smart Assistive Platform for the Visually Impaired
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Our project aims to enhance web accessibility for visually impaired people by developing an educational platform with an integrated virtual assistant. This application helps the visually impaired students to read the content and access the website without any third-party help. The virtual assistant helps users explore the website efficiently, provides explanations of concepts, and assists with on-site navigation. In addition, this virtual assistant allows the users to retrieve the real-time information beyond the website. This feature helps the visually impaired students to access the current global information effortlessly. Additionally, this platform ensures independent learning by implementing the text-to-speech conversion to read the educational content and also the content beyond the website. By integrating these features, our project expands digital accessibility, empowering visually impaired students to explore educational materials and stay informed with ease.

title: Smart assistive system for laborers
venue: ​Smart Cities Symposium 2018
abstract: A smart assistive system for laborers is designed and built with a novel integrated three-fold objective. First, it provides workers in excessively hot conditions with some head cooling comfort. Second, it monitors the workers' health state via his/her heart pulse rate. Third, and in case of danger or emergency, it allows the supervisor to communicate with and locate the worker in distress. Towards this goal, a standard helmet was retro-fitted with a heat sink and a Peltier device both lined for a better thermal insulation and uniform head cooling. Two Java-based mobile applications were developed, one for the worker, the other for the supervisor. The former monitors the worker's position and his/her heart rate every 30 seconds and sends this information in real time to the supervisor's mobile application via Google's Fire base Realtime database. An Arduino microcontroller is used to interface the heart sensor and the Peltier unit to the worker's mobile application. If the heart rate is found to be out of safe bounds (pre-set by the supervisor), an alarm message is triggered in both applications and a direct communication is attempted between both parties. In case of failure, the worker's location may be displayed by the supervisor using Google Map for rescue purposes. With an initial cost estimated at $50, the potential benefits of this prototype system were successfully tested achieving a cooling difference of about 4 degrees between the worker's head and the ambient temperature. With a custom-made helmet and outfit design involving a more efficient thermal insulation and a cooler unit, the merits of this smart system may be extended to higher levels of safety and comfort contributing to a smarter working environment in cities.

title: Smart Attendance System using RFID and Raspberry Pi
venue: 2023 Second International Conference on Electronics and Renewable Systems (ICEARS)
abstract: Attendance is most important in schools, colleges and also in workplaces. In schools, colleges and educational institutions, attendance plays an important role. In educational institutions attendance is used to monitor student activity. Attendance is a key parameter which needs to be monitored which helps in visualizing the student progress in academics in day-to-day life. Attendance is helpful for parents who may notice their child going only to schools or college. In work places attendance plays a key role which enhances the work schedule and determines the workload of the employee and the contribution of the employee in his work. It is very mandatory to decide the salary of the employee based on the number of days he has worked. Logging down the attendance in institutions level is done by instructors, who are responsible to take attendance in each lecture hour. This mark down of attendance on an hourly basis is basically tedious work. In some academic regulations loss of attendance due to manual errors may result in mark reduction or attendance shortage may recorded. To automate the process of logging attendance in an autonomous way, this study has designed an efficient solution to log attendance each and every lecture hour without the intervention of the course instructor. The proposed system helps the educational institutions and instructors to focus on the academics rather than logging attendance manually.

title: Smart cafe system implementation
venue: 2016 3rd International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development (INDIACom)
abstract: With the growing speed of advancement of technology, Smart phones have essentially become important part of our lives. The functionality of smartphones is similar to that of a personal computer. Most of the people own a smartphone nowadays because of the fact that it can be easily used, easily understood has wide variety of applications for various purposes. The android environment is highly popular and useful nowadaysand provides the developers with a large platform accompanied by large number of options. The interface provided by eclipse IDE with ADT or Android Studio for the development of android app is very easy to use and since it is open source, many new developers are trying their hand in order to develop apps of real time use to humans. Also, since the Android programming is based on Java language, it is relatively simple and easily understood than C or C++.

title: Smart campus service link: Adaptation and interaction planes for campus and university environments
venue: 2017 8th IEEE International Conference on Cognitive Infocommunications (CogInfoCom)
abstract: Our research group has started to design and develop an application which holds the most important attributes for today's world like intelligence, adaptation and extensibility. The base idea behind this work (which is called by us as Smart Campus) is to help, improve and ease the everyday tasks and communication between students and instructors in a University environment. The proposed distributed and layered architecture exposing all the necessary features (scalability and extensibility) to achieve its goals. We have followed the proper standards, recommendations and protocols during the design phase. The primary requirements are based on the functionalities which are missing or need to be improved in our University's Campus. Our result is a system which provides real-time interaction between its users and integrates the most important external data sources to support its users using services in a cloud environment.

title: Smart Communication Aid: An AI-Driven Sign Language Converter using ASR and NLP
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computing and Data Science (ICCDS)
abstract: Hearing-impaired individuals often struggle to communicate effectively with those who can speak, leading to a significant communication gap in daily life. Previous solutions, such as text-based applications or human interpreters, have presented various challenges, including slow processing, dependency on another person, or ineffective representation of sign language. To address this issue, this research introduces a Text and Speech-to-Sign Language Converter that instantly translates written text or spoken words into sign language. The system first accepts input in the form of text or speech. If speech is provided, Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) converts it into text. Then, a Natural Language Processing (NLP) model processes the text and translates it into corresponding sign language gestures. These gestures are displayed through an animated character, making communication more interactive and accessible. A key feature of this project is the integration of a Kaggle dataset containing animated signs, ensuring clarity and accuracy in sign representation. Unlike previous methods, this system operates autonomously in real time without requiring human assistance. It has broad applications in schools, hospitals, public spaces, and daily interactions, significantly enhancing accessibility for individuals with hearing impairments and promoting their inclusion in society.

title: Smart Connect: An AI-Based Platform for Daily Wage Job Matching
venue: 2026 International Conference on Innovative Computing, Intelligent Communication and Smart Electrical Systems (ICSES)
abstract: AI-Based Platform For Daily Wage Job Matching helps to recommend the worker to the client based on the requirement of the client. Today, any of the educated people struggle to get a job. This idea is mainly focused on unemployed daily wage workers getting jobs from the surroundings. The job involves work like plumbing, electric work, and others. Small businesses in their relative location. This project is aimed at connecting the people and wage workers without a third-party involvement. So, there are no broker charges. This improves the revenue of the worker. This project helps customers to find the employee based on the recruitment they post in the application. Our technique helps to recommend employees by matching the customer's work needs. This also ensures the security to authenticate the client and the worker. This works by verifying the information of the worker, like certification and government IDs. This ensures the safety of both worker and client. The client can also track the worker using the GPS from their home or any other place from their mobile at the assigned date and time of the work if the worker allows. After the work is done by the worker, that customer can post a review, feedback, and a rating for the worker. This is the feedback system; other people can easily reach the review and rating through the feedback without any cheats. This ensures development of the trust between the worker and employee. It also ensures the satisfaction of the client and customer.

title: Smart Dashboard for Water Quality Monitoring and Predicting in Koi Fish Farming Using IoT and Sarima Modeling
venue: 2024 12th International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICoICT)
abstract: Maintaining optimal water quality is critical for ensuring healthy growth and minimizing mortality rates in koi fish farming. This study develops a smart dashboard system using IoT sensor data to monitor and predict key water quality parameters, specifically pH levels, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), and temperature. The Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model is utilized to analyze data collected from April 1st to April 30th, 2024, capturing seasonal variations. Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) tests confirm the data's stationarity, validating the accuracy of the models. SARIMA(1,0,1)(1,0,1)[S] is selected as optimal due to minimal seasonal influence. The dataset is allocated into 80% for training and 20% for testing sets, demonstrating strong predictive accuracy for pH (MAPE = 5.08%) and TDS (MAPE = 2.86%), while highlighting areas for improvement in temperature predictions (Temperature In MAPE = 19.38%, Temperature Out MAPE = 22.44%). The developed smart dashboard facilitates real-time monitoring, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and promoting sustainable aquaculture practices.

title: Smart exploration in reinforcement learning using absolute temporal difference errors
venue: Proceedings of the 2013 International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Exploration is still one of the crucial problems in reinforcement learning, especially for agents acting in safety-critical situations. We propose a new directed exploration method, based on a notion of state controlability. Intuitively, if an agent wants to stay safe, it should seek out states where the effects of its actions are easier to predict; we call such states more controllable. Our main contribution is a new notion of controlability, computed directly from temporal-difference errors. Unlike other existing approaches of this type, our method scales linearly with the number of state features, and is directly applicable to function approximation. Our method converges to correct values in the policy evaluation setting. We also demonstrate significantly faster learning when this exploration strategy is used in large control problems.

title: Smart Garbage Monitoring System using IoT and Cloud Computing
venue: 2022 IEEE Students Conference on Engineering and Systems (SCES)
abstract: Solid waste management has been one of our key environmental challenges, which, in addition to disrupting the environment's equilibrium, has negative consequences for society's health. One of the most pressing issues of our time is identifying, monitoring, and managing trash. The conventional method of manually monitoring garbage in waste bins is a complex, time-consuming procedure that requires more human work, time, and money, and is in no way compatible with modern technologies. In this paper, a smart garbage monitoring system is designed by using the concepts of IoT and cloud computing. We automate the process of garbage monitoring using ultrasonic sensors and NodeMCU. Cloud computing is used to analyze and access the real-time data collected through deployed bins. Further, we use the cluster-first route-second algorithm to provide an optimal route for garbage collection. An android application is also developed for the users to obtain the status of bins in their neighborhood and fetch the location of the nearest empty dustbin from their location.

title: Smart Gesture Interpretation and Speech Synthesis System using AI
venue: 2025 International Conference On Emerging Computation and Information Technologies (ICECIT)
abstract: Deaf people and individuals who are Deaf or hard of hearing, unable to speak, rely on sign language to convey messages to others and their communities. Sign languages are complex, previously agreed upon visual manual languages that convey messages using hand actions. Smart Gesture Interpretation and Speech Synthesis system using advanced Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision technologies to fill communication gaps between the deaf and hard of hearing communities. The system integrates Media Pipe and OpenCV to produce a real time interpretative platform that detects hand movements using a webcam. MediaPipe’s sophisticated hand tracking tracks 21 hand landmarks, while OpenCV operates on images with incredible speed and precision. The system includes audio output by Google Text to Speech technology, translating detected sign language or gestures into words and audio directly. This forms an end to end communication bridge between individuals who are hard of hearing and unable to speak. This revolutionary solution empowers individuals.

title: Smart Glove for Impaired People to Convert Sign into Voice with Text
venue: 2023 Intelligent Computing and Control for Engineering and Business Systems (ICCEBS)
abstract: The Smart Glove for Sign Language Translation is an innovative technology that has the potential to improve communication for people who are speech and hearing impaired. The glove uses flex detectors and accelerometers to detect sign language gestures, which are then converted into spoken language that can be understood by others. One of the key advantages of this technology is its portability, enabling users to communicate easily and conveniently anytime and anywhere. The glove also uses Bluetooth technology to wirelessly communicate with an Android phone, which can be used to convert signs into written or spoken language. Despite its potential benefits, there are still some limitations that need to be addressed. The glove may not accurately recognize all sign language gestures, leading to misinterpretation of the user's intended meaning. Additionally, the cost of the technology may be prohibitive for many individuals, especially those living in developing countries. Despite these limitations, the Smart Glove for Sign Language Translation proposed a positive step forward in improving communication for speech and hearing impaire individuals. As technology continues to advance, it islikely that i will see further improvements in this area, resulting in even more efficient and cost-effective solutions. Ultimately, these advancements have the potential to significantly enhance the quality of life for people with speech and hearing impairments, enabling them to better communicate and connect with others.

title: Smart Glove for Sign Language Interpretation and Vocalization
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Trends in Engineering Systems and Technologies (ICTEST)
abstract: Speech remains the primary mode of global communication. However, individuals with speech or hearing impairments face significant challenges due to their reliance on sign language, which often proves inaccessible to the general populace. The "Smart Glove for Sign Language Interpretation and Vocalization" project seeks to bridge this communication chasm by offering a straightforward and effective means of communication for deaf or hard-of-hearing individuals. The project entails a glove equipped with sensors capable of detecting diverse sign language gestures. Sensor data is processed by an Arduino microcontroller and transmitted to an Android device via Bluetooth. Subsequently, the Android device translates sign language into spoken language and vice versa. Recognizing the frequent utilization of both hands in sign language, this prototype provides a practical solution to facilitate communication for speech-impaired individuals The system supports multiple languages beyond English. It enhances its usability for diverse users. By offering multilingual capabilities, the system promotes inclusivity and accessibility, making it a versatile tool for different linguistic communities.

title: Smart Gloves Technology for Sign Language Translation: Enhancing Communication Accessibility
venue: 2024 International Conference on Cybernation and Computation (CYBERCOM)
abstract: Imagine a world where hands-on communication replaces spoken words, fostering hearing-deaf communication. Smart gloves are transforming accessibility and sign language translation. These advanced gloves identify complicated handwriting and sign language gestures in real time using several sensors and machine learning algorithms. After that, advanced algorithms translate the gestures into spoken or written words, enabling hearing individuals to converse with deaf people. Smart gloves identify and understand hand gestures, helping deaf and mute persons communicate in real life. Smart sign language gloves use sensor technology and machine learning to improve communication. Flex sensors measure finger bending, accelerometers and gyroscopes hand orientation, and touch sensors finger placement. Glove micro controllers handle sensor data in real time. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or long short-term memory (LSTM) networks read gesture input and convert it into text or voice. High accuracy across sign language dialects, low latency for real-time translation, and comfortable, inconspicuous gloves are key hurdles. Recent advances include deep learning gesture detection accuracy, battery longevity, and haptic feedback for two-way communication. This technique may improve communication accessibility in virtual reality interfaces, human-computer interaction, and deaf and hard of hearing.

title: Smart Green Corridors: An IoT-Based System for Ambulance Route Optimization
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Trends and Innovations in ICT (ICEI)
abstract: Smart Green Corridors is a traffic signal optimization system designed to prioritize emergency vehicles. It detects sirens using a device's microphone and activates an ESP32 camera to confirm the vehicle's presence and direction. Based on this data, traffic signals are dynamically adjusted to create a green corridor, enabling faster and safer emergency response. This software-focused solution enhances urban mobility and reduces delays for emergency services.

title: Smart Hearing Multilingual Device with Gesture Detection
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Innovative Technologies in Computing, Electrical and Electronics (IITCEE)
abstract: A significant issue that arises is the communication barriers suffered by individuals with speech and hearing impairments. The smart system includes sign language to voice and text to sign language conversion system which enables bidirectional for differently abled people. The proposed project includes the Raspberry Pi5 which acts as the processing unit connected to a camera for detecting hand gestures and speech input. The text will be detected and will be converted into the sign language. It utilizes the google translator API for multilingual support. It even converts the sign into speech with the help of Pygame. This allows to bridge the communication gap in the society.

title: Smart Heat Stress and Toxic Gases Monitoring Instrument with a Developed Graphical User Interface Using IoT
venue: 2019 International Conference on Electrical, Communication, and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In any given environment, human body's ability to maintain homeostasis accounts his probability of life and death. Thus, its importance cannot be overlooked, as it allows hormones and enzymes to be `fine-tuned' at a specific set of conditions, and allows efficient operation. The interest in the human body physiological capacity to endure extreme heat and cold conditions has raised enormously in the last few decades because of global warming and the sudden changes in temperature. This research focused on the development of a smart real-time monitoring instrument to detect and measure heat stress and toxic gases (CO, NO2 and H2S) on Java developed Graphical User Interface (GUI) using the Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The designed system uses DHT 22 (temperature and humidity), MQ7, MQ136 and MQ131 (CO, H2S and NO2 gas) sensors which are coupled with SEN0170 wind sensor. Atmega 328-PU with its Wi-Fi shield 101 is used for the purpose of controlling and Wi-Fi communication between Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and GUI. The performance of the developed system was critically appraised and the accuracies measured from the toxic gases, Temperature Humidity Index (THI) and Wind Chill Index (WCI) were recorded as 97.3%, 97.8% and 96.2% respectively.

title: Smart Helmet for Accident Detection and Driver Health Monitoring
venue: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Innovations & Applications (IC-AIDA)
abstract: The smart helmet system is conceived as an innovative safety solution that integrates rider safety, health awareness, and road conditions into a single smart platform. The central idea of smart helmet integrates to perform as a guardian of the rider, continuously supervising the state of the rider and the external environment to promote safe travel. The system initially monitors the riders physiological state to obtain or sway indicators of heart activity and wellness states, looking for abnormalities that introduce risk while riding. At the same time that this occurs the smart helmet system analyses the riders breath to quantify alcohol on/off the breath, providing immediate prioritization of safety measures by securing the fit of the helmet and alerting for reckless riding. This response will simultaneously be available to caretakers or authorities as a notification and just-in-time notification (via alarms) indicating the need for warning. In addition to the health monitoring described previously, the smart helmet will use computer vision to track for potholes or other dangerous road conditions to warn the rider in real-time. All this data will be viewable by the rider for their own viewing or shared with others or saved to the cloud. The smart helmet is creating a connected ecosystem of safety for the rider.

title: Smart Hospital Connectivity and Integrated Service Management System
venue: 2026 International Conference on Smart Futuristic Technology
abstract: The digital transformation of hospital operations has become a need that arises from the growing need for effective healthcare provision. Most conventional hospital systems rely on stand-alone processes and paper-based records, leading to data duplication, inefficiency and interoperability problems between departments. Limitations of this kind can be overcome by a proposed integrated web-based multi-hospital management system that aims to simplify interactions among patients, physicians, laboratory staff, pharmacists, and hospital administrators. Accordingly, this paper presents an integrated web-based multi-hospital management system, targeting the simplification of interaction among all the above-mentioned stakeholders of a hospital. Therefore, the Smart Hospital Connectivity and Integrated Service Management System facilitates the tracking and management of patient records from multiple hospitals on a centralized online platform. Consequently, the system integrates features such as online scheduling, making payments for laboratory tests, and live doctor–patient communication.The Smart Hospital Connectivity and Integrated Service Management System provides for tracking, sharing, and managing patient’ information in multiple hospitals in a single centralized online platform. The key features of the system include online scheduling, paying for laboratory tests, and live doctor–patient communication. Experimental testing has proven the effectiveness of the platform in handling multiple users simultaneously, making secure online payments, and exchanging trusted messages between patients and physicians. The proposed Smart Hospital Connectivity and Integrated Service Management System contributes to a modern health infrastructure by promoting digitalization and evidence-based decision-making in the Management of Hospitals.

title: Smart Maintenance for CAF Trams: An Automated Approach
venue: 2025 IEEE 25th International Symposium on Computational Intelligence and Informatics (CINTI)
abstract: Precise tracking of a vehicle fleet is essential for efficient urban transportation. This study develops an automated system for collecting and processing maintenance logs from CAF Urbos trams, using open-source tools and reverse engineering. The development followed an agile methodology and was validated through on-site testing in the BKV Zrt. Budafok depot. Compared to the traditional manual process-where downloading and converting log files typically requires $\mathbf{1 0} \boldsymbol{-} \mathbf{1 5}$ minutes-our solution makes diagnostic data available almost instantly upon vehicle arrival. This represents a measurable reduction in human resource demand, error potential, and downtime, while supporting preventive maintenance with real-time insights.

title: Smart Monitoring of Groundwater
venue: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
